# CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager

**Join 2Excel as our CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager**

**Reporting to:** Accountable Manager  
**Location:** Doncaster – role requires regular travel to the various 2Excel sites across the UK, hybrid working considered.  
**Type:** Full-time  
**Salary:** Competitive DOE  
**Start Date:** ASAP

**About us**

2Excel Aviation Ltd, part of the 2Excel Group, is an innovative aerospace and aviation services company operating across defence, security, critical national infrastructure, charter, engineering and disaster response. We save lives, clean seas, save trees and support Nationally-important services.  With specialist teams and unrivalled aerospace approvals, we design, build, test and operate aircraft to deliver mission-critical services and data-driven insights. Our success is built on the talent and experience of our exceptional people.

**Why This Role Matters**

At 2Excel, excellent compliance and safety are at the heart of everything we do.  As our CAMO Compliance Monitoring Manager, you won’t just tick boxes, you’ll shape the integrity of our operations, influence Company culture and ensure we demonstrate the highest standards in aviation.

As a Nominated Person, reporting directly to the Accountable Manager and working closely with our AOC Compliance Monitoring Manager, you will be responsible for continuously reviewing and ensuring compliance in line with regulatory requirements and Company procedures for multiple aircraft types across its Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation (CAMO).

This is your chance to lead from the front, drive continuous improvement, and make a real impact across the business.

**What You’ll Be Doing**

The CAMO CMM acts as the specialist compliance lead for continuing airworthiness oversight.  You will improve, maintain and control a robust compliance monitoring framework, ensuring that CAMO audits, contracted activity oversight, corrective action management, regulatory change impacts and compliance performance are effectively planned, monitored, escalated and reported.

You will identify non-compliances and consequential risks, driving corrective and preventative actions and ensuring our teams are always audit-ready.

You will liaise directly with Regulators and the Company senior leadership, providing clear insights and recommendations.

You’ll act as a deputy for the AOC CMM.

**About you**

You’re likely to have spent much of your career to date within the aviation sector and although you may not always have worked in compliance monitoring, you’ll have proven significant experience of it and be able to effectively develop, run and use a Compliance Management System.  You’ll have practical experience of continuous airworthiness management, aircraft maintenance oversight, CAMO processes or surveillance of such activities.  Candidates who also have experience of AOC and ATO Operators and a deep understanding of ICAO Annex 19 will be at a significant advantage.

You’ll have practical experience of human factors, aviation safety and compliance management systems, standards and practices. You’ll be familiar with audit planning and conducting root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies.  You’ll also have a proactive mindset with a passion for continuous improvement.

This operationally independent role is a CAA Nominated Postholder position.  Therefore, you’ll probably already have experience of working at that level, or you’ve been deputising and you’re ready to take the next step. In order to fulfil this requirement, you’ll have at least 5 years’ relevant work experience with a minimum of 2 years in aeronautical industry roles and/or a relevant engineering degree or maintenance technician qualification acceptable to the CAA. You’ll swiftly be able to demonstrate detailed knowledge of our exposition and operational manuals and understanding of maintenance methods and operational procedures.

You will be a strong communicator, with the confidence to engage, persuade and influence at all levels of our aviation organisation.  You will have excellent organisation skills, with the ability to prioritise your own workload, working under your own initiative and with little guidance.

In addition, applicants must be able to demonstrate the Right to Work in the UK, hold a valid UK Driving Licence due to the travel requirements and obtain a UK Security Clearance (SC).

**What You’ll Get**

* Direct access to the Accountable Manager and senior leadership.
* Opportunities to shape policy and drive innovation.
* A supportive team environment that values your expertise.
* Competitive salary and benefits package which includes but not limited to 25 days of annual leave from day one which increases with length of service, flexible working arrangements, company pension, Group Life Insurance and private medical cover.

If you’re passionate about compliance, thrive on responsibility and want to be part of a company that values excellence and progress—apply now and help us soar even higher.

To apply, please upload an up to date CV. We would also like you to include a covering letter, telling us how you meet the requirements of the role.

# Engineering Manager

## Build and lead a new team of security-cleared engineers on a multi-year UK defence programme in Warminster. Hire the team, set how it works, deliver.

## Build and lead a new engineering team on a live UK defence programme

We run a multi-year defence programme from Warminster with real contractual commitments to a UK customer. We are standing up a dedicated, security-cleared engineering team for it — and we are hiring the manager who will build and lead that team.

This is a build role. There is no team to inherit on day one: there is a programme that matters, headcount to fill, and open decisions about how the team should work. Some engineer roles are already in flight; the rest are yours to define and hire.

## The role

As Engineering Manager (EM II) you would build a single, technically complex team and then lead it — accountable for its delivery, its health, and the growth of every engineer you bring into it. You would own delivery outcomes that reach into adjacent teams on the programme, work in a demanding stakeholder environment alongside a defence customer, and develop your engineers towards senior and Staff+ technical leadership.

To be straight about the trade-off: a build role gives you unusual influence over who joins and how the team works, and it comes with the pressure of delivering to a customer while you are still hiring. Recruiting security-cleared engineers is slow and the pool is small, so patience and a high bar matter more here than speed.

Technical excellence is foundational at 4C Strategies, on both career tracks, and **this is not a post-technical role.** We do not expect you to write code every day — our framework is explicit that managers stay technically grounded even when they are not coding daily. We do expect you to still be an engineer in the ways that count: reviewing code properly rather than rubber-stamping it, taking part in architecture and design decisions on the merits, and being able to pick up a piece of the build and ship it when the team is stretched or the problem is genuinely yours to solve.

We also want someone who still finds the technology itself interesting. Curiosity about how systems actually work, what is changing in the field, and why one approach beats another is not a nice-to-have here — it is what makes your judgement worth trusting to the engineers you hire. If you would describe yourself as post-technical, this is the wrong role, and we would both rather know that now.

Our engineering career framework is dual-track: the individual-contributor and manager paths are valued equally, and moving between them is normal rather than exceptional. This role suits someone who built real technical depth as a senior or staff engineer and now wants to build a team and grow the people in it — not someone looking for a title, and not someone looking for a way out of engineering. Management here is a change of craft, not an exit from the one you have.

Day to day you will:

* Build the team: shape the roles you need, hire cleared engineers, and onboard them so they become productive quickly
* Establish how the team works — delivery cadence, code review, quality and operational standards — from a blank sheet rather than an inherited process
* Own the team's delivery commitments to the customer while it is still growing
* Coach and develop each engineer deliberately against our engineering competency framework, including towards Staff+ technical leadership
* Own delivery outcomes that span adjacent teams on the programme
* Stay hands-on where it counts: review code and designs, take part in architecture decisions, and write code yourself when the team needs it — not daily, but not never
* Represent the team to a defence customer, and create the conditions for it to do its best work

## What we are looking for

* Experience formally managing software engineers as direct reports, with real accountability for their growth, performance and delivery
* Evidence you have hired well — engineers you recruited, ideally in a market where strong candidates were scarce and the bar had to hold
* Experience setting up how a team works, rather than only running a team someone else designed
* A strong and still-current technical foundation built as a senior or staff-level engineer — enough depth to be credible on architecture and design, to review code properly, and to write it when the situation calls for it
* A genuine interest in the technology itself — you keep up with how the field is moving because you want to, not because a job description told you to
* A track record of delivering software against external commitments and hard constraints
* Evidence you have grown engineers: someone is measurably better because you managed them
* Eligibility for UK security vetting (see below)

Merits, not requirements:

* Existing SC or DV clearance
* Experience standing up a new team, or hiring into a security-cleared or otherwise regulated market
* Defence, simulation, training or another regulated domain

We weight demonstrated people leadership and technical judgement together, and we will probe both. A manager here needs both: the framework expects technical excellence at every level, and a team you are about to build needs someone who can hire and grow it — and who the engineers will respect technically on day one.

## Security and eligibility

This role is on a UK defence programme and requires **security vetting**. You will need to be eligible for SC/DV clearance, or already hold it. As part of the application we ask about nationality, dual nationality, and UK residency history, because those bear directly on vetting eligibility.

We will explain what the process involves early on. Nothing about it should surprise you late.

## How we hire

We publish our process, because a good interview should not be a surprise. You will meet:

1. Hiring manager screen
2. System design
3. Leadership and people management
4. Technical leadership
5. Delivery and execution
6. Culture interview
7. Your questions — time set aside for you to ask us anything

Every interview has a written script and a scored rubric, applied the same way for every candidate. We tell you what each session covers before it happens.

## What you can expect from 4C Strategies

* Warminster-based, with hybrid working — typically around three days a week on-site at our office or a customer site, the same pattern as the engineers you would hire. Some of the work needs to be done on-site, and the exact pattern can vary with the programme's needs. Easily commutable from Bath, Salisbury, Trowbridge and the surrounding area
* Competitive salary, reviewed annually
* Pension Scheme with 5% employer contribution
* Private healthcare including dental
* Enhanced family leave (maternity, paternity and adoption)
* 25 days holidays (plus bank holidays)
* Life Assurance
* Cycle to work scheme
* Company social events

## Why Join 4C Strategies

The work matters: what your team builds helps armed forces, public safety and resilience organisations train, prepare and respond. Building the engineering team for a large, multi-year programme is a rare opportunity — you would shape who joins, how they work, and how the systems get built, alongside experienced engineers and military specialists elsewhere on the programme. And you would do it in an organisation where technical excellence is expected of managers too, and where the individual-contributor track is valued as highly as management.

## Application Process

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV. A short cover note on your experience and motivation is welcome but not required. We review applications on a rolling basis. The process starts with a screening interview with the hiring manager; candidates who progress go through the full Engineering Manager loop described above. Permanent, full-time.

Action for Children’s Scottish Friendly Wellbeing Service started in June 2023 and have secured funding until June 2027. The aim of the service is to improve the mental health and wellbeing of vulnerable school pupils in Glasgow and aimed at schools with the highest levels of need, as evidenced through Scottish Government Table of SIMD.

This can also include direct work with families in the home or community as well being 1:1 with young people within the school.

**Bouncing Back**

Bouncing Back is an early resilience programme which is a lower-level intervention than Blues. It gives large groups of children and young people useful and evidenced based tools to support their wellbeing. This process also supports us to identify young people who need a higher-tier intervention, such as Blues or direct support.

**Blues**

The Blues Programme is an internationally acclaimed wellbeing programme for young people aged 13-19. Over six weeks, it teaches emotional resilience and reduces low mood and anxious thoughts.

Young people who would benefit from the Blues are identified through a questionnaire. The questionnaire (called a CES-D questionnaire) assesses the frequency of negative thoughts and feelings over the past week the young person has experienced indicators of low mood, anxiety and depression. Reporting more indicators results in a higher score.

Rowe Price, Visa, Mastercard, Robinhood Ventures, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures, DST Global, and Lone Pine Capital, Airwallex is leading the charge in building the global payments and financial platform of the future. If you’re ready to do the most ambitious work of your career, join us.

## **Attributes We Value**

We hire successful builders with founder-like energy who want real impact, accelerated learning, and true ownership. You bring strong role-related expertise and sharp thinking, and you’re motivated by our mission and operating principles. You move fast with good judgment, dig deep with curiosity, and make decisions from first principles, balancing speed and rigor.

You’re humble and collaborative; turn zero‐to‐one ideas into real products, and you “get stuff done” end-to-end. You use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster. ## **Who you are**

We are looking for an **Associate Director, Payments/Scheme Economics** to own the integrity, visibility and management of Airwallex’s payment costs, starting with card scheme fees and interchange fees across Visa and Mastercard.

**Reporting to the Head of Strategic Finance,** you will be the subject matter expert on scheme economics, translating complex and rapidly changing network rules into accurate system configurations, financial outcomes and business decisions. You will ensure we understand what every payment should cost, that those costs are accurately reflected across our systems and financials, and that we systematically identify opportunities to improve payment economics as we scale.

Over time, the remit will expand across other card schemes, local payment methods and the broader payments cost base.

### 

## **What you’ll do**

* **Own scheme economics and rule interpretation:** Maintain deep expertise across scheme fees, interchange and network rules. Interpret scheme bulletins, operating regulations and fee schedules, translating changes into clear financial, product and operational requirements.
* **Ensure accurate payment cost configuration:** Translate complex scheme rules into fee tables, eligibility criteria and transaction-level logic. Partner with Product and Engineering to ensure cost calculation, allocation and customer billing accurately reflect current network rules across markets and payment flows.
* **Protect payment cost integrity:** Establish robust governance, testing and controls across scheme configurations. Reconcile expected costs against actual network charges, identify anomalies and leakage, and drive root-cause resolution.
* **Build granular visibility into payment economics:** Develop robust models and analytics across markets, products, payment methods and transaction types, creating a clear view of unit economics, margin drivers and cost movements.
* **Drive structural cost and margin optimization:** Identify, quantify and execute opportunities to improve economics through transaction qualification, BIN routing, cost configuration, and other levers. Partner with Product, Finance and Commercial teams to prioritize the highest-value opportunities.
* **Shape pricing and commercial decisions:** Translate underlying payment economics into recommendations for customer pricing, product design, new market launches and commercial strategy, ensuring growth is supported by sustainable unit economics.
* **Build scalable infrastructure and automation:** Partner with Product, Engineering, and Data teams to strengthen cost engines, fee allocation logic, dashboards and automated controls. Apply AI and advanced analytics to accelerate rule interpretation, detect anomalies and surface optimization opportunities.
* **Own complex scheme economics issues:** Serve as the escalation point for scheme pricing, interchange and rule-related questions, working directly with Visa, Mastercard and other payment partners where required.

* **Deep knowledge of card payment economics**, particularly Visa and Mastercard interchange, scheme fees, transaction qualification and network rules.
* **Strong ability to operationalize complex payment rules**, translating fee schedules and network requirements into system logic, configurations and controls.
* **Experience with payment cost systems and controls**, including interchange tables, scheme fee logic, BIN-based rules, transaction attributes or similar payment configurations.
* **Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities**, including experience working with transaction-level data, economic modeling and reconciliation of expected versus actual payment costs.
* **Strong commercial judgment**, with the ability to connect detailed payment mechanics to pricing, product decisions and margin optimization.
* **Exceptional attention to detail and ownership**, with the discipline required to manage complex rules where small errors can create meaningful financial impact at scale.
* **Strong cross-functional execution**, with the ability to work effectively across Product, Engineering, Finance, Data, Operations and external payment partners.

* **Own the process, and keep raising it.** Drive severity maturity with Risk on financial and regulatory materiality - in a regulated brokerage a severity call can also start a reporting clock, so the model has to map cleanly onto those thresholds. Own the escalation path and what happens when a page goes unanswered, agree the thresholds for taking an incident to engineering leadership, and keep the service catalogue and its ownership current - time spent working out who owns a failing service is customer impact.
* **Own both bridges.** Your team connects the engineers and technical support fixing the problem, who need uninterrupted focus, to the partner communications teams, who need a continuous and accurate feed. You open the channel, supply the facts and hold the update cadence to account. Afterwards, your team runs the retrospective with SRE - who own the technical depth - and builds the post-incident package while the room is still warm, every item ticketed, owned and tagged, delivered inside a service level you define and then hold, before reliability programme management drives it to closure. You then synthesise the discussion into short, digestible learnings and publish them to the whole engineering organisation, so one team's failure becomes everyone's lesson instead of a document three people read.
* **Own the KPIs.** Time to respond and time to mitigate end to end, including the definitions and data hygiene beneath them: what separates mitigated from resolved, and whether a timestamp means what it claims. Establish a defensible baseline before committing to targets, then move them by severity. Review and approval, not authorship, is where postmortems stall, so report overdue reviews by team and incident with a next action against each.
* **Build it as a product, then automate it with AI.** Everything is documented, versioned and deployable, so you can stand up command from the artefacts alone; the process needs to scale considerably faster than the team. The automation we are after is AI workflows and agents rather than scripts and dashboards - agents that set an incident up, assemble the timeline as it runs, draft the RCA and the action package, and chase the update that is due or the review that is overdue. You own that roadmap: what an agent may do unsupervised, what still needs a commander's judgement, and the decision-tree quality that makes either of them safe.

**Who You Are (Must-Haves)**

* You have **stood up** an incident command or major-incident function, not only worked inside one - you have owned the severity model, built the roster and driven adoption across teams.
* 5+ years in production engineering, SRE or technical operations, including hands-on command of high-severity incidents.
* You have led a distributed team across time zones and run a 24x7 rotation.
* You get engineers you do not manage to do things, and you can defend a severity call to someone who disagrees with it.
* You have built reliability metrics people trust, and you know the difference between improving a number and improving reality.
* You are disciplined about scope. You can say "that is not ours" and route it, in the middle of an outage, without leaving a gap.
* You write well enough that your process documents actually get used, you can hold a bridge calm under pressure, and you can brief an executive mid-incident without either downplaying it or dramatising it.
* You understand FinTech and the trust stakes of API-driven financial platforms.
* You use AI and agentic automation to remove toil rather than to add tooling.

**Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)**

* Formal incident command training - ITIL, Major Incident Management or crisis management.
* You have run a certification, game day or drill programme, or built a pool of certified responders beyond your own headcount.
* Experience with modern incident management and on-call platforms.
* You have built a service catalogue or ownership registry that people actually maintained.
* You have worked with programme management or reliability functions to convert incident follow-ups into funded roadmap work.
* Familiarity with incident reporting obligations in regulated financial services - DORA, Reg SCI, FINRA or equivalent.
* Online securities trading or capital markets experience, or another regulated, market-hours-sensitive domain.
* You have deployed the same operating model into a second region or entity.

# Warehouse / Supply Chain Manager, AWS Cloud Logistics (ACL)

## Description

AWS Cloud Logistics is hiring a Logistics Fulfilment Manager to own the operational performance of our Data Centre Fulfilment Centres (DCFCs) and Forward Stocking Locations (FSLs) across EMEA. This is a critical IC role responsible for the end-to-end logistics execution that enables AWS data centre infrastructure deployment in the region.  
  
The DCFC programme is currently in build-out status, meaning this role will combine operational excellence in existing sites with greenfield programme delivery for new facilities. The successful candidate will manage Warehouse Service Provider (WSP) performance, drive warehouse and transport operations, and partner across Supply Chain, Procurement, Security, and Data Centre Operations to scale capacity ahead of AWS growth in EMEA.  
  
A key pillar of this role is owning the generation, updating, and management of Service Requirement (SR) documentation — ensuring operational specifications are defined, maintained, and aligned with evolving programme needs. The role works closely with the Procurement team on new site enablement and establishing operational throughput requirements, but does not carry commercial negotiation responsibilities.  
  
The role will liaise with the ACL Transport team and local DC Logistics teams to define, design, and manage local transport operations supporting DCFC/FSL sites.  
  
This role reports directly to the ACL EMEA leader and requires up to 40% travel to visit DCFC/FSL sites, vendor locations, and prospective new sites. While primarily focused on EMEA, travel may extend globally to support cross-regional initiatives and best-practice sharing.  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Own the end-to-end operational performance of DCFCs and FSLs across EMEA, including service levels, cost per unit, inventory accuracy, quality defects, safety, and on-time delivery  
  
Own Service Requirement (SR) documentation — generation, updating, and ongoing management to ensure operational specifications remain current and aligned with programme needs  
  
Liaise with the ACL Transport team and local DC Logistics teams to define, design, and manage local transport operations supporting DCFC/FSL sites  
  
Manage the WSP portfolio for EMEA DCFC/FSL operations — QBRs, performance scorecards, escalation handling, and strategic partnership development  
  
Drive standardisation across sites and countries; eliminate root causes of recurring defects and scale playbooks across the network  
  
Lead vendor management activities including performance management for Warehouse Service Providers (WSPs) and third-party logistics providers (3PLs)  
  
Work closely with the Procurement team on new site enablement, establishing operational throughput requirements, and supporting RFX events with technical and operational input  
  
Own warehouse operations oversight across DCFCs and FSLs — receiving, storage, kitting, staging, and dispatch of data centre hardware  
  
Support DCFC site selection for new facilities — evaluate locations against operational, security, and logistics criteria  
  
Drive compliance with physical security standards across all DCFC/FSL sites, working with Security teams to meet hyperscaler requirements  
  
Deliver continuous improvement through process standardisation, Lean methodologies, and data-driven decision making  
  
Represent DCFC/FSL operations to senior AWS Infrastructure Services leaders and cross-functional partners  
  
Travel up to 40% to visit sites, vendors, and prospective new locations (primarily EMEA, with potential global travel)  
  
About the team  
Amazon Cloud Logistics (ACL) is the global logistics organisation within AWS Infrastructure Services responsible for the physical movement, storage, and staging of data centre infrastructure worldwide. # Junior Platform Engineer

### **Who this is for**

An early-career engineering role inside Operate, our managed service. Security or observability background — either is welcome. 

You have been working for eighteen months to three years in a hands-on technical role — a platform team, a SOC or security engineering team, an MSP or MSSP, an infrastructure or DevOps team, a vendor’s support or professional services desk — and you are looking for your first move. You have had your hands on something that runs in production and matters to somebody. You want to go deeper, faster, in a smaller business where the work you do is seen. This is not a graduate scheme and it is not a helpdesk. It is a real engineering seat with real customers, real supervision and a clear path up.

### **About Apto Solutions**

Apto Solutions is a Bristol business that runs telemetry, observability and SIEM platforms for other organisations. Banks, airports, energy companies, engineering firms and government bodies depend on those platforms to tell them whether their systems are healthy and whether they are under attack. When those platforms are quietly working, nobody notices. When they are not, our customers find out the hard way. Our job is to make sure they never do. 

We work across Splunk, Cribl, Microsoft Sentinel, Grafana, Datadog and OpenTelemetry. We are a partner-led business with deep vendor relationships, and we build a lot of our own platform tooling on top. We are small, profitable and growing fast — the plan is to triple the business by 2028 — and we are hiring engineers who want to grow with it rather than be carried by it.

### **The Role**

This is a hands-on engineering role inside Operate, our managed service. You will help run customer telemetry platforms day to day, improve them, and contribute to the platform that lets us run them well. You will do this as part of a small engineering pool, with a senior engineer checking your work before it reaches a customer and a line manager who is accountable for your development. 

Operate has two shapes and you will work in both. 

**Operate Core is always-on.** It is continuous ownership of a customer’s platform — health, ingestion, data quality, alerting, upgrades, capacity. There is no handover and no final deliverable. The platform is ours to keep healthy for as long as the customer is ours. Success is measured in the absence of surprises and in the platform being demonstrably better in six months than it is today. 

**Operate Attach is sprint-based improvement.** A customer has a defined problem — noisy alerts, a data source that will not normalise, ingest costs running away, a detection gap, a migration — and we take a scoped block of work and fix it. Attach has a start, a shape and an end. It sits on top of Core, for the same customers, with the same engineers. 

Alongside that you will take a share of professional services delivery: shorter, project-shaped engagements that are usually how a customer first meets us.

### **What You’ll do**

Everything below is done with supervision at first and with increasing independence as you show you can carry it. We will be explicit with you about where that line is and how it moves. 

#### ***Day-to-day health of customer platforms.***

Ingestion pipelines, data quality, alerting, licensing and capacity, upgrades and patching. You will start by owning a slice of a named customer estate, and you will be expected to notice problems before the customer does. 

#### ***Incident and problem work.***

Triage, diagnosis and resolution — and then the harder part, which is the root cause and the permanent fix so it does not come back. 

#### ***Content and configuration.***

Detections, dashboards, parsers, normalisation, alert rules, pipeline routing — built properly, peer reviewed, version controlled, documented. 

#### ***Attach sprints and PS work.***

Taking a defined piece of a scoped improvement, delivering it, and being able to show what changed. 

#### ***Automation.***

If you do something manually three times, we expect you to want to automate the fourth. Most of our platform tooling started as an engineer being annoyed by something. 

#### ***Documentation and runbooks.***

Your own, to a standard, every time. Undocumented work is unfinished work.

### **What this role is NOT**

Being clear about this matters as much as the role definition itself. 

#### ***It is not a SOC analyst seat.***

You are not sitting in a queue triaging alerts against someone else’s runbook. You help build and run the platform that the analysts depend on. 

#### ***It is not a service desk or first-line support role.***

You will talk to customers about technical matters, but the work is engineering, not ticket handling. 

#### ***It is not a data science role.***

We work with very large volumes of machine data, but the work is systems and operations engineering, not modelling or statistics. Python and dashboards are not the same thing as running a platform. 

#### ***It is not a graduate scheme.***

We paused our graduate hire to open this role instead, because we want someone who has already spent time in a production environment and knows what it feels like when something breaks at an awkward hour. 

#### ***It is not a project role with a finish line.***

Core has no end date. If what you enjoy is shipping a thing and walking away, you will find the continuous half of this job frustrating.

### **Who we are looking for**

We are indifferent to whether your background is security or observability. Either one is a good starting point, and the interesting work at Apto sits where the two meet — the same telemetry usually has to serve both a security question and an operational one. What we need is depth in one and genuine curiosity about the other.

#### If your background is security:

* Microsoft Sentinel and KQL, Splunk and SPL, or another SIEM at the level of having onboarded log sources, built or tuned analytics rules, and fixed things when ingest broke.
* Some understanding of the detection lifecycle — writing, testing, tuning and retiring rules — and of why normalising messy multi-vendor data matters.
* Curious about how platform health is measured, what an SLO is, and how observability people think.

#### If your background is observability:

* Grafana, Prometheus, Datadog, Cribl or OpenTelemetry at the level of having built or maintained dashboards, alert rules, collectors or pipelines that other people relied on.
* Some understanding of metrics, logs and traces as different signals, and of why alert noise and ingest cost are engineering problems rather than facts of life.
* Curious about how attacks show up in data, what a detection is, and how security people think.

#### Behavioural

Beyond the lens, the things that actually predict success here are behavioural. We look for five attitudes, and we look for them in the evidence you give us, not in the adjectives you use about yourself. 

* **Engagement** — you take on the problem in front of you rather than the ticket in front of you.

* **Empathy** — you can see the situation from the customer’s side, and from a colleague’s side.

* **Resourcefulness** — you get unstuck. Documentation, source code, a lab, a colleague, a vendor. You do not sit and wait.

* **Curiosity** — you want to know how it works underneath, not just which button produces the result.

* **Building** — you leave things better than you found them, and you build the tool rather than repeating the task.

### **Experience we’re looking for**

Roughly eighteen months to three years in a hands-on technical role. We care much more about what you have actually done than about the number of months attached to it, and we know that at this stage most of what you have done was somebody else’s decision. That is fine. We are looking for the shape of it. 

* You have had your hands on a telemetry, SIEM, observability or monitoring platform that was running in production — not only in a course or a home lab. You have onboarded a data source, tuned an alert, applied an upgrade, or been the person who had to work out why the data stopped arriving.

* You have carried something over time rather than only delivering a task and moving on — a set of alerts you looked after, a customer estate you knew well, an on-call rotation, a service that was yours to keep healthy.

* You are comfortable in Linux, in at least one query language, and you have written scripts that did something useful. Python is what we mostly use; anything credible is a fine starting point.

* You have automated or fixed something real and you can show it. A script, a repo, a before-and-after number, a description concrete enough for us to ask sensible questions about.

* You can write. A clear runbook, a readable incident note, a straight message to a customer. This is a customer-facing role.

* You have worked in at least one of our vendor families — Splunk, Cribl, Sentinel, Grafana, Datadog, Elastic, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry — or a close analogue. The specific product is negotiable. Real exposure is not.

If you meet most of this and not all of it, apply anyway and tell us which parts you do not have. We would rather read an honest gap than a padded CV.

### **Where this role sits, and where it goes**

You report to the Operate Service Manager. They are your line manager: workload, priorities, performance, development and your quarterly evaluation. Day to day you work alongside the senior and mid-level engineers in the pool, who review your work, pair with you and are the people you ask. Technical authority sits with our Solution Architects. The customer relationship sits with the Technical Account Manager, so you will spend time in front of customers on technical matters and you will not be left to negotiate scope on your own. 

Progression at Apto is capability-based, not time-served. There is no minimum tenure. We run a published capability framework across technical competence, project discipline, customer orientation, behaviours and attitude, and a quarterly evaluation that draws on your line manager, your Solution Architect and your Technical Account Manager. You will know exactly what the next grade requires of you from your first week. The distance between this role and a mid-engineer is capability, and we will tell you honestly where you stand against it every quarter.

### **The platform work – why this is interesting**

Most managed service jobs are the same job with a different logo on the ticketing system. This one is not, because we are building our own platform underneath the service and you will work on it. We have replaced a vendor-licensed telemetry backend with an open-source stack we run ourselves. A base platform (secret  ;-)) On top of that sits multi-vendor collection — the pattern that lets us onboard a Splunk, a Cribl or a Sentinel customer without rebuilding it from scratch each time. Beyond that, the vendors are all shipping AI and agentic layers — MCP servers, agentic investigation, cross-vendor gateways — and we already have that work live with a customer. You will get early, hands-on exposure to it while most of the industry is still writing slide decks about it.

### **Working at Apto**

Apto is a small business at an important stage of growth. The team is highly capable and works to standards that matter. We do not have the layers of process that large organisations have, which means you will have real responsibility earlier than you would elsewhere, and real accountability for the outcomes. We are based in our office in Clifton, Bristol three days per week, remote two days per week. 

Salary is £35,000 to £42,000 depending on experience and assessed capability, plus bonus, pension and the usual benefits. The position is permanent and full-time. You will need the right to work in the UK; we are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

## To Apply:

Send your CV and a short note to careers@aptosolutions.co.uk with “***Engineer (Junior)***” in the subject line. The note should cover three things. 

* Describe a platform or service you helped keep running. What was it supposed to do, what happened when it stopped doing it, and what did you personally do about it? We are not expecting you to have been in charge. We are interested in what you did with the part that was yours.
* Tell us about one thing you have automated, built or fixed, with evidence. A link, a repo, a before-and-after number, or a description concrete enough that we can ask you sensible questions about it.
* Tell us which lens is yours — ***security or observability*** — and what you are curious about in the other one. Also confirm Bristol three days a week, your right to work in the UK, and your notice period.

Applications that do not cover these three points will not progress. It is our first test of whether you read the brief.

# Portfolio and Product Planning Director – Roadmaps and Capacity

**Job ID** 2026-19396

Arm is at the centre of the world’s computing ecosystem. More than **350 billion Arm-based chips** have shipped to date, and Arm’s compute platform supports innovation across cloud, AI, automotive, IoT, edge computing, and other major technology markets. (Arm)

As AI, silicon, software, and systems become more connected, Arm’s roadmap and product choices have enterprise-wide and industry-wide impact. This role presents a fantastic opportunity for an impact-led portfolio leader to shape how Arm governs roadmaps, plans capacity, manages product approvals, and prioritises resources across the enterprise.

You will work within the Portfolio and Product Planning team, helping Arm turn strategy into roadmap choices, investment decisions, and delivery outcomes.

Are you ready for the challenge!?

# Job Overview:

The Arm Portfolio and Product Planning team works across the organisation to drive, influence, and shape how business strategies become reality through Arm’s products, solutions, and roadmaps.

As Portfolio and Product Planning Director – Roadmaps and Capacity, you will coordinate Arm’s central roadmap and capacity planning capability. You will set the vision, define the operating model, and ensure roadmaps are governed, high quality, and actively used to support value-led decisions.

You will lead a compact group and work closely with the Head of Portfolio and Product Planning. Together, you will continue developing Arm’s portfolio, roadmap, and capacity capabilities at the enterprise level. This includes building the governance, data quality, tooling, and ways of working needed to scale Arm’s roadmap-led planning model.

You will also be actively involved in Arm product and solution authorizations, preparedness assessments, and the associated lifecycle. Working with operational divisions, engineering groups, financial teams, commercial departments, and manufacturing, you will assist in making proposals clear and evidence-based. They will be prepared for discussion with Arm leadership and the Portfolio Board.

This role needs someone who can balance pace with structure, connect planning silos through roadmaps, make capacity management a core planning capability, and use data, tools, and insights to improve enterprise decision-making.

## **Responsibilities:**

* Lead Arm’s roadmap and capacity planning capability frameworks, setting the vision, operating model, governance, and execution rhythm.
* Run and develop a small team covering roadmap, portfolio governance, capacity, and delivery planning.
* Work with the Head of Portfolio and Product Planning to mature Arm’s enterprise portfolio and roadmap capabilities.
* Ensure roadmaps are standards-led, high quality, decision-ready, and actively used in portfolio, investment, lifecycle, and delivery decisions.
* Lead the coordination model for how Arm resources are planned, reviewed, prioritised, and raised.
* Build resource prioritisation frameworks that connect capacity to strategic value, business impact, delivery risk, and product outcomes.
* Lead roadmap and capacity scenario planning across demand, staffing, timing, dependencies, and trade-offs.
* Support Arm product and solution approval and readiness activities across the lifecycle.
* Partner with Business Units to develop strong proposals for Arm executives and Portfolio Board.
* Influence senior collaborators across Business Units, Engineering, Finance, Commercial, and Manufacturing.
* Build the roadmap and capacity function by balancing agility with structure, creating shared ownership, using data and tools to scale, and encouraging constructive challenge.

## **Required Skills and Experience :**

* Significant experience in portfolio management, product management, long-term planning, roadmap management, or business planning.
* Validated ability to set a vision, build capability, lead a team, and deliver measurable outcomes.
* Experience in roadmap governance, capacity planning, resource management, product approvals, readiness reviews, or investment prioritisation.
* Strong understanding of ERM tools, capacity planning processes, and value-led resource prioritisation frameworks.
* Strong business judgement, with the ability to connect roadmap demand, capacity constraints, investment choices, lifecycle readiness, and product outcomes.
* Experience influencing senior team members across Business Units, Engineering, Finance, Commercial, Operations, and executive forums.
* Good understanding of the semiconductor industry and Arm’s product range.
* Ability to turn complex portfolio data and product proposals into clear recommendations and executive narratives.
* Excellent interpersonal skills and confidence operating in senior decision-making forums.

## **“Nice To Have” Skills and Experience :**

* Technical, engineering, or SoC background.
* Experience with enterprise portfolio management or strategic portfolio management platforms.
* Experience implementing portfolio operating models, governance standards, lifecycle frameworks, or planning transformation.
* Experience connecting roadmap, capacity, finance, delivery, commercial, and manufacturing data into decision frameworks.
* Familiarity with AI-enabled planning, reporting, or portfolio insight capabilities.

## **In Return:**

By joining the team in charge of coordinating product offerings and planning, you will help develop how Arm defines roadmaps. You will also guide how capacity is allocated, resources prioritised, product and solution investments approved, and strategic ambition turned into delivery!

You will work across IP, Silicon, CSS, SoC, and software, with exposure to senior leaders and enterprise-level portfolio decisions. This is a role for a leader who wants to create impact: set the vision, build the operating model, lead the team, deliver the change, and make it happen.

To note, by sending us the requested information, you consent to its use by Arm to arrange for appropriate accommodations. Although this is not an exhaustive list, examples of support include breaks between interviews, having documents read aloud, or office accessibility. ## **Hybrid Working at Arm**

Arm’s approach to hybrid working is designed to create a working environment that supports both high performance and personal wellbeing. We believe in bringing people together face to face to enable us to work at pace, whilst recognizing the value of flexibility. Within that framework, we empower groups/teams to determine their own hybrid working patterns, depending on the work and the team’s needs. In some cases, the flexibility we can offer is limited by local legal, regulatory, tax, or other considerations, and where this is the case, we will collaborate with you to find the best solution. Please talk to us to find out more about what this could look like for you.

We are a diverse organization of dedicated and innovative individuals, and don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

* Our *Platform* teams have design expertise but are often too far removed from individual implementations to influence the moments that matter most.

The result is pretty predictable: we move quickly into “how” before we are confident about the “what” and “why.”

Your mandate is to slow down at the right moment and make sure we’re solving the right problem - then help the team implement the best platform-valid solution.

This is a founding role. You would be the first Forward Deployed Designer (FDD) at Artificial, hired into an enabling function within the Platform team, with the mandate to define how the function works and to build it out. Later, FDDs would join the Transform teams in hands-on client roles: you’d take part in hiring them (with our support), then line-manage them directly.

* **Grow and manage the team.** Take part in hiring subsequent FDDs and line-manage them as they join.
* **Join customer + FDE sessions early** (problem framing and discovery), not only at reviews once decisions are already fixed.
* **Translate requests into problems.** For example, turn “we need a confirmation button before this step” into:

  + the user behaviour driving the request
  + two or three platform-valid approaches
  + a recommendation, with trade-offs explained
* **Prototype and test ideas quickly** using the most effective medium (written specs, wireframes, workflows, or light code). We care more about clarity and platform realism than polished artefacts.

* **Codify patterns and precedents** so knowledge moves from individual memory into shared team infrastructure.

* the design system already exists

Are you an experienced Risk & Compliance leader looking for the opportunity to shape and lead the risk, compliance and governance agenda across a growing healthcare group?

We’re looking for a Head of Group Risk & Compliance to join Ascenti Group in a senior leadership role with responsibility for developing a pragmatic, effective and proportionate approach to risk and compliance across our organisation.

Reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer and working closely with our Executive Team, Senior Leadership Team and colleagues across the Group, you’ll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, strengthen our controls and help ensure our colleagues, patients and customers remain safe and protected.

What you’ll be doing

This is a broad and influential role, leading our Group Risk & Compliance function and providing expertise, challenge and guidance across a wide range of areas.

You’ll be responsible for:

* Developing and continuously improving our Group risk and compliance frameworks, ensuring they remain effective, proportionate and aligned with regulatory requirements.
* Establishing and monitoring our risk register, working with senior stakeholders to identify risks and ensure appropriate mitigations are in place.
* Leading our corporate compliance framework across areas including data protection, information governance, health & safety, ISO standards and corporate risk.
* Acting as our Data Protection lead, working alongside our external Data Protection Officer and overseeing GDPR compliance, policies, training, data processing activity and privacy impact assessments.
* Overseeing information governance and supporting the effective management and protection of organisational information assets.
* Leading internal and external audit activity, ensuring actions and findings are addressed effectively.
* Overseeing business continuity, incident and risk management, whistleblowing and fraud/bribery investigations.
* Managing our insurance and claims processes, including relationships with insurers and brokers.
* Supporting customer due diligence, contractual compliance, tender activity and supply chain compliance.
* Leading the development and review of Group policies, creating greater clarity around ownership and ensuring our policy framework remains practical and effective.
* Chairing and contributing to relevant governance and compliance committees.
* Providing practical advice, training and support to colleagues and senior leaders across the Group.
* Acting as the Group’s Designated Safeguarding Lead, setting the overarching framework, standards and policies and working closely with Deputy DSLs within our Business Units.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for an established Risk & Compliance professional who can combine strong technical knowledge with pragmatic, commercially aware leadership.

You’ll bring:

* Significant experience working within compliance, risk management or a related discipline, ideally within a regulated environment.
* Strong knowledge of regulatory requirements and ISO standards.
* Experience across areas such as data protection, information governance, health & safety and corporate compliance.
* A proven track record in risk management, incident handling and developing effective compliance frameworks.
* Experience leading audits, customer due diligence and supply chain compliance.
* Excellent leadership, communication and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to work effectively with senior leaders across multiple areas of a business.
* The ability to translate complex regulatory requirements into clear, practical processes that work operationally.
* A relevant degree, professional qualification or equivalent experience within compliance or risk management.

Experience working within a matrix or multi-channel organisation, leading organisational change, or holding specialist qualifications in areas such as ESG, data protection or audit would be an advantage.

Why join Ascenti?

We are Ascenti – a leading provider of physiotherapy and mental health services, helping thousands of people live active lives every day.

With more than 25 years’ experience supporting both the public and private sectors, we’ve built a business around strong clinical standards, collaboration and a commitment to doing the right thing.

This is an opportunity to take ownership of a genuinely Group-wide function, working with senior leaders across our organisation and helping shape how risk, compliance and governance evolve as the business continues to grow and mature.

You’ll have the scope to make a visible impact: strengthening existing frameworks, introducing improvements where needed and creating a risk and compliance approach that protects the business while enabling our teams to operate effectively.

Most importantly, you’ll be joining an organisation united by a shared purpose: helping people live fuller lives.

GMP empowers buying teams with informed financial plans, oversees holistic category performance, and continually refines budgets to reflect customer demand - ensuring the business invests in the right product, at the right time, in the right quantity.

You will hold strategic control of product category plans for your area of the business, working across Merchandise Financial Planning, Strategic Inventory Planning and Assortment Planning to translate strategy into budgets, width and depth, and open-to-buy (OTB) decisions. You will lead a team of Planners and Assistant Planners in formulating short- and long-term category plans, distributing and re-allocating budgets, and interpreting performance to drive action and recommendation.

Reporting to the ASOS Merchandising Director, you will drive category performance with an end-to-end view across product teams, delivering a dynamic approach to OTB management that improves sales and margin - and doing it with the strategic alignment, commercial curiosity, proactivity and trusted partnership that GMP expects of every one of its leaders.

1. Strategic Thinking

* Support the Merchandising Director in formulating customer-facing (gender/category) pre-season sales and stock strategies, and distribute budgets to commercial product teams accordingly.
* Own strategic planning and trading of category performance, overseeing intake and OTB allocation to deliver the stock requirements the business needs.
* Determine investment priorities based on a combined view across insight, business units and categories.
* Maintain an agile, dynamic approach to OTB management that keeps ASOS flexible, drives profitability and protects competitive advantage.
* Maintain in-depth knowledge of category performance and KPIs, continually challenging and re-defining them to maximise sales and profit.
* Co-ordinate and oversee delivery of end-use strategies (e.g. cold weather, high summer, occasion), providing product teams with budget and phasing guidance.
* Interpret analytical data to guide width and depth by product type across business units.
* Set price status guidelines for product categories to protect full-price performance.

2. Business Knowledge

* Drive in-season trading through re-allocation of budgets based on customer demand, optimising stock health and Prime Stock Mix.
* Use supply chain and lead-time expertise to keep the buy agile and flexible to changing customer demand.
* Assimilate channel team requirements into category plans to ensure local market needs are met.
* Use the latest analytical data to support decision-making, analysing trading patterns and acting on unexpected sales reactions or budget gaps.
* Partner with your buying division director(s) to translate the Merchandise Financial Planning framework into a category strategy they believe in — the plan only works if the narrative behind the numbers lands.

3. Leadership

* Manage a Merchandise Planning team, making strategic and trading decisions in a fast-paced environment.
* Translate GMP and company strategy into clear team objectives, empowering Planners and Assistant Planners to deliver against them.
* Champion GMP’s Alignment, Ownership, Energy behaviours across the team - clear priorities, unambiguous ownership, and a pace that sustains engagement.
* Contribute to the Merchandise Planning Evolution programme, supporting capability-building and the team’s adoption of new planning tools, including GMP’s emerging agentic AI pilots.

## Core Responsibilities

### 1. Applied Machine Learning

* •Problem Framing: Translate ambiguous client requirements into well-posed machine learning problems with defined success criteria and realistic scope.
* •Modelling: Select, implement, and tune models appropriate to the problem and the data available, resisting unnecessary complexity where a simpler approach performs.
* •Statistical Rigour: Apply sound experimental design, validation strategy, and error analysis, including investigation of bias, data leakage, and distribution shift.
* •Data Exploration and Feature Engineering: Conduct thorough exploration of structured and unstructured data, and perform the cleaning, transformation, and feature construction needed to make it modellable.
* •2. NLP and Language Technologies
* •Model Development: Design, fine-tune, and evaluate NLP models for tasks including classification, information extraction, entity recognition, summarisation, and semantic similarity.
* •Information Retrieval: Build and evaluate retrieval systems spanning sparse, dense, and hybrid approaches, including embedding model selection, chunking strategy, reranking, and query understanding.
* •Generative AI: Apply large language models to client problems through prompting, structured output, RAG architectures, and fine-tuning where warranted, with a clear understanding of each failure mode.
* •Evaluation Design: Define task-appropriate metrics and build evaluation harnesses for systems where ground truth is expensive, ambiguous, or subjective.
* •3. Knowledge Representation and Graph-Based Approaches (desirable)
* •Ontology and Schema Design: Contribute to the taxonomies, ontologies, and graph schemas used to structure client domain knowledge.
* •Graph Construction from Text: Apply entity recognition, entity linking, and relation extraction to build knowledge graphs from unstructured sources.
* •Graph-Augmented Retrieval and Reasoning: Explore graph-based approaches to retrieval and reasoning where relational structure adds value beyond vector search alone.
* •4. Delivery and Engineering Quality
* •Production-Ready Code: Write clean, well-tested, maintainable Python in line with Attercop's coding standards, contributing to shared codebases and reusable components.
* •Hand-Off and Integration: Work closely with AI Engineers to move models and pipelines into client systems, providing the documentation, tests, and interfaces required for a clean handover.
* •Tooling: Assist in evaluating and adopting new tools, frameworks, and techniques that enhance the team's capabilities and the quality of client deliverables.
* •Ownership: Take responsibility for the quality of your own output, seek peer review proactively, and escalate technical risks or blockers promptly and constructively.
* •5. Research and Innovation
* •Horizon Scanning: Stay current with developments in NLP, information retrieval, and generative AI, bringing relevant ideas and techniques to the attention of the wider team.
* •Prototyping: Contribute to internal R&D efforts, prototyping new approaches and helping to assess their viability for client applications.
* •Documentation: Record research findings, methodologies, and implementation details clearly, sharing knowledge with colleagues and, where appropriate, external audiences.

### Professional Experience

* •We'd expect either:
* •A minimum of 3 years of professional experience as a Data Scientist or Research Scientist with a substantial proportion of that time spent on NLP or language-centric problems in a commercial or applied research setting, alongside a degree (or equivalent demonstrable experience) in a quantitative discipline such as computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics, or engineering; or
* •A PhD in one of those disciplines with a research focus on NLP or machine learning.

* •Machine Learning (essential):
* •Solid grounding in machine learning fundamentals, model evaluation, and experimental design.
* •Demonstrable experience building and validating models on real, imperfect data
* •Working knowledge of scikit-learn and PyTorch, and comfort reading and adapting research code.

# **QMS Engineer**

**Location:** Yorkshire

**Salary:** £45,000 - £50,000

**Contract Type:** Permanent

If you’re a Quality Engineer who believes quality should be visible on the manufacturing floor rather than managed purely from behind a desk, this role offers the opportunity to make a genuine impact.

You’ll help develop, measure and continually improve the QMS, working closely with Manufacturing, Quality and wider technical teams to ensure processes remain effective, compliant and practical. This is a hands-on position within a regulated medical device environment, with a strong emphasis on ISO 13485.

The role would suit someone who enjoys challenging existing processes, using data to understand where improvements are needed and building a quality-first mentality across the organisation.

**The Role**

You’ll take an active role in improving the QMS, identifying trends, managing quality issues and ensuring improvements translate into stronger manufacturing performance.

Key responsibilities will include:

* Own and analyse QMS performance metrics, using meaningful data and trends to identify risks, weaknesses and improvement opportunities.
* Drive continuous improvement across the QMS, developing quality plans and improvement projects where processes are underperforming.
* Lead and support NCR investigations, ensuring non-conformances are appropriately investigated, documented and dispositioned.
* Determine when issues require escalation into CAPA, supporting robust root cause investigation, corrective action and effectiveness monitoring.
* Use risk-based decision making aligned with ISO 14971 (ISO14971) when assessing product, process and manufacturing quality issues.
* Conduct and support internal, supplier and external audits, ensuring findings are effectively addressed through the QMS.
* Review quality trends and provide clear, evidence-based information to leadership on risks and required actions.
* Deliver training across the QMS, helping Manufacturing and cross-functional teams understand quality processes and expectations.
* Act as an on-floor Quality Engineering contact, providing practical guidance on deviations, documentation, inspection issues and non-conforming material.
* Support NCR, MRB and production investigations, working directly with Manufacturing to resolve issues at source.
* Review production deviations and changes, assessing their impact on product quality and regulatory compliance.
* Support production-related validation activities including process, equipment and software validation where applicable.
* Author and improve procedures, work instructions and quality documentation in accordance with ISO 13485 requirements.
* Support CAPA and root cause activities arising from recurring manufacturing issues, audit findings or negative quality trends.

**Experience Required**

You’ll ideally bring 3–5+ years of Quality Engineering or Quality Systems experience within medical devices or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

You should have practical knowledge of ISO 13485, experience managing NCR and CAPA activities, an understanding of ISO14971, and confidence using data to support quality decisions.

Most importantly, you’ll be someone who is comfortable getting onto the manufacturing floor, asking the right questions and taking ownership of improvement.

If you have a passion for quality, enjoy improving a QMS and believe strong quality systems should help manufacturing perform better rather than simply create more paperwork, this role provides the opportunity to make that difference.

## Job Title

Finance Analyst – Accounts Receivable & Credit Control

## **Job Description**

This is an excellent opportunity for a recent Finance or Accounting graduate, or Accounts Receivable Clerk, to join a busy finance team and gain valuable hands-on experience. The role will focus on Accounts Receivable (AR), Credit Control, and Debt Recovery, providing the successful candidate with the opportunity to develop their skills while making a meaningful contribution to the wider finance function.

The primary focus during the initial phase of the contract will be to identify, investigate, and recover aged debt balances between 1 and 5 years old, working closely with customers and internal stakeholders to resolve historical issues preventing collection. This recovery activity will directly contribute to improving cash flow, reducing bad debt exposure, and strengthening the overall health of the Accounts Receivable portfolio.

The successful candidate will work closely with internal stakeholders and external customers to resolve payment issues, retrieve data for analysis, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and ensure the development of positive customer relationships.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Accounts Receivable Management**

* Monitor customer accounts to ensure invoices are paid within agreed payment terms.
* Maintain accurate customer account records and payment histories.
* Investigate and resolve invoice, billing, and payment queries.
* Reconcile customer accounts and identify discrepancies.

**Legacy Debt Recovery**

* Take ownership of a portfolio of aged debt balances, with an initial focus on accounts outstanding for 2-5 years.
* Investigate historical customer balances and identify barriers to collection, including disputes, missing documentation, incorrect billing, or account ownership changes.
* Liaise with customers and internal departments to resolve longstanding issues and facilitate payment.
* Develop and execute recovery plans for aged and high-risk debt accounts.
* Maintain accurate records of recovery activity, customer communications, and outcomes.
* Escalate accounts where legal action, write-off, or alternative collection strategies may be appropriate.

**Relationship Management**

* Build and maintain professional relationships with customers.
* Act as a key point of contact for accounts receivable and payment issues.
* Work collaboratively with Sales, Customer Service, Operations, and Finance teams to resolve disputes.
* Support positive customer experiences whilst ensuring company debts are recovered.

**Data Analysis & Reporting**

* Retrieve, compile, and analyse AR and debt collection data.
* Produce reports on aged debt, collection performance, and cash recovery.
* Identify trends and recommend actions to improve collection effectiveness.
* Support month-end reporting activities.

**Stakeholder Management**

* Liaise with internal departments to resolve customer queries quickly.
* Communicate account status and collection risks to management.
* Assist in implementing process improvements within the AR function.

**Continuous Improvement & Projects**

* Identify opportunities to improve AR processes and controls.
* Support finance transformation and business improvement initiatives.
* Take part in additional finance projects as business needs require.

**Core Competencies**

**Customer Focus**

* Ability to build strong customer relationships while maintaining professionalism and accountability.

**Communication Skills**

* Confident verbal and written communication skills.
* Comfortable discussing outstanding payments and resolving disputes.

**Relationship Building**

* Develop trust and credibility with customers and internal stakeholders.

**Results Orientation**

* Driven to achieve collection targets and improve business outcomes.
* Demonstrates resilience and persistence when managing challenging situations.

**Analytical Thinking**

* Ability to interpret financial data and identify trends.
* Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

**Problem Solving**

* Investigates issues thoroughly and implements practical solutions.

**Stakeholder Management**

* Works effectively across departments and manages multiple priorities.

**Organisation & Time Management**

* Manages workload effectively in a fast-paced environment.
* Prioritises tasks to meet deadlines.

**Qualifications**

**Essential**

* Experience in a customer-facing role such as retail, hospitality, bar work, customer service, or similar.
* Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office skills.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Strong numerical and analytical capability.

Backed by significant new multi-year philanthropic investment, we are building the data and evaluation infrastructure that enables Babyzone to evaluate and improve its work at scale — capturing what happens across every hub, tracking outcomes for children and families over time, and translating the evidence into national influence.

As Head of Data & Impact, you will own how Babyzone measures its activity, understands its families, and evidences its impact across every hub and central function.

Participant support and caseload management**

* Ability to build genuine, trusting relationships with participants from diverse backgrounds, including people with disabilities, health conditions and complex or multiple disadvantage

* Comfortable working independently and flexibly across a number of community locations, with your own initiative

## About Beyonk Group

Beyonk is the full-scale growth partner for visitor attractions and seasonal events. We combine industry-leading ticketing software, powerful marketing tools, and hands-on marketing services to help operators grow their business and reach millions of new visitors every year.

Our technology makes it simple for visitors to book directly through our partners' websites, while giving operators the automations, integrations, and data they need to run and scale. Through our marketing services division, we work with leading destinations, from family farms to major theme experiences, to drive real visitor growth.

We're growing fast across the UK and US, welcoming thousands of customers a day to incredible experiences. It's an exciting time to join, grow with us, and help millions find and book great experiences.

## The role

This is a player-coach role. You'll run our Account Executive team and own the new business number month to month - not from a spreadsheet, but from inside the deals. You'll join pitches, review calls, coach reps on specific skills and specific deals, and step in personally when a deal needs it.

The motion is high-volume, lower-value SMB software sales: deals averaging roughly £2-8k on short cycles, sold to small business owners who run attractions, experiences and seasonal events. This is velocity selling, not enterprise. If your background is a handful of large, slow, six-figure deals a year, this won't be the right fit - and vice versa, we're not after someone who has only ever run very high-volume, very low-value transactional sales either. We sit in a specific middle, and getting the rhythm right is the job.

We're looking for someone who has built a team that delivers consistently, month after month. You'll manage AEs selling our ticketing and marketing software to attractions, experience providers, and seasonal event operators across the UK and US.

This is a hands-on seat in a lean, high-ownership environment. If you want to manage purely through dashboards and one-to-ones, this isn't the role. If you love the game and love making other people better at it, it is.

## What you'll do

* Own the team's new business number and be accountable for hitting it month to month
* Join pitches and demos alongside AEs, and help close deals that matter
* Review call recordings and coach individuals on specific calls - discovery, demo, objection handling, closing
* Run pipeline reviews and forecast accurately in HubSpot
* Diagnose performance through the funnel - work out whether a rep's issue is activity, conversion, deal size or cycle length, and fix the root cause
* Recruit, onboard and ramp new AEs as the team grows
* Leverage AI tools to raise the team's productivity - call analysis, prospect research, coaching at scale
* Work closely with Customer Success on handovers, and feed market intelligence back to Product and Marketing
* Set the standard on activity, pipeline hygiene and follow-through - and hold the team to it

## What success looks like

* The team hits its number consistently, month after month
* Every AE knows exactly what they need to improve and is measurably improving it
* Forecasts are accurate and leadership trusts them
* New hires ramp on schedule because onboarding and coaching are systematic
* Reps want to work for you - you raise people up, you don't burn them out

## What we're looking for

**Must-haves**

* **SMB SaaS sales leadership in a velocity motion.** You've led a team selling software at high volume and lower value - deals in roughly the £2-8k range, on short cycles. Not enterprise, not a few big deals a year.
* **A proven player-coach.** You've carried a team number as a manager while still joining pitches and coaching reps on individual calls - not managing from the dashboard.
* **Consistent team delivery.** A track record of running a high-performing sales team that hits target month after month predictably, and you can talk specifics about how you built that consistency.
* **Highly analytical.** You think in funnels and can diagnose exactly where a rep's performance is breaking down.
* **A genuine people person.** You coach, motivate and retain, and people measurably get better working for you.
* **Sharp attention to detail**, from CRM hygiene to deal terms.
* **Practical AI in your workflow.** You already use AI to sell and coach faster and smarter, and you can bring the team with you. We'd expect anyone from a modern tech-sales background to be doing this already - if you're not, we'll want to understand why.

**Strongly preferred**

* Experience selling on transaction-based or usage-based pricing - booking fees, commission, take-rate or % of GMV - not only fixed subscriptions
* Selling to non-technical, non-desk-based small business owners - hands-on operators, not procurement teams or in-house buyers

**Bonus points**

* **Seasonality as a core variable** in how you sold and coached - building and managing a number that swings hard across the year
* Experience growing a sales team from around 10 people upwards
* Experience operating across both UK and US markets
* Experience structuring a team into inbound/outbound or SME/mid-market segments

## Salary, location and working pattern

* Real ownership of the number and how the team runs, with direct access to leadership
