Royal Leamington Spa

Ready to revolutionize healthcare, making it faster and more accessible than ever before?

**How we started:**

Founded in 2013 by Dwayne D’Souza, HeliosXwas built on a simple but powerful idea: healthcare should be easier to access, faster to receive, and centred around the individual. From day one, we’ve grown without external funding; scaling profitably through technology, disciplined execution, and deep medical expertise. What started as a challenger idea has become one of the most significant healthcare platforms operating globally today.

**Where we are now:**

We’ve earned the trust of millions of people worldwide through category-leading products and well-known brands, including MedExpress, Dermatica, ZipHealth, RocketRX, and Levity. A key driver of our success is vertical integration; we operate our own manufacturing and proprietary products, led by in-house medical teams, researchers, and pharmacists at the top of their fields.

In 2025, HeliosX treated more than 1.7 million patients globally and reached £781m in revenue, representing +337% year-on-year growth and cementing our position as the clear market leader in the UK. That growth translates into real-world outcomes: our weight-loss treatments helped patients lose 8.5 million kilograms of excess weight in 2025 alone, contributing to an estimated 1,300 fewer cardiac events. This is growth with measurable, life-changing impact at scale.

Today, we operate across four international markets, with successful launches in Germany and Canada and continued expansion in the US. We were also recently recognised in the Sunday Times Top 100 fastest-growing tech companies, further validation of both our momentum and our ambition.

**Where we’re going:**

2026 is another significant year for HeliosX. Our ambition is to surpass £1.1bn in revenue, continue expanding thoughtfully into new international markets and broaden our condition and treatment portfolio. As we scale, we're focused on building the technology, operational excellence and clinical capabilities that will support sustainable long-term growth. Joining HeliosX now means helping shape the systems, teams and products that will define the next chapter of digital healthcare. You'll be solving complex problems at pace, working alongside exceptional people and building products that genuinely improve lives at scale.

**There’s never been a more exciting time to join HeliosX. Come be a part of making our dream of easier and faster healthcare a reality!**

**The Opportunity**

We’re looking for a highly organised and proactive Logistics Coordinator to join our Operations team and play a key role in the day-to-day management of final mile operations across all HeliosX brands and products. This role will work closely with our courier partners to coordinate collections, provide accurate forecasts and ensure deliveries run smoothly, while also supporting performance reporting, investigating delivery failures and managing compensation claims in line with our contractual agreements.

This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced environment, where attention to detail, strong communication and a proactive approach will make a real difference to our operational performance and customer experience.

***This role will be based in our Leamington Spa Hub, with standard working hours of 9:00am–5:00pm, Monday to Friday.***

* Using couriers data to analyse delivery failures - looking to work with courier partners to improve performance.

* Present weekly and monthly performance reports on both service and costs to Supply Chain leadership.

* Proven experience of successful interaction with key stakeholders, both internal and external (third party suppliers).

* Pharmacy / healthcare experience advantage but not essential.
* Ability to demonstrate effective cross-functional working to achieve results.

* Ability to deal with data from various sources and use it to analyse performance and challenge contractors / couriers.

At HeliosX, we want to improve healthcare for everyone, and to do this we need a team of brilliant people who share that ambition. At Humanoid, we are working from a simple hypothesis: AI is rapidly transforming engineering. The bottlenecks are shifting from writing code to how efficiently AI-authored changes can be verified.

We’re looking for a Technical Lead to build the platform that lets our engineers move faster with coding agents while protecting our code, infrastructure, and robots. You’ll give developers and agents the environments, context, and tools to work effectively, and build verification and security into the path from task to healthy deployment. This is a hands-on leadership role and the keystone hire for a new team. You’ll build the critical systems yourself, recruit and lead engineers, and work across Developer Tools, Security, Safety, Simulation, and robot software. Success means increasing engineering output while reducing cost and human review per accepted change, without increasing defects or safety risk.  
  
**What you'll do:**

* Own the path from an agent task to a healthy deployed change, including acceptance criteria, execution, verification, merge, rollout, monitoring, and rollback.
* Build secure, reproducible agent runtimes with task-scoped identity, short-lived credentials, bounded access, cost controls, and re-playable execution records. Proactively detect unauthorized agent activity across our compute clusters, whether internal or external.
* Build the interfaces developers use to launch, monitor, and control agents, alongside tooling for agents to collaborate through shared memory, coordinated work, and appropriately authorized access to company resources.
* Reduce the tokens and retries required for accepted work through better context assembly, model and tool routing, caching, task decomposition, and feedback.
* Give agents fast access to builds, tests, simulation, replay, and hardware-in-the-loop, with acceptance criteria they cannot alter.
* Work with engineering teams to make the codebase easier to navigate and verify through clear interfaces, strong invariants, reproducible environments, fast local checks, and well-documented implementation paths.
* Recruit and lead the team while remaining hands-on. Measure success through cost per accepted change, human review time, escaped defects, and time from push to healthy on the robot.

* Hands-on experience using and integrating coding agents into real engineering workflows. You understand how context, tools, and evals affect reliability, latency, and cost, and can talk concretely about what worked and what didn’t.
* Sound security judgment around workload isolation, identity, permissions, and credentials. You can design appropriate boundaries for agents accessing code, infrastructure, and company resources.
* Experience building reliable automated tests or verification systems and diagnosing failures across code, tooling, and infrastructure. You have good judgment about what automated checks establish and where human review still matters.
* Experience leading engineers while remaining hands-on. You can set technical direction, recruit a strong team, and turn an ambitious goal into systems that engineers use and trust.

Hi 👋 I’m Rich Ashworth, Director of Engineering at hyperexponential.

I lead the Model Authoring value stream that owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models. An actuary might start with an Excel rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved, and is pricing live business. Our job is to turn that into an exceptional user experience and make every step of that credible enough to trust.

I'm hiring a Staff Product Engineer to help set our technical direction and build the next version of our products. It's an individual contributor role, but influence is a huge part of it: the standards the pods work to, the shared enablers underneath the product, and the interfaces where our problems meet other teams'. You’ll be hands-on where the risk is highest.

There's no established playbook for any of this, but there’s an incredible opportunity in front of us. If this sounds like a role that would excite you, I'd love to hear from you.

## About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

## About the Model Authoring team

Model Authoring owns the products our customers use to write and manage their pricing models: the model developer experience and our actuarial agent. An actuary might start with an Excel-based rater and finish with a Python model that has been reviewed, approved and is pricing live business. Our job is to make every step of that credible enough to trust. The team is distributed across our Warsaw and London offices.

As the Staff Product Engineer, you will help set the team's technical direction. This is an individual contributor role, but influence is a large part of it: you'll help define the standards the team works to, raise the technical bar across pods, and own the interfaces where our problems meet those of teams elsewhere in Technology. You'll be expected to move fast and start shaping technical conversations early. We work in an AI-native way, and you'll help define and evolve what that means here.

## What you'll be doing

Establish a set of engineering standards across the Model Authoring pods. The standards are documented and actively referenced in code review, with new pod work conforming by default.

Set and own the technical direction for the team's shared enablers, including how we represent and persist models, the model registry, secure context access, and shared agentic infrastructure.

Establish the technical interfaces between Model Authoring and other parts of the business. Dependencies with other teams are agreed, documented, and progressing without needing to be brokered by someone else.

Work hands-on on the hardest problems in the stream. This is not an advisory role: we would expect you in the code where the risk is highest.

Help define how we work in an AI-native way. Which parts of model development and of our own engineering we hand to agents, what stays human, and what evidence we need before trusting either.

Visibly lift the engineers around you. You're sought out for design input across pods, and there's at least one engineer whose growth is clearly attributable to your support.

## What you'll need to have done

Worked in an AI-native environment, and genuinely want to keep doing so. You've used AI or agentic tools in your own engineering workflow, introduced or experimented with them, and have a real view on what's worked and what hasn't.

Been product-focused rather than purely technical. You understand who your users are, where their pain points are, and how your technical decisions connect to commercial outcomes.

Set technical direction while navigating genuine ambiguity. A proven track record of owning architecture in a domain with no established playbook, and making clear calls on imperfect information rather than deferring them.

Owned a significant technical challenge or service end to end, with the depth to walk through it in detail - the trade-offs, the contracts, the things you'd do differently.

Influenced across teams. You can hold a position under challenge, genuinely listen to pushback, and persuade others - not just present your own view and hope it lands.

Worked effectively across distributed teams - this role spans our Warsaw and London offices, so you'll need to be comfortable building relationships and influence across both.

### Nice to have

Developer experience work, ideally having built tools for developers or - in our case - actuaries. This doesn't have to be your company's core product; internal developer experience initiatives count too.

## You're unlikely to thrive here if

# Product Owner - Salesforce

## Reporting to the Head of Technology, the Product Owner leads and manages key technology products, including Salesforce solutions across Sales, Customer Service, and Commercial operations.

At IAG Cargo we are in the business of moving things. From antibiotics to groundbreaking tech, gold bullion to avocados and everything in between. We move cargo that positively impacts society worldwide. Whatever people need, wherever they are. At IAG Cargo we open the skies and fly the world to bring people the things they really need.  

We are the logistics and cargo brand of International Airlines Group (Aer Lingus, British Airways, Iberia, Level and Vueling). Powered by five airlines, our reach is truly global – but it’s the impact we make that defines us. At IAG Cargo, we believe in keeping the world’s economies turning, and do everything with determined attitudes, curious minds, collaborative actions and heartfelt pride. Join us at our globally recognised logistics business, that is Trusted to Deliver.

#### **About the role**

Reporting directly to one of our Heads of Technology, the Product Owner role has end-to-end accountability for critical technology products within the assigned business area, including Salesforce-based platforms across Sales, Customer Service, and Commercial operations of IAG Cargo.

This role acts as a liaison between IT development groups and business units in order to establish a full product roadmap. They will be responsible for the full lifecycle of these technology products, managing the product backlog, timely delivery of features, enhancements and bug fixes and management of associated technology vendors.

The Product Owner will liaise with Service Operations and Cyber teams to ensure the ongoing operation of the technology meets service level requirements, both from a functional and non-functional perspective.

#### **What you’ll do**

* **Technology Accountability:** Overall accountability for the entire lifecycle of assigned business area technology products (from design, build through to BAU), including CRM platforms such as Salesforce (e.g. Sales Cloud, Service Cloud), ensuring alignment with enterprise platform strategy.
* **Relationship Management:** Serve as the main point of contact between business stakeholders, customers, and the development team. Act as the voice of the customer to ensure technology solutions meet their needs effectively and provide clear recommendations to support informed decision-making.
* **Business Expertise:** Understand the underlying business of the technology product and collaborate with the Product Manager in order to identify product opportunities, shape the vision and define the product roadmap with a strong understanding of CRM-driven processes such as customer management, sales pipelines, and case handling, and their integration with wider enterprise systems and customer data platforms.
* **Product Backlog Management:** Manage and prioritise the product backlog, ensuring features, user stories, and bug fixes are well-defined with clear acceptance criteria and aligned with business priorities and product roadmap, ensuring optimal use of platform capabilities (e.g. standard vs custom Salesforce functionality).
* **Change Delivery:** Accountable for the successful delivery of all changes to the product, whether project-driven, small changes, or bug fixes.
* **Development Oversight:** Lead and participate in all Scrum ceremonies, including sprint planning and retrospectives, collaborating with QA teams to resolve issues before release, ensuring alignment with Salesforce release cycles, platform constraints, and best practices.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Continuously improve product development processes for better efficiency and communication.
* **Quality Assurance:** Ensure underlying technology meets performance service levels, identifying areas for improvement and implementing solutions including compliance with internal cyber, architectural, and data standards, as well as relevant industry regulations and policies, and adherence to Salesforce platform governance, data model integrity, and integration standards.
* **Product Support**: Work closely with Service Operations and support partners, to ensure the day-to-day operations of the product meets operational SLAs and customer expectations, ensuring effective support models for SaaS platforms such as Salesforce, including incident, release, and change management.
* **Supplier Management:** Act as point of escalation to the vendor, including Salesforce delivery and support partners, for any delivery or operational issues.
* **Knowledge Management:** Build the internal knowledge base product features, processes, and updates and become the product “subject matter expert”, including platform capabilities, limitations, and roadmap (e.g. Salesforce releases and features).
* **Industry Expertise:** Monitor industry trends relevant to the product and its customers, including competitor activities, emerging technology and supplier landscape.
* **Value Realisation:** Define and track product outcomes, ensuring delivery is aligned to measurable business value and strategic outcomes (e.g. adoption, efficiency, revenue impact), not just feature completion.

#### **It's all about you**

What you’ll bring to IAG Cargo:

* Demonstrates clear leadership and an ability to influence and persuade across the organisation at senior levels, leading by example and aligning stakeholder groups around a common vision.
* Collaborative, open working, resulting in recognition as a valued partner by colleagues, customers and senior stakeholders across the organisation.
* Sound judgement, attention to detail, solution focused and ability to make effective decisions in a fast-paced environment.
* The ability to communicate complex ideas in a clear, concise manner (verbal and written) across functional and technical departments.
* Ability to work on multiple tasks at any one time, handling conflicting demands, prioritize workload and effectively delegation while maintaining high quality standards.
* High emotional intelligence and solid interpersonal and relationship building skills.
* Strong analytical and product management skills required, including a thorough understanding of how to interpret customer/business needs together with the technology platform road map into manageable product backlog user stories.
* Entrepreneurial self-starter who is self-motivated but also a team player
* Experience in leading cross-functional teams and motivating them to go the extra mile.
* Advocate of Digital and Agile approaches, drive simplicity and scalability.
* Strong understanding of CRM platforms (preferably Salesforce) and the ability to leverage out‐of‐the‐box capabilities to deliver scalable business solutions

Skills and Experience:

Essential Experience:

* Proven experience working in agile environments and familiarity with agile lifecycle management tools.
* 2-3 years of experience in a product-focused role, with experience working in the Airline or Logistics Insurance industry.

Desirable Experience:

* Experience with SaaS products and vendors.
* Experience in establishing product teams and ways of working.
* Experience working with Salesforce or similar CRM platforms in a product or delivery capacity.

#### We’ll treat you right

Wherever you work within IAG Cargo, you’ll play a part in helping us deliver what the world needs and join a diverse and inclusive business that’s making a difference.

As well as a competitive salary, bonus, we offer a range of benefits to support our colleagues, which include:

* For health and wellbeing we offer a free onsite gym facility as well as access to the UNMIND app and a community of Mental Health First Aiders
* Access to discounts on Apple, Cinema tickets and loads of other goodies through Perks at work

**Diversity and Inclusion**

Our recruitment procedures positively support our diversity and inclusion agenda.

All candidates are considered strictly on their merits in relation to the criteria for the role, treated fairly and consistently, and have their individual needs responded to throughout the process.

Reporting to the Divisional Finance Director, you will own financial controlling for the Group’s Technology business – delivering a clean, timely month-end close and a well-controlled balance sheet.

You will also oversee a global, functional P&L and have significant interaction with the Group Finance Team (also located in Birmingham).

You will coordinate the locally required statutory, tax and VAT work through a Netherlands finance lead and an external Dutch accountancy firm. This is a controls-first role but will also require supporting ad-hoc work initiatives, as well as some FP&A activities as required.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Financial Control & Month-End Close**

* Own the month-end close and reporting timetable for both Dutch entities in Sage Intacct, including journals, accruals, prepayments and reconciliations. Be a key point of contact to the Group team regarding Prophix (FP&A tool) upload and reconciliation.

* Maintain balance-sheet integrity through timely reconciliations, review, provisioning and a robust controls framework.

* Prepare consolidation inputs and manage group-GAAP / IFRS alignment and intercompany balances.

* Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable with a focus on cash balances. Work collaboratively with the Birmingham Shared Services team, ensuring appropriate controls are in place over all transactions.

**Statutory, Tax & Compliance**

* Coordinate the externally-prepared Dutch statutory accounts (Dutch GAAP) and KvK (Dutch Chamber of Commerce) filing with the external accountancy firm.

* Coordinate corporation tax (Vpb) and support transfer-pricing requirements with the external firm.

* Own the statutory audit relationship and review locally-prepared VAT (BTW) and ICP (intra community transactions) submissions.

* Ensure the statutory calendar is met in full, supporting the Netherlands finance lead.

**Reporting, Planning & Analysis**

* Lead the production of month and year-end results for both Dutch entities, including management analysis highlighting variances, trends and impacts on the annual business plan and quarterly forecasts.

* Prepare the budget, forecast, monthly variance analysis and management commentary, and produce board and management reporting packs.

* Develop financial models and analysis to guide planning and decision-making, defining KPIs and dashboards that support data-driven decisions.

* Partner with local Sales and operations, providing guidance to both finance and non-finance staff to enhance financial acumen across the business.

**Team Leadership & Continuous Improvement**

* Line-manage accounting teams in the Netherlands and UK, providing day-to-day guidance, development support and performance oversight.

* Provide guidance on the use of financial systems, ensuring the integrity of the data held within them.

* Champion the adoption of new financial processes and systems that enhance efficiency, accuracy and insight, acting as a change agent and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

* Drive close automation and support the transition of transactional processing into the Shared Services Centre.

* Other ad-hoc tasks and reporting as required in line with the remit of the role.

## Requirements

* Fully qualified accountant (ACA/ ACCA/ CIMA) with significant post-qualification experience in a financial control or similar role.

* Proven financial controller experience, ideally across multiple or international entities.

* Strong technical grounding in month-end close, balance-sheet control, consolidation and foreign-entity reporting.

* Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate complex financial data into actionable business insights.

* Exceptional relationship-building skills, with a proven ability to establish trust and credibility across all levels of an organisation.

* Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of conveying financial concepts to non-financial stakeholders.

* Proficiency in financial systems and tools, with a preference for candidates with experience in Sage Intacct or similar platforms, including close automation and controls.

* Strong MS Excel skills.

* Desirable (but not essential): SaaS / subscription based / recurring-revenue (ARR) experience, awareness of Dutch GAAP and Dutch tax/ VAT (not essential), and experience of shared-services or finance centralisation.

* Positive can-do attitude and strong communicator

* Someone who enjoys collaboration with global teams

Our client is a leading global investment management company headquartered in London. It manages over $228 billion in assets and serves institutional investors, pension funds, wealth managers, and other sophisticated clients worldwide. The firm specializes in quantitative investing, alternative investments, systematic trading strategies, and technology-driven asset management. Data science, machine learning, and AI are core components of its investment and research processes.

As part of our collaboration we will focus on two foundational capabilities required to enable safe and scalable AI adoption across the enterprise: Agentic Security and AI-Ready Data Foundations.

### What project we have for you

We build the data foundations and evaluation frameworks that make AI useful, reliable and safe inside regulated financial firms. The value of an AI agent depends not only on the models behind it, but also on the quality of the structured and unstructured data it consumes and the accuracy, relevance and traceability of the outputs it produces. Your job is to measure that quality, identify where it breaks down and turn the findings into practical improvements.

This is an \***engineering**\* role, not an analytical one. You will build the agentic workflows that reason over the firm’s research content, and the ingestion, evaluation and guardrail tooling that makes their output trustworthy enough for investment professionals to act on. None of this tooling exists today — you would be building it from scratch.

### What you will do

* Designing, building, and maintaining the Python services, libraries, and command-line tooling that make up the internal infrastructure platform.
* Working with the engineering teams who consume the platform to understand their workflows and turn recurring pain points into platform features.
* Replacing manual infrastructure operations with codified, self-service workflows, so that environments are reproducible, reviewable, and safe to change.
* Building observability into the platform through metrics, structured logging, and alerting, so failures surface before consuming teams report them.
* Owning production issues in the platform end to end, from triage and root cause analysis through the code or configuration change that prevents a recurrence.
* Managing and scaling the compute and storage the platform provisions across on-premises hardware, balancing performance against cost as usage grows.
* Building security into the platform by default: secrets management, least-privilege access, dependency hygiene, and an auditable history of every infrastructure change.
* Evaluating new tools, libraries, and patterns, and folding the ones that earn their place into the platform roadmap.

### What you need for this

* 7+ years of experience as a DevOps / platform / systems engineer, with a track record spanning both infrastructure operations and broader platform engineering — not purely a helpdesk/ops role.
* Software development background: comfortable reading and writing production code, understanding how applications are configured and run, not just how they’re deployed. This helps when working directly alongside dev teams on their workloads.
* Python (required): solid, production-level scripting and tooling ability — automation, integrations, and support for platform/migration work. Not necessarily building a Python platform product, but extending and maintaining real code.
* Linux systems (required): strong fundamentals — processes, networking, storage, permissions, package management. Comfortable troubleshooting at the OS level across a fleet of machines.
* Infrastructure as code: hands-on production experience with Ansible and Terraform. Able to write, review, and maintain IaC that’s treated like application code (version control, review, testing).
* Migration experience (highly relevant): direct experience with, or strong aptitude for, OS-level migrations (e.g., CentOS to Ubuntu) and application/workflow migrations (e.g., Airflow 1.x DAGs to Airflow 2.x). Comfortable auditing existing workloads, identifying compatibility gaps, and planning cutover.
* Kubernetes: working knowledge of how clusters are built, upgraded, and retired, and how workloads get moved between clusters with minimal disruption — relevant to migrating teams off unsupported clusters onto supported ones.
* CI/CD: experience with at least one major pipeline tool (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins) and the practices around it — automated testing, staged rollouts, safe release processes.
* Observability: familiarity with Prometheus, Grafana, or equivalent, and the ability to use monitoring data to diagnose issues across distributed systems.
* Security awareness: practical understanding of secrets management, access control, and dependency/supply-chain hygiene — enough to spot and flag risk, even if not the platform’s primary security owner.
* Collaboration and communication: able to sit with a dev team, understand their workload and pain points, and communicate technical trade-offs clearly to both engineers and non-engineers.
* Problem-solving: persistence in root-causing failures rather than just restarting services or working around symptoms.
* English level B2.

**Personal Skills**

* Adaptability: comfortable when priorities, tooling, or migration scope shifts mid-project.
* Curiosity: pays attention to how other teams solve infrastructure problems and brings useful patterns back.
* Communication: writes and speaks clearly enough that other teams can act without a follow-up meeting.
* Teamwork: works well embedded with teams outside their own, and shares knowledge freely.
* Ownership: follows a problem to its root cause instead of handing it off once symptoms disappear.
* Attention to detail: catches the small things — an unpinned dependency, an overly broad permission, a config drift.
* Prioritization: can judge what to tackle first when multiple teams need help at the same time.
* User focus: treats the engineering teams using the platform as customers, and measures success by whether their work gets easier.

* Clear instructional copy

* Knowledge checks, quizzes and assessments
* Supporting learning materials

At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have strived to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. By automating routine checks and corrections, our tools speed up production, freeing developers to grow, discover, and create.

ThinkRail is an innovative project within JetBrains' Innovation Hub. Its aim is to develop a declarative programming language tailored to AI-spec-driven development. Our goal is to build an infrastructure that enables the efficient creation of complex systems with AI, while maintaining the trust of users and flexibility in the results.

Thinkrail (GitHub, Blog, Website) is now open source and in alpha, and we’re entering the next stage of the product’s development: initial market penetration. We’re focused on bringing it into real-world projects and turning it into a robust, production-ready system. To help us get there, we’re looking for an Entrepreneur in Residence to join the team. You’d be joining at an early stage, with plenty of opportunity to influence the product as it continues to evolve.

**About the role**

We are looking for an Entrepreneur in Residence/Product Lead to work alongside the technical founder and own the product strategy for Thinkrail.

This is not a traditional product management role. Your focus will be on deeply understanding real developer workflows: where specs, architecture, and code break down, what causes friction, and what problems are actually worth solving. You will translate these insights into concrete product requirements and priorities.

### **In this role, you will:**

* Own the product strategy: Define the direction, validate key hypotheses, and decide what to build first.
* Run continuous discovery: Talk to developers and customers to understand real workflows, pain points, and opportunities.
* Define the initial scope: Identify the ICP, core use cases, and priorities for zero-to-one development.
* Shape GTM: Help define positioning, messaging, launch, and go-to-market strategy.
* Track the ecosystem: Stay close to competitors, adjacent tools, AI developments, and market trends
* Work closely with engineering: Keep a small team focused, aligned, and moving quickly in a highly ambiguous environment

### We will be happy to have you on our team if you have:

* 8+ years of product management experience with end-to-end ownership of strategy, discovery, and delivery
* Startup experience is a must, ideally in a small team, with a strong track record of building and shipping zero-to-one
* Experience with developer tools or AI products is required
* High autonomy, speed, and comfort making decisions with limited information
* Strong technical fluency and the ability to work closely with engineers. Coding experience is a plus
* Founder, co-founder, C-level, or similar experience is a strong advantage
* Experience with GTM, marketing, launches, developer advocacy, or public speaking is also a plus

### **Why join Project Thinkrail?**

* Foundational work: Help define a new direction in developer tooling at the intersection of programming languages and AI.
* Deep technical problems: Work on language design, formal specs, tooling, and AI agents – not surface-level features.
* Real ownership: Own the product’s strategy and direction, working in a role closer to that of a founder than a classic PM.
* JetBrains environment: Enjoy startup-level autonomy with JetBrains’ engineering culture and long-term mindset.

# Senior Software Developer (JCP Core Foundation Licensing and Quotation)

Belgrade, Serbia; Berlin, Germany; Limassol, Cyprus; Madrid, Spain; Munich, Germany; Paphos, Cyprus; Prague, Czech Republic; Remote, Germany; Warsaw, Poland; Yerevan, Armenia

If you want to build and own the systems that decide what JetBrains customers are entitled to use and bill them accurately for it, this is for you. You will focus on designing backend services, keeping complex commercial flows correct, and tackling hard distributed systems challenges on the critical path of every paid request.

**About JetBrains**

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

**What you’ll do**

At JetBrains, the Cloud Platform department builds the underlying infrastructure that powers authentication, paid capabilities, usage metering, and accounting. Within this department, the Licensing & Billing team sits right at the center of our commercial model, turning what a customer buys into what they are actually allowed to use, and accounting for that consumption accurately enough to bill on.

The complexity of our entitlement, quota, and metering systems continues to grow. In this role, you will own the correctness and evolution of these backend services, take full ownership of end-to-end data flows, tackle distributed consistency across unreliable upstream systems, and ensure revenue-affecting data migrations happen cleanly without taking services offline.

**Day to day, you will:**

* Design, build, and operate backend services that decide what a customer is entitled to and what their usage costs.
* Own flows end to end, from ingesting licensing and purchase data from upstream systems to enforcing quotas and recording consumption.
* Evolve our domain model to handle new commercial structures, combining seat-based plans and usage-based models.
* Design integrations with external systems, ensuring correctness through idempotency, ordering, reconciliation, and eventual consistency.
* Plan and execute live data migrations using feature flags, dual writes, backfills, and verification at every stage.
* Build observability into our systems by defining invariants, metrics, and alerts to catch silent divergence before customers do.
* Design internal APIs with explicit focus on versioning, backward compatibility, and developer experience for other JetBrains teams.
* Improve system performance and reliability under continuous production load while decommissioning legacy subsystems.
* Write integration tests against real dependencies and maintain reliable test infrastructure.
* Investigate production incidents, find root causes, and follow through on lasting fixes.

**What you’ll bring**

* An engineer’s dedication to accuracy, especially in domains where system errors have direct financial impact.
* Pragmatic judgment when designing distributed systems where correctness under unreliable delivery is the main constraint.
* A habit of trusting metrics, traces, and logs to understand production behavior rather than relying on assumptions.
* Comfort navigating and simplifying large existing codebases containing legacy decisions.
* Clear, direct communication skills to agree on API contracts across teams with different priorities.
* A focus on testing as an essential design tool rather than an afterthought.

**What you’ll need**

* A proven track record of building and operating backend services on the JVM platform using Kotlin or Java.
* A solid working knowledge of relational databases, including transactions, isolation levels, locking, indexing, and live schema migrations (PostgreSQL preferred).
* A deep understanding of distributed systems patterns, such as idempotency, retry strategies, eventual consistency, and data reconciliation.

## About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at **Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout** already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $14M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.

AI-synthesized from this funder's mission + the role family. Not a hiring guideline.

## About this role

Salary: £74,960.00 - £93,700 Closing date: Wednesday, 16 September 2026 Contract type: Permanent Interview dates: 1st stage (8 and 12 of October) online/Remote; 2nd stage: face to face The Wellcome Trust is a global charitable foundation. We improve health for everyone by funding science, leading policy and advocacy campaigns, and building partnerships.

We committed to spend £16bn in the ten years to 2032, funding new discoveries in life, health, and wellbeing, and taking on three global health challenges: mental health, infectious disease and climate and health. We are looking for a Technology Lead, Discovery (Data Linkage and Data Architecture) to join our team. Where in Wellcome will I be working?

The Discovery team at Wellcome focuses on investing in people and ideas that generate new knowledge and deeper understanding of life, health and wellbeing, with the potential to transform how health challenges are identified, prevented and addressed in the future.

Through initiatives such as the Discovery Research programme, Wellcome Leap and the Wellcome Sanger Institute, the team supports a broad and ambitious portfolio of research, combining flexible funding, innovative programmes and world-leading research to drive meaningful, long-term impact.

A major focus of the Discovery department is to advance our ambition through investments in data, digital tools, technologies and AI as a core capability that transforms how discovery is conceived, conducted, and scaled. What will I be doing?

In this role, you will identify and develop opportunities to advance data linkage and architecture in support of Wellcome’s Discovery strategy, leading high-impact data and technology initiatives from concept through to delivery.

You will work closely with colleagues and external partners to build strong research collaborations, shape strategic priorities, and help maximise the impact of the Discovery Data for Science and Health team’s work.

As a Technology Lead, Discovery (Data Linkage and Data Architecture), you will be responsible for: Identifying and developing funding opportunities in data linkage, data architecture and digital technologies that support Wellcome’s Discovery strategy and maximise the impact of research and innovation.

Building an expert understanding of the health data landscape, particularly in the UK, to identify emerging opportunities, inform investment decisions and shape strategic priorities.

Leading and delivering funding activities, including landscape reviews, funding calls, requests for proposals, contracts and discretionary awards, while providing technical expertise throughout the process.

Developing strong partnerships with researchers, funders, industry and other stakeholders, representing Wellcome externally and fostering collaboration to advance shared goals.

Working closely with colleagues across Discovery, Solutions, Equity and Policy teams to align priorities, share expertise and strengthen Wellcome’s portfolio of data and digital technology investments.

Providing leadership and oversight across key initiatives, supporting delivery through matrix management, ensuring high-quality outputs, managing risks and budgets, and contributing to an inclusive and collaborative team culture. Is this job for me?

This role could be a great fit if you have a strong background in health data, scientific research or digital technologies, along with a deep understanding of the UK health data landscape and how data can advance science and health research.

You'll be comfortable leading complex projects, building relationships across research, funding and industry communities, and using your technical expertise to shape strategic decisions.

We're looking for someone who is curious, collaborative and adaptable, with excellent communication skills and a desire to learn, grow and help others do the same in a fast-moving environment. To apply for this role please submit an updated CV and answer 2 application questions to demonstrate that you meet the minimum requirements for the role.

Minimum Criteria: Demonstrable knowledge of the current state of, and trends in, data linkage, data architecture and digital technologies in science and health research and practice PhD, MD or equivalent level of training in a quantitative, computational, clinical, biological or physical science discipline, with a high-level understanding of the data and software systems used and being developed in science and health.

Experience of working with health relevant or scientific data in a technical and/or strategic capacity. Performance marketing at Kraken is being rebuilt from the ground up. Manual bid management, creative iteration, budget allocation, and audience targeting are being replaced by agent systems that detect signals, make decisions, and execute continuously, learning from every result.

# Lead Software Engineer - Solution & Data Architecture - B2B SaaS Fintech

**Hybrid**EngineeringFull time

London, England, United Kingdom

## Description

**Landytech** is building the intelligent operating platform for modern investment management. Our AI-powered platform, Sesame, brings together investment, corporate and accounting data across asset classes, custodians, currencies and legal entities, creating one secure, trusted source of truth from which our clients can understand their wealth and act with confidence.

Sesame is much more than a reporting tool. We build technology that helps asset owners, asset managers, private banks and trust and company service providers run their entire investment ecosystem: automating complex data and document ingestion, surfacing portfolio and risk insights, anticipating liquidity needs, supporting investment decisions and deal flow, streamlining collaboration and turning intelligence into action through AI.

From family offices managing multigenerational wealth to financial institutions serving clients at scale, Sesame replaces fragmented data and manual processes with clarity, control and smarter decisions.

**Why this role exists**

Our domain is a healthy challenge: multi-custodian, multi-currency, multi-entity financial data, modelled thoughtfully and available at scale. The platform is Kotlin and Spring microservices, with Python where it pays off: metrics, analytics and our AI work. Good features start well before any code gets written, with clear communication about the outcomes to be delivered, followed by planning, prototyping when it helps, and a design the team agrees on.

As technical lead of an R&D team, you'll work closely with a Product Manager on initiatives, improvements and bugs: shaping the work, breaking it down, handing it out across the team, and owning what ships.

You go deep enough into the requirement to push back on it, ask the questions that need asking, and tell apart what the client needs from what the requirement says.

Then you work out how it fits. Usually the right answer is the simple one built on architecture we already have, and defending that is part of the job. Sometimes it isn't, and you're the one who flags that this is a truly new capability, writes the spec and plan, and takes it to our other architects to poke holes in before we commit.

You'll do all this in a team that uses coding agents every day, and you'll help shape how we do that well.

**What you'll own**

You own the partnership with Product: one PM, one lead engineer, one roadmap. You sit with product and domain experts before the ticket exists, understand the business problem, push back on the requirement where it needs it, and come back with honest trade-offs on cost, risk and time. You plan, size and hand out the work, and keep the team unblocked while it ships.

Security, scalability, availability and performance are design inputs on every initiative, not a hardening phase at the end. You cover tenant isolation, auth, data protection and auditability, because our clients' data is about as sensitive as it gets. You know how the system behaves under load and at month-end when everyone runs reports at once, you set the SLOs, and you make sure we can see whether we're meeting them. You are the escalation point when the team hits something genuinely hard, and you go in and solve it with them.

For every significant initiative you produce the design: what changes, in which services, what the contracts and data flows look like, what we reuse and what we leave alone. You write it down, take the challenge from our other architects, and improve it. When a requirement exposes a gap in the platform, you name it and propose what should exist.

You own feature architecture end to end, from the React frontend through our Kotlin and Spring services, across data stores and events, down to Azure. You decide what goes where, and push hard for the simplest solution the existing architecture can carry.

You set the coding standards, API design, testing, quality gates, and security and dependency hygiene. That now covers how we work with coding agents: the rules they follow, the skills and MCP integrations we build over our own systems, and the review process that holds quality as more code gets generated. You're the one who challenges what an agent proposed, because plausible code that passes its tests can still be wrong about concurrency, a data model or a failure mode.

You model the financial domain: positions, transactions, instruments, valuations, entities and hierarchies, so it holds up as new asset classes, custodians and jurisdictions arrive. You build pipelines that stay correct when the source data is messy, late or wrong, and fast enough to run over long histories on demand.

You line-manage a squad: objectives, one-to-ones, feedback that moves careers, hiring, onboarding and code reviews people learn from. You bring back what's new and make sure it lands with the team rather than staying in your head.

You stay hands-on throughout - this is not a role where you stop writing code.

**What we're looking for**

* 8+ years building backend systems in production, with real depth in **Kotlin and/or Java (17+)** and the **Spring** ecosystem (Boot, Web, Security, Data).
* A track record of **architecting systems, not just services**: you've owned significant design decisions in a distributed or microservices platform and lived with the consequences.
* Strong **data modelling and SQL** skills, plus experience designing data ingestion, transformation or ETL pipelines. You've dealt with data you couldn't trust.
* Enough **Python** to design and review it. Our metrics, analytics and AI services are written in it, so you need to be able to reason about them, not to be a Python specialist.

## Description

Landytech is on a mission to revolutionise the way that investment managers, asset owners and their advisors access asset information. Powered by Sesame, an industry-leading investment reporting platform, we are helping clients in over 15 countries make informed investment decisions and deliver insights faster.

The company is growing rapidly and it's an exciting time to join, having secured $12M in Series B funding in January 2023. In just four years, it has gone from two co-founders to a team of 80+ staff, with offices in London and Paris. At Landytech, we see diversity as our strength with a team from over 15 countries and 14 languages spoken.

**The role**

AI has made producing screens easy. It has not made products coherent. We are looking for someone to own the experience of Sesame end to end - the client journey, the interaction logic, the look and feel, and the consistency of all of it - and to build it.

If you are an engineer who has always had a view on how the product should look and behave, this is a role where that judgement is part of the remit rather than a side interest.

*We have posted this role under two titles - Design Engineer and Product Experience Designer - to reach both backgrounds. Same role, same team. Apply once, to whichever fits you better.*

**How we work**

We have rebuilt our product process around AI rather than bolting it on:

- AI is used heavily at every stage of both design and engineering, not just at the production end

- Our design system lives in code, used by engineers and AI tooling alike

- Tooling changes every few months and we expect it to

You will have real scope to shape how we work, and to help build the parts that do not exist yet.

**What you will shape**

How much of this you lead outright will depend on your experience and on how it fits with the team already in place. There is room to take on more over time.

* **The front-end experience layer.** You will build the interfaces that matter most, particularly the dense and difficult ones, and help set the patterns others follow
* **The design system.** Developed in code with the rest of the front-end team, with a leading voice in what belongs in the system
* **Look, feel and consistency.** The product should feel like one thing, and you will help define what that one thing is and uphold it in review and in tooling
* **The client journey.** You will be in front of investment professionals, family offices and their advisors, and trusted to act on what you hear
* **Craft in dense financial interfaces.** Tables legible at scale, numbers at the right precision, drill-downs that survive a messy real portfolio under load

**The must-have: setting the standard AI works to**

AI is very good at producing attractive interfaces. Given a design system, almost anyone can now generate a credible screen.

The harder problem, and the one this role exists to solve, is making sure what we build expresses the product's logic, density and intent rather than simply reusing its components. That means defining the standards and instructions our tools work to, reading the output critically enough to see why something is subtly wrong, and tightening the rules so it does not recur.

Using AI to produce interfaces is not the skill we are looking for. Directing it to our standard, consistently and at depth, is.

Increasingly this is engineering work: it lives in the repo, in the tooling, and in what the agents can and cannot reach for.

**Strongly valued: design expertise**

We are not looking for a front-end engineer willing to tolerate design work. We are looking for real UX judgement.

* You can say what is wrong with a flow, not just implement it faster
* You think in objects, relationships and states before components
* You have taste in what matters here: hierarchy, typography, density, restraint
* You are comfortable doing the upstream thinking, including what should not exist at all

No portfolio required. Shipped interfaces we can look at, and the decisions behind them, is what we want to see.

**Also valued: product management instincts**

If you have talked to clients directly, decided what not to build, and owned an outcome rather than a ticket, we will weight it heavily.

**What we are looking for**

We do not expect anyone to have everything below - we would rather meet someone exceptional in two areas than adequate in all three.

* 5+ years in front-end engineering, ideally React and TypeScript, with libraries such as shadcn/ui
* Experience building and maintaining a design system in production, not just consuming one
* Data-dense interfaces at scale - virtualised tables, charting, performance under real load
* Fluency with AI-assisted development, and the specification skill described above
* Willingness to work directly with users and own the experience, not the implementation alone
* Comfortable as an editor and enabler: reviewing others' work, teaching, holding a line
* Genuine curiosity about finance. You need not arrive knowing what a capital call is

**Our process**

Our interview process is likely to include a portfolio or work conversation, a short practical exercise based on a real Sesame flow, and a working session with a product manager and an engineer. We adapt the steps to the candidate and will always tell you what to expect in advance.

* Deliver an exceptional candidate experience from first conversation through to offer, acting as a trusted and credible ambassador for Legora throughout.

**What you bring**

You understand that hiring decisions are business decisions, and you hold yourself accountable to the same outcomes as the teams you hire for. You're hands-on, sharp, and trusted by senior leaders to shape teams that win. We're looking for:

## **✅** About the Role

As a Software Engineer on the AWS Emulator team, you’ll help expand and harden LocalStack’s AWS emulator by taking ownership of individual services and making them behave as closely as possible to real AWS.

The challenge is genuinely unusual: you’ll reimplement cloud services that you can only observe from the outside. Making a service “work” is one thing; matching AWS behaviour — including edge cases and undocumented details — is a very different engineering problem.

We’re looking for someone who learns quickly, enjoys tackling unfamiliar problems, and can turn incomplete information into working solutions. You’ll have end-to-end ownership of your services, from investigating how they behave and deciding what needs to be built through implementation, testing, and ongoing improvements.

AI is a core part of how the team works. You’ll use modern AI coding and agentic tools to make development more efficient while maintaining the quality and reliability expected by LocalStack users. The role offers a clear path to broader service ownership and technical leadership as your scope grows.

* **Internalize services off moto.** Independently take AWS services from moto-backed to fully first-party implementations, owning store design for persistence, full API operation coverage, and conformance to LocalStack conventions rather than transplanted moto code. Measured by services shipped and their size.
* **Close parity gaps in owned services.** Raise snapshot-test coverage against real AWS for the documented API surface for owned services, with a measurable reduction in parity defects reported from the field.
* **Own services end-to-end after they ship.** Act as first responder for their services: customer-reported parity bugs triaged and turned around within 5 days median, including those that surface through Terraform and CDK rather than direct API calls.

* Experience with distributed systems, storage, or protocol conformance.

Social care is one of the UK's most important sectors, yet much of the technology supporting it hasn't kept pace with what's possible.

* **Integrate**, offering intensive consultancy and leadership support to embed AI into workflows and drive business transformation.

Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers.

## **What you'll do**

This role is scoped by skill rather than by product. The problems below span multiple departments and show up across our Search and Places data work, our Location and Navigation Intelligence work, and the Platform work that makes Mapbox usable by agents. You'll be hired into one specific team or product area, but you'll work across teams where your expertise meets the highest-priority AI problems. You should expect to move between teams and tech stacks as the work demands.

At this level you own the technical design and delivery of a multi-component AI system, and you are accountable for the quality of what ships in your area.

## **In this role, you will:**

* Define how the products you own should work, build a measurement framework for it, and build evaluation systems for non-deterministic behavior. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results.
* Run continuous evaluation of the products we build, whether APIs, SDKs, data representations, or reference applications, from the position of the end user, whether developer, agent, or consumer. Assess the gaps such as misuse of parameters or integration anti-patterns, recommend the fixes, and make sure they land.
* Own the MVP against an agreed north star technical design, and balance technical perfection against shipping useful increments.
* Build data pipelines and the tooling around them: ingestion, conflation, entity resolution, quality checks, and the batch and streaming jobs that keep a large dataset current.
* Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Evaluate what fits the problem and constraints , and decide when to adopt what exists versus build your own.
* Design feedback loops so that using a product generates data that improves it. Instrument systems so failures arrive with enough context to reproduce, then turn the recurring ones into evaluation cases.
* Design the boundary between a model and the tools it calls. Build or improve the model harness, decide what the model handles, what it delegates, and how to keep it working from the state it actually fetched.
* Work to a latency and cost target per request: streaming, partial results, caching, model routing, prompt structure.
* Build the internal harnesses and tools (CLI, MCP, and others) your team needs to iterate quickly, and share the parts that generalize with other teams.
* Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice.
* Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them.
* Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

##

‍

‍

‍  
We are now building out an in-house development function, and this is the first hire into it.

‍

## Role Overview

Almost everything we run internally has been built in-house: reconciliation tooling, bank API integrations, document verification, operational reporting, and our client-facing platform. Software is not a support function here. It is how the business moves faster than firms ten times its size.

‍  
We are looking for a Junior Developer to work directly alongside our Lead Developer on that toolset.

‍  
This is not a role where you will be handed a ticket and a specification. You will be handed a problem, usually described by someone in operations or trading who does not know what the solution looks like, and you will be expected to work out what actually needs building.

‍  
We build with AI tooling as standard. We are not looking for someone who can write a linked list on a whiteboard. We are looking for someone who can take an ambiguous business problem, break it down, build something that works, and know the difference between code that runs and code that is correct.

‍

‍

## Your Mission

#### Business Development & Portfolio Growth

* Build and maintain internal tools that automate manual operational processes
* Work directly with operations, trading, and compliance to scope problems before building anything
* Integrate with third-party systems: bank APIs, Salesforce, internal databases
* Investigate and fix defects in existing systems, including code you did not write
* Test your own work properly, including the failure cases, before it goes anywhere near live data
* Document what you build so someone else can pick it up
* Flag risk early and loudly, particularly anything touching client money

‍

* 0-3 years previous experience in developing
* Demonstrable ability to build and ship working software, however you acquired it. Degree, bootcamp, self-taught, or a folder of things you built for yourself, we genuinely do not mind
* A working understanding of at least one language (we mostly use Python and JavaScript) and the confidence to pick up others as required
* Comfort with the fundamentals: APIs, databases, version control, how data moves between systems
* Fluent, critical use of AI coding tools. You should be able to tell us where they have been wrong and how you caught it
* Evidence that you have built something nobody asked you to build
* Clear written communication, including the ability to explain a technical decision to someone non-technical

We are looking for someone to lead tracking and measurement implementation across our client base. This is a hands-on build role with genuine client ownership, not an oversight role.

You will audit and rebuild measurement setups end to end: GA4 and Google Tag Manager, server-side tagging, consent and CMP configuration, paid media conversion tracking, CRM integrations and app measurement. **Salary up to £45k DOE**

**This is a hybrid role that will require travelling to our Leeds HQ.**

### What you’ll be doing

#### **Measurement architecture and implementation**

* Audit GA4 properties end to end — data streams, key events, custom dimensions and metrics, channel groupings, cross-domain configuration, internal and staging traffic exclusion, attribution settings and data retention.
* Rebuild and configure GA4 to a documented standard, including e-commerce and enhanced measurement.
* Own GTM web containers: audit, restructure, naming conventions and governance, trigger and variable design, and disciplined version control and publishing.
* Design and implement server-side GTM — hosting via Stape, Addingwell or GCP, custom clients and tag transports, and phased migration from client-side without breaking data continuity.
* Diagnose measurement failures: duplicate transactions, inflated user counts, misfiring tags, attribution gaps and cross-platform discrepancies, using live debugging, BigQuery and platform interfaces.

#### **Consent and compliance**

* Audit, configure and rebuild consent management platforms – OneTrust, Cookiebot, Civic and similar – including cookie catalogues, categorisation and blocking behaviour.
* Implement and validate Google Consent Mode v2 across both client-side and server-side environments.
* Manually audit hard-coded tags across client sites to confirm they genuinely respect consent. This is the work most audits skip, and it is where the real exposure sits.
* Maintain cookie and tag registers, and support clients on PECR and UK GDPR obligations alongside their legal and compliance teams.

#### **Paid media measurement**

* Audit, build and validate conversion tracking and pixels across Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Microsoft Ads and affiliate platforms.
* Implement enhanced conversions, Meta Conversions API, TikTok Events API and equivalent server-side event flows.
* Resolve deduplication, event match quality and consent-driven signal loss so that automated bidding is working from data we trust.
* Work directly with our paid media teams to translate measurement problems into campaign decisions, and vice versa.

#### **Data and CRM integration**

* Integrate Salesforce with Google Ads and GA4 for offline conversion import and closed-loop reporting.
* Extend the same approach to Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn and other platforms using Zapier, native connectors or custom endpoints.
* Configure and use BigQuery exports for validation, reconciliation and reporting.

#### **App measurement**

* Audit and implement app tracking across Firebase and GA4, including event taxonomy and parameter design.
* Handle App Tracking Transparency and in-app consent, and audit SDK behaviour against the consent state.
* Work with mobile measurement partners on attribution setup, SKAdNetwork and deduplication against web activity.

#### **Specification, QA and documentation**

* Write bespoke data layer specifications that development teams can build from without coming back with questions.
* Run structured QA before and after every release, with a documented test plan rather than a spot check.
* Produce audit reports and implementation documentation that clients keep and actually use.
* Set and maintain the internal standards, templates and naming conventions the wider team works to.

### **What you’ll bring**

##### **Essential**

* Hands-on implementation experience with GA4 and Google Tag Manager, in an agency, consultancy or complex in-house environment.
* Demonstrable server-side tagging experience.
* Strong working knowledge of consent management and Consent Mode v2, and the confidence to audit tag behaviour manually rather than trusting a vendor dashboard.
* Conversion tracking experience across major ad platforms.
* Ability to write clear technical specifications a developer can build from.
* Able to own a project plan, hold a timeline and flag risk early.

##### **Desirable**

* CRM-to-ad-platform integration, particularly Salesforce, and familiarity with tools like Zapier for the platforms without native connectors.
* App measurement: Firebase, GA4 for apps, and any of the major MMPs (Branch, AppsFlyer, Adjust).

# Head of Engineering, Rewards

**Who we are**

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

**Why United Kingdom**

The UK is home to our headquarters where more than 70 team members are based. Our London office is located at Sea Containers, just by London Bridge - this is also where a significant number of our most senior leaders sit, which makes it a natural base for a Head of Engineering.

So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in United Kingdom.

**About The Role**

Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people.

Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale.

The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve.

This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader.

Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs.

You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes:

* Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end.
