## **The Opportunity**

This is one of the highest-leverage commercial roles in the business. As Sales Director, you'll own the entire sales system at Relay — strategy, structure, process, and performance across all four of our segments: Pitstop/Field Sales, Enterprise, Large Parcel, and SME Parcel. You'll set the standards that let each segment lead build well, and you'll be personally accountable for the sum of the results.

Beyond the day-to-day, this role has a genuine builder's brief: creating the infrastructure and team capabilities that take Relay international over the next few years. If you want to shape how a fast-growing carrier goes to market at scale — and leave a lasting mark on how that machine works — this is the role.

## 

## **What You'll Own**

### Sales strategy and structure

* Design the shape of Relay's sales organisation across all four segments — how they relate, where they overlap, how resource is prioritised
* Define the sales motion for each segment: who it sells to, how, and through which channel
* Keep strategy current as the business and market evolve

### Data and performance management

* Set the metrics that matter across pipeline, conversion, quota attainment, and productivity
* Build or oversee the dashboards that surface them
* Use data to make decisions on resourcing, territory design, and where to invest or pull back — instinct complements data here, it doesn't replace it

### Process, structure, and scalability

* Own the sales playbook, forecasting cadence, deal review process, CRM hygiene standards, and comp and quota-setting principles
* Upskill and coach the existing team on pitch, process, and performance
* Build infrastructure that scales for the next three years, not just today's headcount

### Team leadership and org design

* Lead the four segment sales leads (Pitstop/Field, Enterprise, Large Parcel, SME Parcel) and any central sales ops or enablement partners
* Decide what's centralised across functions versus what each segment lead owns locally
* Hire, develop, and coach those leads so each can build out their patch well

### Global and remote team leadership

* Lead teams remotely across time zones and geographies as Relay expands into the Americas and Europe
* Proven capability to do this is a requirement — it can't be learned on the job here

### Exec partnership and GTM planning

* Partner with the CCO and other function leads on revenue planning, headcount decisions, and commercial trade-offs
* Translate company strategy into a sequenced sales roadmap and GTM direction
* Push back clearly when targets or timelines aren't realistic

## 

## **Who Will Thrive in This Role**

* Multi-motion sales leader. You've led more than one kind of sales motion — for example, high-volume SMB or transactional sales alongside enterprise or mid-market relationship-led sales. You're comfortable setting standards and managing performance across both. You've carried a number yourself and led others doing the same. This isn't a role for a single-lane specialist.
* Data-driven and structured operator. You define the metrics that matter, build or oversee the dashboards, and use data to make resourcing and process calls — not gut feel alone. You have a track record of introducing or significantly upgrading forecasting discipline, CRM hygiene, territory design, and comp structures in ways that improved consistency and scalability. You think in systems across a multi-year horizon, not just the next quarter.
* Global and remote team builder. You've led sales teams across multiple geographies or time zones, ideally including the US and Europe. You're comfortable setting standards, culture, and expectations remotely. Having helped take a company into a new country is a bonus; the core requirement is proven capability.
* People leader and org designer. You've led sales managers or leaders — not just individual contributors — and operated at least one layer removed from the front line. You have a track record of hiring and developing leaders beneath you, and making clear calls about what to centralise versus what to delegate.
* Exec partner. You've partnered directly with a CEO, founder, or C-suite on revenue planning and commercial trade-offs. You can push back on unrealistic targets while maintaining trust, and you can translate company strategy into an actionable, sequenced sales roadmap.
* Builder, not just operator. You've introduced new process, data infrastructure, or org structure in a previous role — not only operated within a system someone else built. This role is not about being a super-IC closer or a sector-pedigree hire; logistics experience is welcome but not a requirement or a filter.

* 25 days of holidays
* Enhanced parental leave.
* Hardware of your choice.
* Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more).

* **Aim with Precision:** You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.
* **Play to Win:** You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.
* **1% Better Every Day**: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.
* **All In, All the Time**: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.
* **People-Powered Greatness**: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.
* **Grow the Whole Pie**: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

# **Job Description**

**Senior / Lead Embedded Software Engineer (C)**

**Salary range from £48,000 to £65,000 depending on experience**

**About the Role**

We have opportunities for ambitious Embedded Software Engineers at Senior and Lead level to join our multidisciplinary engineering team at the forefront of additive manufacturing technology.

Our embedded software platforms are central to the control, sensing, communication, monitoring and real-time processing capabilities of our next-generation products. Working within Research & Development, you will contribute to the full product lifecycle, from concept and architecture through verification, release to production, and long-term support.

These are hands-on engineering roles, combining embedded software development, debugging and verification with close collaboration across electronics, FPGA, systems, algorithms and mechanical engineering teams. Depending on experience and grade, you will also provide technical leadership, influence engineering strategy, and mentor developing engineers.

The software frequently interacts with microcontrollers, FPGAs, sensors, communication networks and analogue electronics. As such, a strong appreciation of system-level design and hardware/software interaction is essential.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Embedded Software Development**

* Develop embedded software architectures and applications from concept through to production release.
* Design, implement and maintain high-quality C software with a focus on performance, reliability, maintainability and portability.
* Develop low-level drivers, middleware and application-layer software for embedded systems.
* Implement communication interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet and industrial communication protocols.
* Optimise software for real-time performance, memory usage and deterministic behaviour.
* Support product sustainment, issue investigation and software improvements throughout the product lifecycle.
* Develop reusable software frameworks and libraries for use across multiple projects and product generations.

**Verification & Validation**

* Develop robust software verification strategies covering unit, integration and system-level testing.
* Create automated test frameworks and regression test suites.
* Define verification plans, acceptance criteria and coverage objectives.
* Support hardware-in-the-loop, system integration and product validation activities.
* Drive continuous improvement in automated testing, continuous integration and software quality metrics.
* Investigate and resolve complex software and system-level defects.

**Systems & Product Development**

* Capture, analyse and refine requirements, ensuring clear traceability from customer and system requirements through to implementation and verification.
* Work closely with systems, electronics, FPGA, algorithms and test engineers to deliver integrated solutions.
* Evaluate and implement control, signal processing and embedded algorithms on target hardware platforms.
* Contribute to safety, reliability and compliance activities, including design assurance and audit-ready engineering evidence.
* Produce and maintain high-quality technical documentation, including software architecture specifications, interface definitions, design descriptions and verification reports.

**Technical Leadership**

* Provide technical leadership for embedded software development activities across projects.
* Drive engineering excellence through design reviews, code reviews, development standards and best practices.
* Support planning, estimation, technical risk management and project delivery.
* Mentor engineers, graduates and apprentices, helping develop both technical capability and engineering judgement.
* Promote reusable software architectures and continuous improvement across tools, methodologies and processes.

**Essential Requirements**

* Degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics or a related discipline.
* Strong commercial experience developing embedded software using C.
* Solid understanding of embedded software principles, including:

  + Real-time and deterministic systems
  + DMA and Interrupt-driven architectures
  + Memory management
  + State machines
  + Communications protocols
  + Multi-threaded and event-driven systems
* Experience developing software for microcontroller-based systems.
* Experience debugging software on target hardware using modern debugging tools.
* Understanding of software development lifecycles, version control and testing methodologies.
* Ability to communicate effectively within a multidisciplinary engineering team.

***(Additional Requirements for Lead Embedded Software Engineer)***

* *Significant experience architecting complex embedded software systems.*
* *Proven ability to lead software development activities through the full product lifecycle.*
* *Strong understanding of requirements management, design reviews and engineering governance.*
* *Experience mentoring engineers and providing technical leadership.*
* *Demonstrated ability to balance technical excellence with delivery objectives.*

**Desirable Requirements**

* Experience with ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers and associated development environments.
* Knowledge of C++, Python or scripting languages used for automation and testing.
* Experience implementing industrial communication protocols such as EtherCAT, Modbus, CANopen or IO-Link.
* Experience with Git, Azure DevOps and CI/CD workflows.
* Familiarity with unit testing frameworks and static analysis tools.
* Understanding of control systems, signal processing and numerical algorithms.
* Knowledge of FPGA-based systems and hardware/software partitioning.
* Experience of high-speed digital electronics, EMC and mixed-signal systems.
* Experience working within regulated or safety-conscious product development environments.

**Person Specification**

You are a passionate and capable engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and delivering robust, high-quality products.

You combine strong embedded software expertise with a systems-level mindset and are comfortable working across disciplinary boundaries. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively and take ownership of technical outcomes.

At Senior level, you are a trusted delivery engineer capable of independently owning significant work packages.

At Lead level, you provide technical direction, mentor others and help ensure successful project delivery.

You are naturally curious, pragmatic and quality-focused, with a strong appreciation of how embedded software interacts with electronics, FPGA technology, mechanical systems and user requirements to create reliable, high-performance products.

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. Are you an experienced BMS, electrical or critical-power engineer who enjoys analysing system performance, solving complex technical issues and turning data into practical recommendations?

 

We are looking for a Senior BMS & Electrical Systems Engineer to join Schneider Electric’s Digital Services Remote Operations team.

 

This is a proactive engineering role focused on remotely monitoring and analysing sophisticated electrical and Building Management Systems across a portfolio of major customers. You will use system data, diagnostics and analytics to identify issues, improve reliability, uncover energy-saving opportunities and help customers get more from their assets.

 

Internally, the position is titled **Senior Engineer I, Digital Services Remote Operations**.

You will support an assigned portfolio of customers, including large and complex organisations operating multiple Schneider Electric systems.

 

Your responsibilities will include:

 

* Monitor connected electrical and BMS assets and investigate system events, alarms and performance issues.
* Carry out remote diagnostics and troubleshoot complex technical problems.
* Analyse system and asset data to identify trends, potential failures and opportunities for optimisation.
* Conduct predictive analysis and provide recommendations that improve asset reliability and performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve energy efficiency and overall system operation.
* Turn complex technical data into clear reports, visualisations and practical recommendations.
* Provide technical consultancy and guidance to customers, helping them understand system performance and recommended actions.
* Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders and act as a trusted technical point of contact.
* Support colleagues with complex or escalated technical issues and share knowledge across the wider team.

 

**What are we looking for?**

 

You will have a strong engineering background in one or more of the following areas:

 

* Building Management Systems, BMS
* Electrical distribution or electrical systems
* Critical or secure power
* Data centres or other critical environments
* Building automation, controls or connected building systems

 

You should also be comfortable working with system data and using it to diagnose problems, identify trends and recommend improvements.

 

**We would particularly like to hear from you if you have:**

 

* Strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills.
* Experience analysing BMS, electrical or asset-performance data.
* Knowledge of predictive analytics or condition-based monitoring.
* Experience working with asset management, monitoring or IoT platforms.
* The ability to interpret technical information and explain findings clearly to customers.
* Strong communication and customer-facing skills.
* A proactive problem-solving approach and the confidence to work independently.
* Experience supporting large, complex or high-profile customer environments.

This is a UK-based role.

 

The position is primarily focused on remote monitoring, diagnostics and customer support, rather than regular site-based engineering.

There is no shift pattern, with the team working standard office hours.

* Work with sophisticated connected electrical and building systems.
* Develop your expertise in diagnostics, predictive analytics and IoT technologies.
* Work directly with major customers and influence how their systems perform.
* See the impact of your recommendations on reliability, energy efficiency and customer performance.
* Work in a flexible environment that values technical expertise, collaboration and continuous learning.

London, England, United Kingdom

We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical intern to join our Operations division under the Middle Office team at Schonfeld in our London office. * Working knowledge of Python, SQL, and/or another programming language

# Salesforce Platform Architect

London, United Kingdom

## Job Description

**Who we're looking for**

We are seeking an experienced Salesforce Platform Architect with a proven track record of owning the architecture, integrity and technical direction of large-scale Salesforce implementations within global financial services organisations. The ideal candidate combines deep technical mastery of the Salesforce platform with the breadth to think holistically across technology, data and operating model. They will have high standards, an eye for detail, a continuous improvement mindset, and the judgement and credibility to influence senior stakeholders across both business and technology.

You will define and own the target-state architecture for the Salesforce ecosystem, set the technical principles and guardrails that engineering teams build within, and make the trade-offs needed to keep the platform scalable, secure, maintainable and cost-effective. A strong understanding of the financial services industry is essential. You should be comfortable operating from pre-programme mobilisation through to production, shaping solution direction on complex change while safeguarding the long-term coherence of the platform.

**About Schroders**

Schroders is a global investment manager which provides active asset management, wealth management and investment solutions. We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. We serve a diverse client base that includes pension schemes, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, high net worth individuals, family offices, as well as end clients through partnerships with distributors, financial advisers, and online platforms.

Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.

**Technology at Schroders**

There's a huge amount of change happening at Schroders. Technology is shaping our business more and more, creating numerous opportunities. As a significant financial player, we can put substantial backing behind good ideas. While we have enormous responsibilities to our clients and shareholders, our tech teams are friendlier and more informal than you might expect.

**The base**

We moved into our new HQ in the City of London in 2018. We're close to our clients, in the heart of the UK's financial centre, and we have everything we need to work flexibly.

**The team**

The Asset Management Platforms department at Schroders is a global technology change delivery function that oversees and executes all technology delivery within the organisation. The Client Engagement team sits within Client Technology and is responsible for all platforms associated with the provision of client relationship management, with a strong emphasis on the Salesforce ecosystem (including Sales Cloud, Service Cloud and Financial Services Cloud). The core team is responsible for understanding business needs, solving complex problems, mobilising and delivering large change programmes, and maintaining the integrity of the Salesforce platform and associated capabilities.

**What you'll do**

* Own and evolve the end-to-end target-state architecture for the Salesforce platform across both our Public and Private businesses, balancing business value, scalability, security, maintainability and total cost of ownership.
* Define and champion the architectural principles, patterns, standards and guardrails that engineering teams design and build within, ensuring solution coherence across a multi-team, multi-workstream portfolio.
* Lead solution design for complex and early-stage (pre-project) initiatives, translating ambiguous business problems into robust, well-reasoned architectural direction with clear options and trade-offs.
* Own the integration architecture connecting Salesforce with upstream and downstream platforms (APIs, event-driven patterns, middleware such as MuleSoft, ETL and data platforms) to enable joined-up client journeys and high-quality, trusted data.
* Govern platform integrity—data model, security model, governor limits, org strategy, technical debt and release management—ensuring the platform remains performant, secure and sustainable as it scales.
* Provide architectural assurance across delivery teams through design reviews, technical governance forums and alignment to AMP enterprise architecture and Global Technology lifecycle standards.
* Take a holistic view of the target state, recognising that the outcome will often include changes to the business operating model and data architecture alongside the technology platform.
* Drive DevOps and CI/CD maturity from an architectural standpoint—branching strategy, environment and sandbox strategy, automated testing and release management—to accelerate delivery and reduce risk.
* Harness emerging AI capabilities—including Salesforce Einstein and Agentforce—to enhance productivity, decision-making and client engagement, guiding practical use cases from concept to a well-architected implementation.
* Ensure architecture reflects the regulatory and compliance context of asset management (for example, data privacy, client communications and marketing compliance).
* Mentor and coach engineers and analysts, lead by example on technical craftsmanship, and raise the architectural capability of the wider team.
* Collaborate with and contribute to relevant AMP architecture and delivery communities of practice, helping to define good practice and improve standards and ways of working.
* Work closely with the Client Platform Architect to ensure the Salesforce target state aligns with the wider Client Technology architecture and enterprise architecture direction.

**The knowledge, experience and qualifications you need**

**Essential**

* Extensive hands-on Salesforce experience within a large, global financial services organisation, with a proven track record of owning platform-level architecture and technical direction.
* Salesforce Certified Technical Architect (CTA).
* Salesforce Certified Application Architect and System Architect; Platform Developer I/II highly desirable.
* Deep understanding of Salesforce architecture, data modelling, security, sharing, governor limits, org strategy and platform best practices, with the ability to take a holistic view of the target state across technology, data and operating model.
* Strong integration architecture experience using REST/SOAP APIs, event-driven patterns and middleware such as MuleSoft to connect Salesforce with the wider technology estate.
* Proven experience defining DevOps and CI/CD strategy and tooling (e.g. Git, Copado, Gearset, Azure DevOps), automated testing and release management on the Salesforce platform.
* Ability to define architectural principles and guardrails and to govern delivery teams' adherence to them without becoming a bottleneck.
* Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences and influence at all levels.
* Strong knowledge and experience of the end-to-end SDLC (Agile, Waterfall, hybrid etc.) and modern engineering disciplines.
* Good eye for detail and hands-on experience of producing high-quality architecture artefacts, technical designs and specifications.
* Awareness of how regulatory and compliance requirements (for example, data privacy, client communications, marketing compliance) influence architectural decisions.
* Experience of working with global colleagues and stakeholders and sensitivity to cultural differences, time zones etc.

**Desirable**

* Familiarity with sales enablement and content management platforms, ideally Seismic, including content automation, personalisation workflows, analytics and CRM integration.
* Experience delivering within complex, multi-vendor and third-party ecosystems, including management of strategic platform providers.
* Experience within client engagement, distribution or client relationship management functions in an asset or investment management context.
* Understanding of modern technology architectures, including cloud-based platforms and API-driven ecosystems, and how CRM connects with data lakes and analytics platforms.
* Exposure to AI-driven capabilities (Einstein, Agentforce) and how these integrate into platform architecture and client engagement workflows.

**What you'll be like**

The ideal candidate for the Salesforce Platform Architect role will be a pragmatic and collaborative technical leader who takes pride in engineering craftsmanship while thinking strategically about the long-term health of the platform. You will be comfortable making and defending architectural decisions, balancing business urgency with technical quality, and holding solution direction to account across multiple teams. A natural mentor, you will raise standards across the team, lead by example, and engage credibly with technical peers and senior stakeholders alike. Your innovative approach will drive the exploration of cutting-edge tools, patterns and AI-enabled solutions, ultimately enhancing platform quality and business outcomes.

That's why inclusion is a strategic priority for us, and we are an equal opportunities employer. Working closely with stakeholders across the business, the role helps promote robust tax risk management and effective governance across the private assets platform.

**The base**

We moved into our new HQ in the City of London in 2018. We’re close to our clients, in the heart of the UK’s financial centre and we have everything we need to work flexibly.

* Support the Head of Private Assets Tax in applying the Group Tax risk framework and agreed tax risk appetite to private asset products and structures.
* Provide second-line tax input and undertake risk-based review of complex or higher-risk transactions and tax positions.
* Contribute to tax guidelines and standard positions for fund and investment structures, including key tax guardrails aligned to agreed risk appetite.
* Review investor terms, side letters and structuring proposals where these may depart from agreed principles or create material tax risk.
* Assist in the assessment of proposed departures from Group Tax policy or agreed tax principles, documenting implications and escalating to the Head of Private Assets Tax where required.
* Help maintain visibility of early-stage structuring activity, including through relevant governance papers and forums where appropriate, in order to identify matters requiring second-line review, challenge or escalation.
* Contribute to the application of agreed principles and expectations for external adviser engagements, and provide input or review for complex or high-risk matters where required.
* Help maintain governance materials and control tools, including playbooks, checklists, review thresholds and escalation triggers, to promote consistent tax risk management.

* Be the client's trusted Paid Search lead, leading strategic conversations about performance, growth opportunities and where to invest next.

* Build a joined-up growth plan with the Growth Strategist — you own Paid Search, they own social spend, offer strategy and conversion strategy — bringing your expertise to those decisions and agreeing shared priorities.
* Connect search intent and product performance with creative, offer and landing page decisions, sharing insights across teams and turning them into coordinated tests.
* Plan around promotions, stock availability, product margins and repeat purchase behaviour, keeping channel decisions grounded in the client's wider economics.

* Stay hands-on with campaign builds, bidding, product feeds, testing and optimisation, maintaining strong standards for account structure, measurement and reporting.
* Keep clients in the loop on current testing, key account changes and ongoing strategy through weekly, monthly and quarterly updates.

* Help build the systems and ways of working that let a small team grow while maintaining quality and client confidence.

# Security Operations Engineer (Europe - Remote)

Europe (Remote)

### **Mission – Why we exist, what we do, and why we need you**

SpotMe is a leading B2B event platform that helps enterprises increase the impact of their events by delivering CRM-connected, high-quality experiences across in-person, virtual, hybrid events, and webinars. With a strong focus on life sciences, SpotMe powers Onomi: an HCP engagement product that enables medical and commercial teams to run impactful congresses, symposia, advisory boards, and webinars. Together, SpotMe and Onomi turn events into a company’s most effective engagement channel.

This role sets and runs the security configuration of the company across different tools we use.

This position is the ideal role for **someone who wants to raise the level of IT security in an environment where it carries real weight**. Our customers are enterprises, and more than half a million healthcare professionals engage on Onomi every month. How our own accounts, laptops and tools are secured is part of that picture rather than a back-office concern. This is not about one access request or one control, it is about lifting the IT layer that everything else sits on.

As a Security Operations Engineer, you will be reporting to the Chief Security and Trust Officer and you will spend roughly:

* 35% Identity, access and lifecycle. Joiners, movers and leavers, access requests and approvals, associate access, security hygiene across our SaaS tools, access reviews. Google Workspace is our identity layer.
* 20% Endpoint management and protection. Implementing both across our macOS fleet, then keeping the fleet in a known state and triaging what the tooling reports once it is live.
* 30% Security controls and access models inside our tools. Around a dozen SaaS applications, each with its own permission model, its own security controls, its own limits on what can actually be enforced, and its own logging capability. You will manage how each should be configured, design the role and permission structures inside them, work out what a given plan tier does and does not allow, and know where a tool is blind so we can compensate elsewhere. This also covers the alerts and logs from the tools we already have, including threat intelligence.
* 15% Building internal tooling. Access reporting, cross-tool investigation, and a small, deliberately tuned detection layer. Built primarily with Claude Code, jointly with the CSTO, against a written specification that already exists.

This is an IT security role covering identity, device management and internal telemetry, with a real build component. It sits in security rather than IT because the work is judged on risk rather than on service.

The role is both preventive and reactive. Most of it is preventive: closing gaps before anyone else finds them, and building the visibility that shows you where they are. But when a security event happens, you are part of the response, and security events do not keep office hours. This is not a shift pattern or a formal on-call rotation, and it is not frequent.

### **Objectives - The problems you will solve**

In your first 1 month:

* You have a complete inventory of our tools and of how access to each one is granted and removed.
* You know which accounts exist across those tools and which of them map to a real person.
* You run onboarding, offboarding and access requests independently, without escalation.
* You have given us your first read on the environment: the three or four things you would fix first, why each one matters, and what it would take.

After 3 months:

* You have a view of the *security* settings in each cloud/SaaS tool we use, what each is capable of enforcing, and what it currently enforces.
* You have recommended the changes worth making in priority order, and the first of them are already applied.
* You have produced the plan and the recommendation for the new endpoint management and protection: the options, the obstacles we will hit, and how you would get past them.

After 6 months:

* New endpoint management and protection are running across the fleet and you can report coverage.
* There is one place that shows who has access to what across all tools, and access reviews run from it and produce the evidence export.
* The new Security Dashboard is built to the point where a real investigation can be done in it.

### **What you need to be great at:**

* Working across multiple areas of security rather than specialising in one, in combination with “standard IT activities”. Identity, endpoints, tool configuration and logging all sit in this role, and none of them get a dedicated person.
* Judging the balance between security that limits people and what the business actually needs to get done. Knowing which control is worth the friction and which one will simply be worked around.
* Because of our business, users often need immediate action. Some tickets can wait a week and some arrive as a Slack message because a customer event is happening now. Judging which is which, without treating everything as urgent or making people escalate to get attention, is a daily call.
* Google Workspace as an identity platform, including SSO and SAML app integration, groups and org units, admin roles and delegation, context-aware access, the security and admin audit logs and the alerts built on them
* Understanding the usage of APIs, minimally knowledge around REST and HTTP methods status codes, authentication via API keys, OAuth 2.0

### **What we are most curious about:**

* How you decide between buying and building, what you base it on, and how the decision survives in real life.
* Where you think the effort really belongs when it comes to security settings and capabilities, and which attack vectors matter most for a company like ours.
* Your process for choosing security tools, what you rule out early, and what you insist on testing before anything gets signed.
* How you adapt your views and actions based on publicly known security incidents and breaches.
* How you handle the human pressure to override security requirements.
* A detection or an alert you switched off, and what convinced you.

*SpotMe recruits, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, parental status, or veteran status.*

## **Our mission: e**liminating every barrier to mental health.

Our AI-native platform helps us deliver personalized support across self-guided tools, coaching, therapy, medication management, and specialty care. As an AI-native company, we believe technology should expand the reach, quality, and humanity of care. Every Spring Health team member is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully, apply human judgment to AI outputs, and keep building AI fluency in ways that support their role and our mission.

The CX Tooling Engineer will design, build, and operate the systems that power Spring Health’s customer experience and support operations at scale.

This role sits within Technology in the Care Division’s Engineering Department and supports production systems across Zendesk, Zendesk Contact Center built on Amazon Connect, Tray.ai, Talkdesk, Decagon and approved operational AI integrations. You will combine platform configuration, workflow automation, systems integration, and technical problem-solving to improve reliability, reduce manual work, and create durable solutions for teams operating in a regulated environment.

You will work closely with Operations, Product, Engineering, Data, Security, Legal, Compliance, and external implementation partners to translate business needs into scalable technical solutions.

This is a full-time, remote position reporting to the Senior Manager of Tooling Management. No regular travel is required; occasional travel for team and company onsites may be requested.

## **What you’ll do**

* Design, configure, test, and maintain Zendesk architecture and extensibility, including forms, fields, triggers, automations, service-level agreements, skills, queues, views, permissions, applications, routing logic, custom data structures, integrations, and workflow automation.
* Build and operate contact-center infrastructure using Zendesk Contact Center and Amazon Connect, including contact flows, queues, routing profiles, phone numbers, recording, voicemail, after-hours behavior, overflow, crisis routing, and escalation paths.
* Design, build, and maintain cross-system workflows in Tray.ai using APIs, webhooks, authentication, conditional logic, data transformation, document-processing services, and controlled system writeback.
* Support approved AI-enabled chat, voice, email, and agent-assist workflows by implementing eligibility rules, intent capture, verification, ticket creation, escalation, human handoff, fallback behavior, access controls, data-minimization or redaction controls where required, auditability, and operational safeguards.

* Monitor platform and workflow health, investigate routing defects, hidden or stale work, status conflicts, integration failures, and reporting gaps, and use operational data and root-cause analysis to implement durable corrective actions.
* Build scalable tooling, permissions, routing, integrations, and service-transition controls that support global launches, specialized teams, outsourced support partners, and round-the-clock operations, replacing brittle or duplicative configurations with standardized and reusable patterns where practical.
* Support centralized tooling intake and partner with Product, Engineering, Data, Security, Legal, Compliance, and operational stakeholders to clarify business impact, translate requests into technical requirements, identify dependencies and risks, estimate effort, define acceptance criteria, and validate outcomes.
* Coordinate with platform vendors and implementation partners on technical requirements, sequencing, dependencies, testing, issue escalation, and delivery quality, while communicating technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
* Deliver production changes with appropriate testing, monitoring, logging, alerting, validation, rollback, and recovery procedures, and maintain architecture diagrams, workflow inventories, test plans, change records, release communications, runbooks, and platform standards.

* Assigned routing, telephony, automation, and integration workflows consistently meet established reliability and successful-execution targets.
* Platform enhancements are delivered against agreed scope, acceptance criteria, testing requirements, and delivery expectations, with risks and dependencies raised early.
* Routing defects, silent failures, stale work, and recurring configuration issues decline from established baselines through monitoring, root-cause remediation, and reusable solutions.
* Eligible repeatable work is increasingly handled through automation or standardized platform patterns, with reductions in manual effort measured.
* AI-enabled workflows demonstrate reliable eligibility, escalation, human-handoff, and fallback behavior within approved use cases.
* Tooling improvements contribute to measurable gains in routing accuracy, first-reply time, resolution time, support capacity, platform reliability, or cost per interaction.
* Material production changes include documented testing, monitoring, ownership, validation, rollback, and recovery procedures.

## **What you’ll bring**

* 3+ years of experience administering, engineering, or operating customer experience, contact-center, workflow, automation, and integration platforms in a production environment.
* Hands-on experience with Zendesk configuration and architecture, including business rules, forms, fields, routing, permissions, applications, integrations, or comparable platform capabilities.
* Experience with an enterprise contact-center platform such as Amazon Connect, Zendesk Contact Center, Talkdesk, Genesys Cloud, Five9, Twilio Flex, or a comparable platform.
* Experience configuring interactive voice response or contact flows, queues, routing logic, phone numbers, recording, voicemail, overflow, after-hours, or escalation behavior.
* Working knowledge of REST APIs, webhooks, JSON, authentication, data transformation, and API-testing tools.
* Experience building or maintaining production workflows using an integration, automation, or orchestration platform such as Tray.ai, Workato, or a comparable platform.
* Experience troubleshooting production issues and identifying underlying technical or process causes.
* Understanding of monitoring, error handling, retry behavior, fallback design, recovery procedures, and production change management.
* Ability to translate operational needs into clear technical requirements and maintainable solutions.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and communication with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
* Ability to independently manage assigned work, make progress through ambiguity, and raise risks or dependencies early.
* Sound judgment regarding platform governance, standardization, access controls, and the maintenance impact of technical decisions.

## **Nice to Have**

* Experience with advanced Zendesk development and extensibility capabilities such as the Zendesk Apps Framework (ZAF), custom objects, events and profiles, custom actions or action flows, Zendesk Copilot, intelligent triage, custom agents or procedures, or comparable platform capabilities.
* Experience with Tray.ai, Workato or another enterprise integration and orchestration platform.
* Experience integrating AI-enabled support platforms, conversational AI tools, or large language model services, such as Decagon, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Zendesk AI/Copilot, or comparable technologies into operational workflows.
* Experience supporting contact-center infrastructure across multiple countries, outsourced support teams, or round-the-clock operations.
* Familiarity with call-recording consent, privacy, retention, data residency, accessibility, or regional telecommunications requirements.
* Experience with DocuSign, document processing, fax automation, customer relationship management integrations, or similar operational systems.
* Experience working in healthcare, financial services, insurance, or another regulated environment.
* Familiarity with infrastructure as code, automated testing, structured deployment practices, or configuration version control.
* Experience with incident response, root-cause analysis, production observability, or reliability engineering practices.

We are seeking a highly experienced **Senior Investment Grade Portfolio Manager** to join our Public Markets team. This senior front-office role will manage a substantial annuity-backed credit portfolio, combining portfolio construction, dynamic risk management and direct transaction execution across global fixed income markets.

The successful candidate will bring extensive experience managing **investment-grade credit portfolios**, combined with deep expertise across **fixed income markets**, including financial and corporate bonds, government debt, private placements and structured credit. Equally important is a very strong understanding of **insurance asset management**, including the application of **Solvency II**, **UK Matching Adjustment** requirements and balance sheet optimisation within annuity portfolios.

Working closely with colleagues across Investments, ALM, Research, Strategy and PRT Origination, you will play a pivotal role in portfolio management, investment decision-making and transaction execution, helping to support the continued growth of one of the UK's leading retirement businesses.

**The Public Markets Team**

The Public Markets team is responsible for the management, optimisation and risk oversight of Standard Life's annuity-backed Public Credit portfolio.

Managing a globally diversified Investment Grade portfolio, the team focuses on credit portfolio construction, Solvency II optimisation, balance sheet efficiency and long-term risk-adjusted performance. The team plays a central role in supporting PRT transactions through asset pricing, portfolio construction, investment execution and ongoing portfolio management.

Working in partnership with colleagues across Private Markets, Macro Markets, Asset Liability Management (ALM), Research, Strategy and PRT Origination, the team contributes throughout the full lifecycle of a transaction, while also maintaining key relationships with banking counterparties and external asset management partners.

**The Opportunity**

As Senior Investment Grade Portfolio Manager, you will be responsible for portfolio management and trading activity across the team's mandate, investing across multiple legal entities and supporting both direct and indirect origination channels, including our recently launched Standard Life PRT Solutions platform.

This role combines portfolio management, credit investing and trading expertise with a strong understanding of insurance balance sheet management. You'll be responsible for delivering investment performance, managing risk, identifying value-accretive trading opportunities and supporting portfolio optimisation across a complex annuity-backed investment portfolios.

For experienced investment professionals with a background in fixed income portfolio management, investment-grade credit and insurance asset management, this represents an opportunity to influence investment strategy at scale within a growing, market-leading retirement business.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Portfolio Management & Investment Decision Making**

* Own portfolio management, investment and trading decisions within agreed mandates and governance frameworks, from idea generation and investment decision-making through to market execution.
* Manage investment-grade credit exposures across financial and corporate sectors, principally within GBP, EUR and USD markets, including specialist asset classes managed in collaboration with external asset managers, including US Municipals and Emerging Markets strategies.
* Deliver recurring trading benefits through a Solvency II balance sheet lens, generating value-accretive investment ideas and proactive credit risk management across annuity portfolios.
* Drive portfolio construction, optimisation and risk management activity across Standard Life's investment grade credit portfolios.

**Pension Risk Transfer & Strategic Portfolio Construction**

* Support portfolio construction and optimisation activities throughout the lifecycle of PRT transactions, incl. maintaining robust, accurate and efficient asset-pricing capabilities supporting origination.
* Work closely with colleagues across Public Markets, Private Markets, Macro Markets, ALM, Research, Strategy and PRT Origination teams from pricing and portfolio construction through to execution, private asset deployment and ongoing back-book management.

**Market Execution & Partner Relationships**

* Build and maintain strong relationships with bank counterparties, including syndicate, debt capital markets, sales and trading teams.
* Partner effectively with external asset managers and evaluate investment opportunities across specialist credit strategies.

**Governance, Conduct & Risk**

* Promote high standards of conduct, control awareness and operational discipline.
* Ensure investment and trading activity is undertaken within agreed governance frameworks, risk limits and internal protocols.
* Communicate investment views, portfolio risks and market opportunities effectively through governance forums, committees and senior stakeholder discussions.

**Overview**  
  

The Measurement Lead will own and drive the measurement agenda across assigned Kellanova segments, brands and markets, ensuring that measurement is not just reported, but actively used to improve marketing effectiveness, investment decisions and learning maturity.

This role sits at the intersection of analytics, media strategy, data governance, experimentation and client leadership. It requires someone who can connect technical measurement outputs — including MMM, causal analysis, geo-lift testing, incrementality studies, dashboards and campaign measurement — with the practical needs of planners, strategists, channel teams and senior Kellanova stakeholders.

The Measurement Lead will be accountable for setting measurement direction, identifying gaps, shaping testing roadmaps, overseeing the use of MMM and experimentation outputs, improving data quality, and ensuring recommendations are translated into clear actions that influence planning and budget decisions.

**1. Measurement Strategy & Leadership**

* Lead the development and implementation of measurement strategies across assigned Kellanova segments, brands and markets.
* Translate high-level business, brand and media objectives into clear KPI frameworks, learning agendas and measurement plans.
* Partner with strategy, planning, channel, data, reporting and global measurement teams to ensure measurement is embedded throughout the planning and activation process.
* Act as the senior measurement partner for internal teams and Kellanova stakeholders, ensuring work is commercially relevant, analytically robust and clearly connected to business decision-making.
* Identify measurement gaps across markets, brands, channels and reporting processes, and shape practical solutions to improve measurement maturity over time.

**2. Test & Learn / Experimentation Ownership**

* Own the Test & Learn roadmap across assigned areas, ensuring experiments are strategically prioritised and designed to answer meaningful business questions.
* Oversee the design and execution of incrementality tests, including geo-lift tests, randomised control trials and other causal measurement approaches.
* Ensure test proposals are supported by appropriate pre-test analysis, including sufficiency checks, budget requirements, reach assumptions, regional considerations, exclusions and success metrics.
* Monitor live tests to ensure they remain on track, escalating risks around feasibility, delivery, data availability or statistical confidence.
* Translate test outcomes into simple, actionable recommendations that inform future planning, channel strategy and investment decisions.

**3. MMM, Econometrics & Investment Effectiveness**

* Lead the interpretation and application of Media Mix Modelling outputs, ensuring MMM is used to guide planning, optimisation and budget allocation decisions.
* Help teams understand and apply response curves, saturation points, marginal ROI, average ROI, diminishing returns and channel interdependencies.
* Challenge simplistic interpretations of MMM outputs where needed, ensuring recommendations consider short-term performance, long-term demand generation, brand effects and practical media constraints.
* Partner with modelling, data science and analytics teams to improve the usability and relevance of MMM outputs across markets and brands.
* Connect MMM findings with experimentation, campaign measurement and market context to build a more rounded view of marketing effectiveness.

**4. Data Quality, Governance & Reporting Readiness**

* Lead the measurement data agenda, working with data, tech, reporting and activation teams to improve the completeness, consistency and usability of media and performance data.
* Work with teams to identify and resolve data quality issues that could impact MMM, campaign reporting, dashboards or test validity.
* Support the transition from manual data processes towards more automated, standardised and scalable measurement workflows.

**5. Stakeholder Management & Client Influence**

* Confidently lead senior stakeholder conversations on measurement approach, test feasibility, data quality, MMM interpretation and investment implications.
* Build trusted relationships with Kellanova stakeholders, Publicis capability teams, regional leads and channel specialists.
* Manage competing priorities across multiple workstreams, ensuring stakeholders are aligned on what matters most and where measurement effort should be focused.

**6. Operating Model, Enablement & Team Leadership**

* Define ways of working for measurement across assigned brands, markets or segments, ensuring roles, responsibilities, decision points and handoffs are clear.
* Create and maintain practical measurement guidance, templates, playbooks, QA processes and stakeholder-facing materials.
* Support and coach measurement managers, analysts or cross-functional team members to improve analytical quality, strategic thinking and communication.

**Required Experience**

* Significant experience working directly with senior clients and internal stakeholders in a complex, multi-market or matrixed environment.
* Proven ability to lead measurement strategy across multiple workstreams, brands, markets or business units.
* Experience interpreting and applying MMM, experimentation and campaign measurement outputs to support real business decisions.
* Demonstrable experience improving measurement processes, data quality, reporting standards, testing roadmaps or analytical ways of working.

This is a Principal role with real team leadership attached, and it stays technical. You will stay hands on: reviewing architecture, reading and writing code, and joining incidents. The role moves between deep technical detail and a 10,000 foot view, often on the same day.

## **What You'll Be Working On**

##### **Reliability, observability and operational correctness**

The priority is not simply whether the platform is up, but whether it is doing its job: client feeds arrive completely, surveillance runs against the right window and expected alerts fire.

You and the team will establish patterns for correctness monitoring, escalation, incident response and disaster recovery, allowing product teams to define their own alerts, service levels and response playbooks

##### **Software craftsmanship and change safety**

Alongside correctness, change safety is our other top engineering priority: the ability to change the platform frequently, in small increments, with confidence that nothing has quietly broken. That means tests that earn trust, reviews that catch design problems rather than typos, deployment that is boring, and the discipline to keep it that way under pressure.

You will own the standard of engineering craft across Surveillance: what good looks like, how it is taught, and whether it holds when nobody is watching.

##### **Architectural coherence**

Each team will make sensible local decisions. Your job is to make sure they add up: that we are not solving the same problem three ways, that the interfaces between domains are deliberate, and that the estate can still be reasoned about in two years.

You will set the technical direction others plan against, including how client environments are managed across their lifecycle and how software reaches production through GitOps and infrastructure as code.

##### **Security architecture**

Not governance, which sits with our Security team, but the engineering picture: how client environment isolation actually works, where the boundaries are, how privileged access is granted and removed, and which risks we have consciously accepted. This includes workload identity, SCIM 2.0 and enterprise identity integration for client provisioning.

Individual teams will secure their own patch. Somebody has to own how it fits together.

##### **Growing the Staff Engineers**

You will manage our Staff Engineers. That means growing their scope rather than directing their work: helping them take on problems larger than a single team, raising the standard of design review and technical writing, and building a bench that does not route through you.

##### **Cost and unit economics**

Cloud cost grows as we add new clients, so it needs to be an engineering concern.

You will work with the teams building our products and our FinOps engineering effort to improve optimisation, capacity strategy and client-level cost visibility. Cost is a shared responsibility, not something owned in isolation**.**

##### **Enterprise client assurance and commercial support**

You will help turn technical assurance around areas such as environment segregation, promotion controls, change management, data residency and disaster recovery into repeatable capabilities rather than bespoke exercises.

You will also review deals for technical risk and represent our architecture with client CISOs and technical stakeholders.

##### **Two boundaries**

Security policy, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification, the security risk register and the compliance programme are owned by our Security team.

You own the engineering controls and technical evidence they depend on, working closely with Security rather than running a compliance function.

Delivery is owned by the teams building our products. You own whether it coheres. Neither boundary makes you an approval gate.

## **What success looks like**

The technical direction is already established. You will inherit goals in flight and formulate plans to deliver the desired outcomes.

We want someone who can get close to the estate and team quickly, build on what is working and move at pace rather than returning to first principles.

Success means teams can move safely and faster because of the platform and the standards, with less operational toil and a growing proportion of engineering time spent on elective work rather than keeping the lights on.

That means:

* Client onboarding becomes increasingly automated end to end.
* Observability lets teams answer common operational questions without elevated production access.
* Change is frequent, small and reversible, and incidents do not scale with deployment frequency.
* Product teams have better visibility into client-level cost and margin.
* Each area has clear ownership and no single person becomes a dependency, including you.
* Our Staff Engineers are operating at greater scope than when you arrived.

## **What You'll Bring To The Team**

You have depth somewhere real, and it does not have to be ours. We are not looking for a specialist in one layer. You might have built your reputation in distributed systems, data platforms, application and product engineering, machine learning, or platform and infrastructure. What matters is that somewhere in the stack you went deep enough to earn the respect of very good engineers, and that you can bring that judgement to areas where you are not the expert.

You have a track record of hands-on, material impact. Not architecture decks, and not delivery you delegated. Things you personally designed, built, or unblocked by getting into the detail, where the outcome mattered commercially and you can explain both the mechanism and the tradeoffs you accepted.

You have enough breadth to challenge a specialist. You will be accountable for areas where someone on your team knows more than you do. You should be able to ask the question that exposes the weak assumption, and to recognise when you are being told what you want to hear.

You have led senior engineers and know how to give strong people meaningful ownership rather than routing decisions through yourself. You can name engineers whose trajectory changed because of you.

You have raised the engineering standard of teams beyond your own. You have opinions about testing, review and change safety that you have actually implemented, and you can tell the difference between a team that has adopted the practices and one that has adopted the vocabulary.

You are comfortable working across distributed engineering centres, and you know that raising craft at distance happens through pairing and review rather than through standards documents.

You treat developer productivity as an engineering outcome rather than a side effect. You have measurably improved how quickly other engineers ship, through paved paths, faster feedback and removing the need to understand internals in order to work safely.

You understand security as engineering controls rather than process, including identity and access management, privileged access, workload identity and client environment isolation. You are comfortable working in environments where enterprise customers expect technical assurance and can hold your own with a client CISO.

You are equally comfortable moving between architecture, code, incidents, client conversations and commercial considerations.

We are particularly interested in people who came up through engineering and infrastructure before moving into platform and security leadership.

## **Our estate, for context**

AWS and Azure · Kubernetes and EKS · Terraform · Helm · GitOps · CI/CD · Elasticsearch · Kafka · PostgreSQL · ClickHouse · Python services · observability and Prometheus · multi-fleet, multi-cell client environment architecture · cloud and Kubernetes security

Nobody knows all of it well. You should recognise most of it and be genuinely deep in some of it.

## **How you work**

You think in systems, and you treat reliability, security and developer productivity as the same engineering problem rather than three competing ones. You prefer automated guardrails to manual approvals, paved paths to documentation and evidence to assertion.

You are credible in a board conversation and credible in a code review, and you do not treat those as different people.

You will work closely with other MLEs, software engineers and MLOps to bring models to production, and carry real ownership of the technical direction and accountable for its performance.

OverviewApplication

Tessl is a fast-growing Series A startup based in London, founded by Guy Podjarny, who previously founded Snyk. We’ve raised more than $100 million from world-class investors, including Index Ventures, Accel, GV and Boldstart. In 2025, Tessl ranked #2 in Sifted’s B2B SaaS Rising 100 and #20 in its AI 100.

We’re building the context layer for AI coding agents and a platform for AI-native software development. As an early member of the team, you’ll help shape how we build and scale a company operating at the forefront of AI and software development.

# Overview of Role

We're looking for a Developer Advocate to be Tessl's voice in the AI developer community — based in our London office and out in the world where developers actually are. Someone who lives and breathes agentic coding, builds real things with Tessl, and helps other developers do the same.

This is a hands-on, high-visibility role. You'll build with the product, create content people genuinely use, speak at events, and be a familiar face across the communities where AI development is being figured out in real time. You'd rather ship a slick integration or a creative app than just write about one.

A big part of this role is education. Alongside the community work, you'll help build and grow Tessl Academy — our home for learning AI native development. You'll turn what you know into structured, hands-on learning that scales beyond any single talk or tutorial, and takes developers from curious to genuinely capable with Tessl.

# Key Responsibilities

**Build with Tessl:** Go beyond writing about the product, build with it. Create apps, integrations, and creative projects using Tessl that inspire and enable the developer community to do the same.

**Teach through Tessl Academy:** Design and deliver structured learning, including courses, hands-on labs, guided projects, and certification paths, through Tessl Academy that take developers from their first agentic build to real fluency. Own the curriculum, keep it current as the product evolves, and pay attention to what actually helps people learn, not just what looks good on a syllabus.

**Content Creation:** Write articles, tutorials, and guides, and produce videos that give developers practical, actionable insights into AI native development with Tessl.

**Community and Events:** Be an active, visible presence in the AI developer community, speaking at events, participating in forums, engaging on social, and helping highlight what developers are building with Tessl.

**Ecosystem Exploration:** Constantly explore the AI developer tooling landscape, identifying integration opportunities and ways to connect Tessl with the broader ecosystem.

**Show Up Where Developers Are:** Run webinars, appear on podcasts, and make yourself at home in other people's communities. That means Discord servers, Slack groups, subreddits, newsletters, and anywhere else developers are gathering.

# What You'll Need

**Already in the conversation:** You're an active voice in the AI developer community, on social channels, where AI discussion is happening. You post, reply, spark discussions.

**Active at events:** You speak at meetups or conferences, engage in developer communities, and have a point of view worth hearing.

**A builder's mindset:** You get excited about making things. Whether that's a slick integration, a creative app, or an experiment that no one's tried yet, you'd rather ship something than just describe it.

**A teacher's instinct:** You can break a complex AI topic into clear, progressive steps that meet developers where they are, and you enjoy the craft of helping someone go from lost to confident.

**Strong communicator:** You can write clearly and engagingly about technical AI topics.

**Development skills:** You're comfortable enough with code to build and hack on things yourself. You don't need to be a full-time engineer, but you ship.

# Nice to Have

* Experience building developer education, including courses, curriculum, academies, bootcamps, or technical training
* Experience with open-source communities and contributor ecosystems

We care deeply about the warm, inclusive environment we’re building at Tessl and we value diversity – we welcome applications from those typically underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this role but are not totally sure whether you’re the right person, do apply anyway!

* **Costruire dal futuro:** Creiamo oggi ciò che verrà domani.

* Lavora attraverso una coda prioritaria di lead valutati in base al profilo e all'intenzione, stabilendo il primo contatto principalmente per telefono, utilizzando email e social media come canali supplementari.
* Qualifica ogni lead rispetto a una serie chiara di criteri: questa azienda rientra nel profilo giusto ed è il momento giusto per parlare?
* Pianifica gli incontri con i commercianti qualificati direttamente sul calendario di un rappresentante di Vendite sul Campo (*Field Sales*) con almeno 48 ore di preavviso, garantendo la partecipazione tramite una conferma e un promemoria il giorno prima.
* Segnala i lead che mostrano potenziale ma che devono essere contattati in un momento più appropriato.
* Chiudi i lead che non rientrano nel profilo adeguato, registrando una motivazione chiara e onesta.
* Mantieni il CRM organizzato: registri accurati, note chiare e stati aggiornati. La persona successiva nel processo dipende dalle informazioni che registri.

* Disinvoltura al telefono e capacità di intrattenere una conversazione approfondita e utile con il titolare di un'azienda che non si aspettava la tua chiamata.
* La capacità di ascoltare più che presentare, riconoscendo la differenza tra una vera opportunità e un semplice "forse".
* Organizzazione e costanza: gestisci la lista, effettui i follow-up puntualmente e mantieni i tuoi registri aggiornati.
* La capacità di gestire un "no" con naturalezza e di mantenere un'energia costante per un'intera giornata di chiamate.
* Padronanza nell'uso di un CRM e di strumenti di vendita moderni, o la capacità di imparare rapidamente a usare nuovi strumenti.
* Fluenza nella lingua Italiana.

## Cosa sarà apprezzato:

* Esperienza nello sviluppo delle vendite o in un altro ruolo commerciale orientato agli obiettivi con una forte componente telefonica.
* L'esperienza nel settore fintech o nella vendita di soluzioni di pagamento costituirà un vantaggio.
* Esperienza con un CRM.

* Incontri qualificati fissati e, soprattutto, incontri tenuti e riconosciuti dal venditore come opportunità rilevanti.
* Qualità della qualificazione: le opportunità che passi al team si trasformano in veri colloqui di affari, piuttosto che in incontri senza potenziale.
* Un flusso costante e affidabile di lead ben qualificati, settimana dopo settimana.

## Perché unirti a Teya?:

* Il ruolo di SDR è il banco di prova in cui si forgiano i grandi venditori. Imparerai il mercato, il prodotto e l'arte della qualificazione fin dal primo giorno, mantenendo il riconoscimento per il tuo contributo a ogni accordo che contribuisci ad avviare.
* Gli SDR con le prestazioni migliori hanno l'opportunità di passare a ruoli di *Field Sales*, assumendo progressivamente maggiore responsabilità nel processo di vendita.
* L'operatività è progettata per aiutarti a raggiungere il successo. I lead arrivano già identificati, arricchiti e valutati, permettendoti di concentrare i tuoi sforzi sulle conversazioni che contano davvero, invece di perdere tempo a cercare dati.
* Avrai a disposizione un quadro di qualificazione chiaro, strumenti moderni e un team che valuta il tuo lavoro in base alla qualità delle opportunità che crei, anziché solo sul volume dei contatti effettuati.

* Stipendio base lordo competitivo di €20.000 + commissioni.
* Contratto a tempo determinato.
* Welfare aziendale (142 € netti al mese).
* Buoni pasto da 8 € netti al giorno con Coverflex.
* 25 giorni di ferie annuali (oltre alle festività locali).
* Lavora con alcune delle migliori menti del settore che stanno cambiando il volto del Fintech in Italia!

Pronto a essere il volto della rivoluzione Fintech in Italia? Se hai la grinta per vendere e la passione per il servizio, vogliamo costruire il futuro insieme a te. Facciamo la differenza, insieme!

Teya è orgogliosa di essere un datore di lavoro che offre pari opportunità.

Ci impegniamo a creare un ambiente inclusivo in cui chiunque, indipendentemente da razza, etnia, identità o espressione di genere, orientamento sessuale, età, disabilità, religione o background, possa prosperare e dare il meglio di sé. # Tech Lead

Full-time | Engineering | London

## Job Description

**We’re on a mission to protect society from fraud and money laundering.** We’ve already protected over 3 million people through life’s big transactions.

Fraud and regulation are rising, costing the UK economy over £100bn every year; this makes it more difficult for businesses to protect themselves and their clients - individuals like you and me - from fraud and money laundering.

Our co-founders Olly and Jack were led to this area when a friend was defrauded of £25K when buying their first property. At the time, anti-fraud technology didn’t exist, which meant that completing the anti-fraud checks required in these processes was largely manual. These big life moments should be exciting, but instead are often confusing and scary due to the painful process of completing these paper-based checks and the risk of fraud.

Thirdfort helps businesses to facilitate these anti fraud checks so that individuals know they can transact safely and seamlessly with professionals during these big transactions. Our anti-fraud platform provides a secure way for professionals in regulated sectors like Lawyers, Estate Agents and Accountants to transfer funds and verify sensitive information through app based document checks, facial recognition and open banking.

Over 1,500 businesses now trust Thirdfort to verify their clients. We are FCA regulated and have raised over \$33m in capital from leading Fintech investors Breega and Element Ventures, as well as the founders of Zoopla, Funding Circle, Comply Advantage, Tessian, Fenergo and Fidel.

### About the role:

We’re looking for a **Tech Lead (IC4)** to join one of our product teams and provide strong technical leadership.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys **solving complex problems**, owning technical direction within a domain, and helping other engineers grow through mentorship and example. You will play a key role in shaping how we design, build, and evolve our systems, while working closely with Product, Design, and other engineering leaders.

You won’t be responsible for line management, but you will be expected to **set direction, raise standards, and take ownership** of the technical outcomes for your area.  
  
For this role, we'd love this person to be able to join us in our London office 2 days per week, being together as a team is valuable for us, especially at this stage of growth.

### About the team:

Our engineering teams are **cross-functional product teams**, made up of engineers with different specialisms working closely with Product Managers, Designers and stakeholders across the business.

We focus on delivering value iteratively while maintaining a high bar for quality, security and reliability. Our ways of working continue to evolve - blending elements of Scrum, Shape Up and continuous delivery and we expect senior engineers to actively influence and improve how we operate.

## As a Tech Lead, you will:

- Provide technical leadership within your team and domain, guiding design decisions and architectural direction.
- Design, build and deliver complex features and systems that are secure, scalable and maintainable.
- Own technical outcomes end-to-end, from discovery and design through to delivery and long-term operation.
- Lead by example in AI-assisted software engineering, using AI to accelerate delivery while maintaining strong engineering judgement and accountability for the resulting software.
- Help the team continuously improve its AI-enabled development practices and identify opportunities to automate repetitive engineering work.
- Represent Engineering at an organisational level, partnering with stakeholders across Product, Sales, Marketing, Support, Operations, Legal and Compliance to shape decisions, manage trade-offs and drive successful technical outcomes.
- Mentor and coach engineers across the team, supporting their technical growth and confidence.
- Set a high bar for code quality, testing, observability and operational excellence.
- Collaborate closely with Product and Design to shape solutions, challenge assumptions and manage trade-offs.
- Lead technical discussions, reviews and incident investigations, helping the team learn and improve.
- Contribute to wider engineering initiatives and influence standards across the technology organisation.

## We’d love to hear from you if:

- You actively use AI-assisted engineering tools in your development workflow and can demonstrate how they have improved the way you design, build, test or maintain software.
- You have significant experience building and operating production software in a modern engineering environment.
- You’ve led technical design and delivery for complex systems or domains.
- You’re comfortable working across backend and frontend systems (for example Go, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python).
- You have strong knowledge of APIs, data modelling, testing strategies and system design.
- You enjoy mentoring other engineers and leading through influence rather than authority.
- You can communicate complex technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- You’re comfortable working in a fast-moving, regulated environment where quality and trust are critical.

## We use and teach:

We’re passionate about supporting your growth and giving you opportunities to work across the stack. Depending on the team, you’ll work with and help shape:

- Go for backend services
- TypeScript and React for web applications
- React Native for mobile applications
- Temporal for workflow orchestration
- PostgreSQL for relational data
- GCP for infrastructure, monitoring and analytics
- AI-assisted engineering tools and coding agents to help us design, build, test, review and maintain software more effectively.

We've created our benefits package to reflect Thirdfort's mission and values. Everything we do is designed to **build on trust**, and we extend this promise to our team by investing in their physical, mental, and financial security to support them through life's big moments. Ultimately, our benefits exist to empower our people, ensuring everyone feels deeply supported, trusted, and equipped to do their best work.
