About Unifeye
Unifeye is a delivery-led, Databricks-first consultancy helping organisations unlock the full value of their data and AI.

We’re a lean, high-growth team based in London, working at the intersection of data, technology and business strategy. We partner with enterprise organisations across industries to solve complex data challenges through modern Lakehouse architectures and AI solutions built on Databricks.

Joining Unifeye means more than delivering projects. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, challenge conventional thinking and make a genuine impact. With a high degree of autonomy, you’ll help shape client outcomes, influence our analytics capability and play a key role in the growth of the business.

The Role
We’re looking for an experienced Senior Data Analyst to join our growing team and help enterprise clients turn their data into insight that senior stakeholders genuinely act on.
This is a consulting role as much as an analytics one. You’ll work directly with business stakeholders to understand the decisions they’re trying to make, shape the reporting that supports them, and build it yourself in Power BI, Tableau and Databricks. Where many analysts execute a plan someone else has written, we’re looking for someone who can walk into the room, work out what the business actually needs to see, and then design the best way to show it.

Alongside client delivery, you’ll contribute to the continued growth of Unifeye’s BI and analytics capability by sharing knowledge, mentoring colleagues and helping shape our reporting standards and reusable assets.

What You’ll Do
Design, build and deliver dashboards and reporting products using Power BI, Tableau and Databricks AI/BI.
Partner directly with business stakeholders to understand their objectives and translate them into clear, decision-focused reporting.
Run discovery sessions, requirements workshops and solution design conversations with client teams.
Define and agree metrics, measures and reporting models that stakeholders trust and adopt.
Rationalise fragmented reporting estates into a curated set of reports that get used and maintained.
Present insight to senior and executive audiences in a way that drives action, not just awareness.
Collaborate closely with Data Engineers, Architects and client stakeholders to deliver high-quality analytics solutions.
Contribute to the development of Unifeye’s internal BI capability, reusable assets, templates and delivery standards.
Stay up to date with the evolving Databricks analytics and AI/BI toolset and help shape the future direction of our analytics offering.

What We’re Looking For
Essential
Previous consultancy or customer-facing delivery experience, you are a consultant first and an analyst second.
Strong commercial experience designing and building dashboards and reports in Power BI and/or Tableau, including data modelling and DAX or equivalent.
Strong SQL and confidence working with complex, imperfect data.
Proven ability to translate business requirements into defined metrics, reporting models and clear visual outputs.
A strong visual and editorial instinct, you have a view on what makes a dashboard genuinely usable, and can explain it.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including with senior and executive audiences.
Comfortable working within a fast-paced, collaborative consultancy environment.
Desirable
Experience working with Databricks, including Databricks SQL and AI/BI dashboards.
A background in management consultancy or a specialist data practice.
Experience in public sector, higher education or other regulated environments.
Exposure to data governance, data quality or migration workstreams.
Databricks certification.

Why Join Unifeye?
We’re building a consultancy where talented people can do their best work.
At Unifeye, you’ll have the opportunity to solve meaningful analytics challenges, work with leading enterprise organisations and collaborate with some of the UK’s most experienced Databricks specialists. As a high-growth business, you’ll have the autonomy to make decisions, influence how we work and help shape the future of our analytics practice.

We offer:
The opportunity to build enterprise analytics and reporting solutions on the Databricks Lakehouse Platform.
High levels of ownership and autonomy from day one.
The chance to make a real impact on clients and the growth of the business.
The opportunity to learn directly from our Chief Data Officer, a Databricks MVP, alongside our experienced architecture team.
Exposure to a wide variety of enterprise analytics, BI and data transformation programmes.
Continuous learning, Databricks certification and career development.
Competitive salary, bonus, generous benefits and flexible remote-first working with occasional travel to our London office and client sites.

If you’re passionate about turning data into insight people actually act on, enjoy working directly with clients and want to help shape a fast-growing consultancy, we’d love to hear from you.

# **About Vantage**

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

## **Product Department**

The Product team at Vantage defines and stewards our global product platform: the customer outcomes we aim to deliver, the standards and reference approaches that make delivery repeatable, and the closed-loop learning that turns each deployment into an upgrade for the next. We do this in partnership with Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, Sales, Site Selection, and Business Development, aligning priorities and trade-offs while preserving clear functional ownership for design execution, construction delivery, and site operations.

## **Position Overview**

Vantage is building a repeatable, product-led approach to delivering hyperscale infrastructure and operating data centers on a global scale. We are hiring a Senior Manager, Product Performance Benchmarking to establish and evolve the product performance benchmarking capability at the heart of that approach. The benchmarking engine is the governed reference for our products across the full lifecycle, regions, and customer configurations, and will sit behind pricing, RFP responses, and executive reporting for a growing global portfolio.

It evaluates the expected schedule, cost, and sustainability of our products across design, delivery, and operations: how long they should take to build, and what they should cost to build and to run.

This is a senior individual contributor role expected to grow into team leadership for someone who combines deep benchmarking, estimating, preconstruction, and project controls experience with the commercial judgement to lead methodology, challenge conventions, and turn data into decisions. You will define what the benchmark should answer, how it is governed, how it is used in decisions, and how internal and external inputs become a durable capability.

## **What You Will Own**

You will build the product performance intelligence capability behind Vantage’s global data center platform. This is not a reporting role. It is a chance to define how one of the fastest-scaling infrastructure companies measures cost, schedule, sustainability, lifecycle performance, and value realization across regions, product configurations, and customer requirements.

The benchmark you build will shape real decisions: how products are configured, how products translate into cost, schedule, and sustainability impacts, how trade-offs are made, where performance is improving, and where the business needs to change. You will work at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, Procurement, Sustainability, and Analytics, with visibility to senior leaders and direct influence over how Vantage becomes more repeatable, data-driven, and product-led.

## **What You Will Do**

* Define the governed benchmarking methodology, baseline assumptions, performance measures, and usage rules Vantage applies globally to configure, cost, schedule, approve, manage, and measure project performance across Product, Engineering, Delivery, Operations, and Sustainability.
* Own the benchmark roadmap across platform, product, regional baselines, configurations, and future product extensions.
* Translate Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability requirements into benchmark scope.
* Lead consultant engagement, reviewing methodology, assumptions, confidence bands, and deliverables.
* Own the WBS/CBS and schedule structure from a product, business-adoption, and use perspective.
* Govern baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic.
* Partner with key stakeholders to incorporate market intelligence, supplier input, and realized cost factors into benchmark updates where appropriate.
* Define target audiences, provide business interpretation, and set reporting requirements for benchmark outputs to senior stakeholders, while partnering with analytics roles on dashboard build and data automation.
* Decide when benchmark outputs are fit for use in RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product decisions, and executive reporting.
* Own what decisions the benchmark enables and state clearly where confidence is insufficient.

## **What Success Looks Like**

* A governed product performance benchmark model exists that connects capital cost, schedule, sustainability and operational cost (energy, efficiency, maintainability) into a single governed reference with explicit methodology, confidence bands, and stated limits.
* Standardized KPIs and performance criteria are set, with the ability to reliably compare projects across approved variants, regions, and product versions from pre-construction through operations.
* Benchmark outputs are used in real decisions — RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, product trade-offs, and executive reporting — under clear fitness-for-use rules.
* The WBS/CBS and schedule structures are adopted by Product, Procurement, Preconstruction, Project Controls, and Sustainability, and held under company change control.
* Baseline, regional variant, configuration bridge, and factor-pack logic is coherent and current, with refresh cycles running on a disciplined cadence.
* Benchmarking exists as a durable internal capability that gets better with data from each delivery project. Results inform enhancements to products, variants, and project delivery to continuously improve.
* Methodology, models, and refresh are owned in-house, with external inputs from consultants, market data, and suppliers integrated deliberately rather than relied upon by default.
* Senior stakeholders receive interpretation, not just numbers: what moved, why, and what decision it supports.

## **What We Are Looking For**

* Benchmarking and cost intelligence: 8–12 years in cost management, quantity surveying, preconstruction, owner’s representative, project controls, infrastructure benchmarking, or equivalent capital-project performance role. Exceptional candidates with fewer years of experience may be considered.
* Capital project modeling: Demonstrated experience building or governing cost, schedule, or TCO models for complex capital programs, including unit rates, quantities, escalation, regional factors, configuration deltas, and confidence ranges.
* Lifecycle performance orientation: Ability to connect capital cost, schedule, energy, operational cost, maintainability, and sustainability factors into a decision-ready view of product performance.
* Continuous learning: Experience comparing benchmarks to actual delivery outcomes and translating variance into actionable recommendations for design, procurement, delivery, or product roadmap decisions.
* Commercial decision support: Proven ability to use benchmarking outputs to inform RFPs, ROM business cases, customer discussions, pricing, procurement strategy, or executive trade-off decisions.
* Governance and adoption: Experience establishing standards, methodologies, or controls that multiple functions or regions were expected to adopt.
* Consultant and stakeholder leadership: Credibility to challenge external consultants, internal customers, and senior stakeholders on assumptions, methodology, and fitness for use.
* Data partnership: Working knowledge of structured data, reporting requirements, dashboards, or analytics workflows, with ability to partner with data teams without needing to personally own BI engineering.
* Communication: Ability to explain assumptions, movement, confidence levels, limits, and recommended decisions clearly to technical, commercial, and executive audiences.

### **Preferred**

* Experience with capital projects, construction, infrastructure, data centers, utilities, natural resources, or other mission critical domains, particularly in estimating, cost control, or owner’s representative environments.
* Experience building a benchmarking or cost-intelligence capability from scratch, not just operating an established PMO or cost function.
* Track record integrating operational and energy costs into capital benchmarking.
* Experience influencing pricing, bid, or investment decisions with benchmark data at executive levels.
* Experience using early design studies, spatial test fits, and configuration comparisons to quantify how site, layout, product, or customer-driven choices affect benchmarked cost, schedule, and lifecycle performance.
* Exposure to structured data environments, cost databases, estimating platforms, project controls, and BI tools; working alongside data teams to productize a model.
* Multi-region or global portfolio experience in procurement, supplier intelligence, benchmarking, or should-cost modeling including normalization of currency, tax/local conditions, regulations, and supply chain factors.
* Chartered status (for example MRICS) or equivalent professional standing.

**Staff Software Engineer – Identity Domain** 

 

**About Vectra AI**  

Vectra AI is transforming cybersecurity through AI-driven threat detection and response. Our platform brings together network, identity, cloud, SaaS, and security telemetry to uncover attacker behaviour, identify risk, and help security teams investigate and respond before threats become breaches. 

Identity is changing rapidly. Alongside human users, organisations increasingly rely on AI agents, service accounts, workloads, applications, API tokens, and other non-human identities to access systems and act autonomously. These technologies create enormous opportunity, but also a rapidly expanding attack surface. 

Vectra’s Identity Domain is responsible for detecting and reducing identity-based risk across identity providers and SaaS environments, including human, machine, and non-human identities. 

 

**The Opportunity** 

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to provide technical leadership within Vectra AI’s Identity Domain, with particular expertise in the emerging security challenges created by AI agents, machine identities, and non-human identities (NHIs). 

This is a senior individual contributor role for an engineer who combines strong software engineering with deep curiosity about how customers build and operate modern identity systems. 

You will need to understand how AI agents are created, deployed, authenticated, permissioned, and connected to enterprise systems and translate that understanding into security capabilities that protect customers as this new attack surface evolves. 

The Identity team owns end-to-end delivery: from ingesting and normalising identity telemetry, through analytics and detection, to publishing detections and findings and making identity observability data available across the Vectra platform. 

You will lead complex engineering initiatives across that lifecycle, remain hands-on with architecture and code, and help teams make strong technical decisions while delivering reliable customer outcomes. 

  

**What You’ll Do**

* Work across team and service boundaries, partnering with Data Platform, Cloud Platform, Data Science, SRE and others

* Engage with Product, field teams, and customers to understand deployment patterns, security concerns, and emerging use cases

* Mentor engineers, share knowledge broadly, and help develop technical leadership across the team

 

**What You’ll Bring** 

**Required** 

* Significant professional software engineering experience building and operating production systems

* Strong expertise in distributed systems, architecture, coding, and technical problem solving

* Demonstrated ability to lead complex initiatives and influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team

* Strong understanding of modern identity systems, including authentication, authorisation, credentials, tokens, and privileged access

* Expertise in AI agents, machine identities, workload identities, service accounts, non-human identities, or closely related identity-security problems

* Practical understanding of how organisations build, deploy, authenticate, and permission AI agents and automated systems

* A customer-oriented mindset and enthusiasm for understanding how technology is used in real-world environments

* Experience building reliable, observable cloud-based services

* Strong judgment when balancing engineering quality, security, technical debt, customer needs, and business priorities

* Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and raise the effectiveness of teams around you

 

**Preferred** 

* Deep knowledge of Entra ID, OAuth/OIDC, SaaS identity ecosystems, workload identity, secrets, or machine-to-machine authentication

* Experience building security capabilities for AI agents or autonomous systems

* Experience with behavioural analytics, detection engineering, anomaly detection, or high-volume security telemetry

* Cybersecurity product experience

 

**What Success Looks Like** 

* Vectra delivers differentiated security capabilities for AI agents and non-human identities

* The Identity team moves efficiently from new telemetry ingestion to customer-visible detections, findings, and observability

* Customers gain meaningful visibility into machine identities, their privileges, behaviour, and risk

* Complex initiatives land predictably with a consistently high engineering bar

* Engineers across the team grow through effective technical leadership and mentoring

 

 

**Why This Role Matters** 

The definition of identity is changing. Increasingly, the actor accessing sensitive enterprise systems may be an application, workload, automation, or AI agent acting autonomously and with significant permissions. 

Securing this world requires understanding not only whether an identity authenticated, but what it is, what it can access, how it normally behaves, and whether its actions make sense in context. 

As a Staff Software Engineer in the Identity Domain, you’ll help Vectra solve that problem end to end, from the data we ingest, through the detections we create, to the findings and observability our customers depend on.

# Endpoint Engineer

## If you love food and technology as much as we do, you’ll love life at Vita Mojo. We’re on a mission to revolutionise the hospitality experience for operators and their customers.

We usually respond within a day

**Location:** Central London

**Job Type:** Full time

**Why join us?**

If you love food and technology as much as we do, you’ll love life at Vita Mojo. We’re on a mission to revolutionise the hospitality experience for operators and their customers. Through our smart digital products, we’re powering the digital transformation of your favourite bars and restaurants. And we want a world where everyone gets the meal they’re hoping for. Each and every time.

**Our Vita Mojo DNA**

We’re proud to have built an award-winning digital platform. Vita Mojo is a positive, energetic and forward-thinking place to work, and when you become a Moji, you’ll be joining a supportive team who’ve always got your back. Our passion for technology and food is matched only by our support for our people.

**About the role**

Vita Mojo's Self-service Kiosks, Point of Sale (POS) terminals, printers and payment devices sit in hundreds of restaurants across the UK and Europe. Every hour one of them is down is an hour a restaurant can't trade properly. Keeping that estate up and healthy is this role.

You'll own the endpoint estate once it's live: managing the fleet through our Mobile Device Management (MDM) platforms, running a maintenance routine that catches faults before they have an impact, fixing remotely, and documenting what you learn so the fix works the second time without you. If you've done End User Computing or endpoint engineering in a corporate environment, the discipline will be familiar.

You'll work alongside our Hardware Solutions Engineer, who owns device specification and strategy, and our Deployment Consultant, who gets devices ordered, staged and installed.

**What you'll be measured on**

* Device uptime across the estate
* How quickly we detect a fault, not just how quickly we fix one
* Accuracy of the asset register against what is actually in the field
* Run-book coverage: this role is not just about the daily doing, learnings and improvements need to be supportable by other teams and influence process, automation and product improvements.

**The day-to-day**

**Estate health and uptime**

The bulk of your week.

* Run a daily health routine across the fleet: offline devices, failing reboots, crashes, connectivity drops, storage.
* Tune the alerting so we find faults proactively, and measure whether that is improving.
* Diagnose and fix remotely: reboots, reinstalls, configuration pushes, storage clean-ups, policy reapplication
* Spot patterns across the estate rather than treating every fault as a one-off

**Maintenance and lifecycle**

* Own a scheduled maintenance cycle rather than waiting for things to break: Operating System (OS) and firmware currency, certificate and licence expiry, storage headroom, temperature monitoring, peripherals
* Day-to-day MDM administration across MDM platforms: enrolment, retirement, policy management, application and OS version control
* Maintain the device configuration baseline, find and correct drift, and keep licence counts accurate
* Plan and run estate-wide changes in controlled waves, with a tested rollback
* Android system-level work: zero-touch enrolment, kiosk and lockdown modes, permissions, log capture and Android Debug Bridge (ADB) diagnosis

**Tuning the Android environment**

* Manage installed software footprint, work out what is needed and disable all unneccesary pre-installed software, system services and background processes.
* Treat patching as a performance lever, not only a security one. Firmware and Android patch levels often carry stability and performance fixes, so knowing which releases are worth taking is part of the job.
* Control what updates itself, and when. Managed Google Play policy, system component auto-updates, staged rollouts and schedules that avoid trading hours, so nothing restarts a device mid-service unless we decided it should.
* Get more life out of older hardware. Part of our estate is five to seven years old and still has to get through a full day's trading.

**Asset data and reporting**

* Own the asset register: serial numbers, naming conventions, location, warranty and lifecycle state
* Keep the mapping honest between what a dashboard says and what is actually sitting in the restaurant.
* Produce the estate reporting that vendor, client and internal conversations rely on

**Support, escalation and documentation**

* Act as third line hardware escalation for the support team
* Be the remote technical hand for third-party field engineers during installs and repairs, and challenge reports when appropriate.
* Attend client sites yourself when a fault won't reproduce remotely. Occasional rather than weekly.
* Turn every recurring fix into a runbook, and maintain the device knowledge base: configurations, known faults, firmware history, peripheral compatibility
* Work the test backlog and chase open vendor defects to a result
* Cover the Hardware Solutions Engineer on defined areas, and join a support rota as our managed service offering launches

**About you**

* You've managed devices at scale through an MDM or endpoint platform. Intune, Jamf, Esper, EloView, SOTI, Workspace ONE or similar. Genuine ownership matters more than which platform.
* You're technical with Android at a system level, not just as a user, or close enough to get there quickly.
* You think in estates: compliance state, configuration drift, patch currency, asset accuracy.
* You're curious about why a device is slow, not only whether it's up.
* You've worked with hardware that lives outside the office: POS, kiosks, payment terminals, printers or handhelds.
* You write things down without being asked, and you finish things. Open items get chased and closed rather than quietly parked.
* You can hold a technical conversation with a vendor, and push back when an answer isn't good enough.

**Bonus points if you**

* Have Android Enterprise experience: device owner mode, zero-touch enrolment, managed Google Play
* Have worked with Elo, Zebra, Sunmi, Epson, Star or payment terminal hardware
* Are handy with ADB, logcat, light scripting or basic SQL for pulling device data
* Have done Android performance or footprint work: memory and storage profiling, start-up time, background execution limits
* Have supported unattended devices in the field: kiosks, lockers, vending, charging or signage
* Have worked in restaurant, retail or hospitality technology

**What this role is not**

* Not a general IT helpdesk role. You won't be resetting staff passwords or fixing laptops.
* Not purely reactive ticket work. Most of your week goes on finding problems nobody has reported yet and maintenance to avoid those problems occurring.
* Not Android application development. Our engineering team owns the Vita Mojo application. You own the environment it runs in.

**Our Benefits and Ways of Working**  
  
We’re proud of the open, inclusive, and supportive culture we’ve built, and continue to build Vita Mojo. We operate a hybrid working model with two in-office collaboration days each week. Outside of those, we trust our team to manage their working day in a way that suits them, while being mindful of team needs, collaboration, and business priorities. This means you can flex your time when needed, whether for personal appointments, family responsibilities, or deep-focus work as long as you’re communicating openly and delivering on your goals.

**Private Healthcare**  
All team members have access to private medical insurance through Vitality Health, offering fast access to high-quality healthcare, wellbeing resources, and the Vitality Programme.

**Life Assurance**  
We provide Group Life Assurance through Legal & General, offering financial protection and wellbeing support to your loved ones in the event of your passing.

**Income Protection**  
Income Protection is offered via Canada Life to support you financially if you’re unable to work due to long-term illness or injury, with additional support to help you return to work when ready.

**Learning & Development**  
We believe that when you grow, we all grow. We’re proud to support professional development that helps you build transferable skills, whether that’s in your current role or to set you up for future success within the company.

We’re also happy to support learning that’s not strictly role-specific, as long as it’s professionally enhancing and contributes to your broader growth at Vita Mojo.

**Holiday Allowance**  
Team members receive 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays. This increases with each full year of service, up to 28 days.

**Carer’s Leave**  
We offer one week (five days) of paid leave annually to support team members caring for a loved one.

**Parental Leave**  
Our enhanced parental leave policy supports all new parents after three months of employment. Primary caregivers receive 16 weeks of full pay, followed by 50% pay for an additional 16 weeks. Secondary caregivers receive four weeks of full pay, plus an additional two weeks after three years of service.

**Health Leave**  
We offer 12 days of fully paid sick leave annually to support your health and recovery.

**Birthday Leave**  
Take the day off to celebrate your birthday—it’s on us.

**Social Events**  
We host regular team socials, from monthly in-office drinks to quarterly offsites, celebrating milestones and enjoying time together as a team.

**Dog-Friendly Office**  
We welcome well-behaved dogs in our offices.

Vortexa is a fast-growing international technology business founded to solve the immense information gap that exists in the energy industry. http://www.vortexa.com/

Ingesting data from multiple external vastly different sources at hundreds of rich data points per second, moving terabytes of data while processing it in real time, running complex and complicated prediction and forecasting AI models while coupling their output into a hybrid human-machine data refinement process and presenting the result through a nimble low-latency SaaS solution used by customers around the globe is no small feat of science and engineering. This processing requires a unique fusion of humans and machines, close collaboration between and deep expertise from data analysts, data scientists, industry experts and the end users.

Vortexa's Data Platform, designed, developed and maintained by the Data Production Team, is a cloud-native ecosystem that powers the full lifecycle of our data and intelligence products. It integrates large-scale data pipelines, machine-learning models, AI agents, human-in-the-loop systems, and microservices to collect, process, connect, and govern global energy-flow data at scale. This platform underpins analytics, operational workflows, and real-time decision-making across the company. Our models ingest and interpret a diverse range of data, from satellite imagery and sensor feeds for millions of energy assets to unstructured commercial and operational shipping data such as customs filings, fixtures, and SPAs. These inputs drive predictive systems that support energy-demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and real-time recommendations for physical and derivative trading.

**What You'll Be Doing**

As a Principal Data Scientist, reporting to Vortexa's VP of Data Production, you will be the subject-matter authority for data science - the person the company turns to on the problems no one has cracked yet - and you will play a central role in designing, implementing, and deploying advanced AI/ML methodologies and production-grade systems. Your work will be held to the scrutiny of energy analysts, traders, operations teams and regulatory stakeholders, and must meet the performance, reliability and robustness standards required for critical energy infrastructure.

You will be:

* Working on frontier problems: where there is no obvious baseline, benchmark or established definition of success. You will be expected to define what good looks like, and bring the rigour needed to reach a meaningful conclusion.

* Raising the ceiling on models already in production: working closely with the pods that own to make live predictions measurably better.

* Taking problems end-to-end: moving across pods and owning substantial projects from initial exploration all the way through to long-term maintenance, ultimately delivering robust, production-grade solutions.

* Turning research into impact: identifying emerging approaches, formulating hypotheses, designing rigorous experiments, evaluating new techniques and translating research into practical solutions that work in the real world.

* Building the capability of Data Science: through technical review, pairing and mentoring, setting the standards for how we work, and by being the person analysts, engineers and product managers bring their hardest questions to.

* Credible with non-technical stakeholders: able to explain modelling trade-offs clearly, set expectations around what is and isn't knowable, negotiate scope and hold a technical position under pressure without losing the room.

We're hiring a Facilities & Contracts Manager to take full ownership of two commercial buildings on the same industrial park — the fabric, the plant, the equipment that keeps operations moving, every contract behind it, and Health & Safety across both sites.

This is a hands-on, single-owner role, not a coordination seat. You'll be our appointed competent person for Health & Safety and the Responsible Person for fire safety, and you'll be the one who knows when the next LOLER examination is due, which contractor is underperforming, and what the landlord owes us. You'll report to the Senior Operations Manager, with a direct line to the Operations Director on anything safety-critical.

If you want a site you can genuinely improve — and the autonomy to do it — read on.

**What you’ll own**

**Sites and buildings**

* Day-to-day operation and maintenance of two commercial/industrial buildings on one park, keeping both safe, compliant, functional and presentable.
* Planned and reactive maintenance across building services: HVAC, electrical distribution, lighting, water systems, doors and loading bays, roofing and fabric.
* The PPM calendar — building it, running it, and evidencing documentation.

**Equipment and plant**

* Warehouse and operational equipment: racking, forklifts and MHE, cold storage and fridges, and associated plant. You'll own servicing schedules, statutory examinations, repairs, spares and end-of-life replacement.
* Cold chain integrity from a facilities standpoint — refrigeration servicing, F-Gas obligations, temperature monitoring and alarm response, contingency planning for failure.

* Minimising downtime: understanding what's critical, what the single points of failure are, and having a plan before something breaks.

**Health & Safety**

You'll be the appointed competent person for Health & Safety across both sites and the Responsible Person under the Fire Safety Order:

* Owning and maintaining the H&S management system: policy, risk assessments, COSHH, manual handling, DSE, working at height, and safe systems of work.
* Contractor safety: RAMS review and approval, permits to work, induction, and CDM duties on projects.
* Accident, incident and near-miss reporting and investigation, including RIDDOR — with root cause analysis and corrective actions that actually close out.
* Chairing H&S meetings, running toolbox talks, delivering inductions and refresher training, and keeping the training matrix current (including forklift and first aid).
* Fire and emergency management: fire risk assessments, evacuation plans, drills, marshals and first aiders.
* Internal audits and inspections, and acting as the point of contact for HSE, fire authority, insurers and environmental regulators.

**Statutory compliance**

You'll be accountable for keeping both sites fully compliant, with the records to evidence it:

* Fixed wiring inspection and testing (EICR), PAT and electrical safety
* LOLER thorough examinations on forklifts and lifting equipment; PUWER and annual SARI/SEMA racking inspections
* Legionella and water hygiene (ACOP L8 / HSG274) — risk assessments, monitoring, remedials
* Fire safety: fire risk assessments, fire alarm and emergency lighting servicing, extinguishers, means of escape, sprinklers/dry risers where fitted
* Intruder alarm, CCTV and access control — servicing, monitoring contracts and response
* Asbestos management, gas safety, lifts and any other applicable regime on site

Where something is out of compliance, you'll flag it early, price the fix and get it closed out.

**Contracts and suppliers**

* Full lifecycle ownership of the facilities contract portfolio: security, cleaning, waste, utilities, landscaping, pest control, M&E, refrigeration and equipment servicing.
* Specification and tendering, commercial negotiation, SLA and KPI setting, performance reviews, and renewal or replacement decisions.
* Writing clear scopes of work so contractors deliver what we actually need, first time.

**Landlord and lease**

* Primary contact for the landlord and managing agent across both buildings.
* Managing the practical side of our lease obligations — repairing covenants, alterations consents, access, service charge review and challenge, and planning for lease events including dilapidations and break/renewal dates under the Landlord and Tenant Act.

**Budget and projects**

* Owning the facilities opex budget and building the capex case for equipment replacement and site improvement.
* Delivering small-to-medium refurbishment and improvement projects end to end: scope, cost, contractor selection, programme, and handover.
* Finding real cost savings — consolidating contracts, energy efficiency, moving from reactive to planned.

**Who you are**

**Essential**

* 3+ years in a dedicated Facilities Management or Building Services role, ideally across more than one commercial or industrial site.
* IOSH General Certificate or equivalent, and experience in leading H&S for a site — writing risk assessments, investigating incidents and running the system.
* Working knowledge of UK statutory compliance in a warehouse or industrial setting — LOLER, PUWER, EICR, L8, fire safety — and the confidence to hold contractors to it.

* A track record of tendering, negotiating and managing a mixed portfolio of service contracts, with evidence of what you saved or improved.
* Experience specifying and delivering capex projects, including writing detailed scopes of work.
* Comfortable being the escalation point. When a cold room fails at 6am, you're the call.

**Nice to have**

* NEBOSH Diploma, IWFM membership, or fire risk assessor qualification.
* Experience in a regulated environment — healthcare, pharmacy, food or life sciences.
* ISO 45001 or 14001 implementation.
* CAFM / maintenance management system implementation.
* Landlord and tenant experience: service charge negotiation, dilapidations, lease events.
* A trade or technical background (electrical, mechanical, refrigeration).

**What we offer**

* £35,000–£50,000 depending on experience
* Share options — you own a piece of what you're building
* Private medical insurance
* Gym and wellness benefit via Wellhub
* Cycle to work and electric car schemes
* 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, generous parental leave and flexible working
* Annual company retreat
* A genuinely early seat at one of the most promising scale-ups in healthcare

**Interview process**

We aim to move quickly and will give you a decision at every stage.

1. Application review — we read every application and respond within one week.
2. Screening call, 30 mins — Google Meet with the Senior Operations Manager on your core experience and fit.
3. Technical interview, 60 mins, on site — with the Pharmacy Operations Lead and a walk of both buildings, then a conversation about H&S, compliance regimes, equipment servicing and contract management. We'll ask you what you'd flag on the walk round, so bring your eye and some examples.
4. Final interview, 30 mins — Google Meet with a member of the UK operations team, focused on how you work and how you'd fit the team.

## About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

## The role

We are looking for an experienced sustainability professional to join our growing Sustainability Advisory team. The team serves as a strategic advisor to Watershed's customers, including more than 20% of the Fortune 500, helping them advance their corporate sustainability programs.

Our primary areas of focus include:

* Decarbonization planning and execution across Scopes 1-3
* Climate target setting, (e.g., SBTi-aligned targets)
* Voluntary and regulatory disclosures, (e.g., CSRD, UK SRS, CDP)

Beyond customer engagements, the Sustainability Advisory team serves as a trusted internal source of expertise. We partner with the Product team to bring sustainability intelligence into the Watershed platform, and with the Go-to-Market team to strengthen Watershed’s expertise, differentiation, and thought leadership.

In this role, you’ll be a highly trusted advisor to sustainability leaders at some of the world’s largest and most consequential companies. You’ll help shape sustainability strategies that make business sense, create the foundation for bold action, and advance progress on complex climate and environmental challenges. You’ll also help build the market-leading corporate sustainability platform by supporting teams across Watershed.

This role is intended for candidates with experience at the Senior Manager or Engagement Manager level, or above, at a leading consulting firm. The scope, autonomy, business acumen, and sustainability expertise required are comparable to those expected at that level or above.

### **You will**

* **Advise sustainability leaders** at many of the world’s leading companies on advancing their sustainability programs. You’ll independently lead strategic engagements across target setting, decarbonization, environmental impact management, and voluntary and regulatory reporting. Working closely with customers, you’ll develop practical strategies and build the business case for sustainability throughout their journey.
* **Build sustainability intelligence** by staying ahead of emerging frameworks, regulations, and market developments. You’ll translate the latest sustainability trends and regulatory changes into clear, actionable guidance for customers and internal teams, helping them remain compliant, competitive, and prepared for what’s next.
* **Help develop new products and services** by exploring emerging sustainability needs across topics and industries. You’ll prototype new ways to create value for customers and expand Watershed’s impact at the intersection of sustainability, advisory, and technology.
* **Shape Watershed’s expertise and point of view** by contributing to thought leadership, customer-facing materials, and internal enablement. You’ll help establish Watershed as a trusted partner for companies navigating the future of corporate sustainability.

### **What we’re looking for**

* 10+ years of professional experience, including at least 4 years at a consulting firm in client-facing roles and at least 4 years working in sustainability.
* Deep expertise in corporate decarbonization and familiarity with key climate frameworks, including the GHG Protocol, PCAF, SBTi, ISO standards, and relevant reporting frameworks and regulations such as CSRD, LSRS, CCDAA, ASRS, ISSB, and CDP.
* The ability to think clearly about complex problems and work confidently with data. You are systematic, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills. You can present complex analyses and recommendations to C-suite audiences and communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* A track record of driving strategic initiatives in complex organizations. You can influence decision-making while managing multiple internal and external stakeholders across organizational levels.
* A strong interest in solving climate change and enthusiasm for helping define the future of corporate sustainability at a high-growth company.

### **Nice to have**

* Fluency in multiple languages, such as English, Spanish, French, or German.

**Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)**

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

Whitefox Technologies is on a mission to reduce energy and water waste in industrial processes. We’re growing fast across the UK, North America and South America.

About the role
This is a new role. You’ll act as a business partner to every department, from innovation and engineering to operations, commercial and finance, finding out how people really work today, where systems don’t talk to each other, and where time goes into assembling data rather than using it. Then you’ll fix it!

You’ll work alongside our existing IT lead, whose strength is infrastructure, equipment and networks. Your focus is different: the business systems, data flow and reporting that sit on top. You’ll overlap on AI and infrastructure, and you’ll be expected to work closely together.

The first phase of the role centres on systems, data integrity and reporting. As that foundation matures, the role is expected to move increasingly into AI and automation, for the right person.


To be clear about what this role is: it’s a hands-on, doing role. You’ll configure systems, build the reports and make the changes yourself, rather than commission others to do it. It is not a financial analyst role, not a pure programming role, and not a data monetisation or commercial data strategy role.

What you’ll deliver in your first year
Review systems and data with every department, produce a prioritised and costed improvement roadmap, and deliver early quick wins so the business feels the impact straight away.
Lead our CRM project, improving how customer data is structured, integrated and used. Deliver self-serve reporting from SAP so that areas like O&M cost, customer servicing and travel data can be pulled without manual effort.
Implement a core set of dashboards, each with a clear owner, that show whether the decisions we’ve made are working, and that are actually used.
Lay the data foundations for a customer data product that brings together customer and product performance data and evidences the energy, water and carbon savings our technology delivers. Put AI-enabled automations into live use and help shape our AI governance framework.

Key responsibilities
Work with department managers and key stakeholders to understand what they do today and where they need to get to, and translate that into practical systems and data solutions.
Improve data flow, data quality and data integrity between our existing applications, including SAP Business ByDesign, our CRM platform and the Microsoft 365 estate.
Identify improvements to existing applications, and plan and implement new or upgraded applications that support our goals and improve efficiency.
Build and maintain Power BI reporting that the business can self-serve, improving information flow and collaboration across teams and regions.
Use AI-enabled tooling as a normal part of how problems get solved, and help the business navigate the evolving AI landscape responsibly.
Help key users adopt good practice in data and systems use, providing training and support where needed.
Live the Whitefox Blueprint values, standards and culture in how you work with colleagues across every location.


About you
You’re equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and in a room with a department manager who doesn’t speak “systems”. **What you’ll be responsible for:**

* **Order validation:** Review orders submitted by Sales, checking products, pricing, contract terms, billing frequencies, credit requirements and supporting documentation.
* **Order control:** Accept complete orders into Operations or return incomplete submissions with clear corrective actions and a robust audit trail.
* **Order ownership:** Own orders through delivery, handover and billing readiness, maintaining accurate statuses, notes, dependencies and target dates in ConnectWise.
* **Delivery coordination:** Coordinate across internal teams and suppliers, proactively chasing actions and escalating delayed, blocked or commercially at-risk orders.
* **Small orders:** Process straightforward orders for up to five SIMs where no equipment or additional delivery activity is required, together with usage bolt-on requests.
* **Quote support:** Manage quotes in ConnectWise CPQ and support Sales with entering the correct products, services, quantities, pricing and customer information.

**Revenue assurance and reconciliation**

* Ensure completed services are submitted promptly to Finance and that recurring, one-off, installation and additional charges are captured correctly.
* Validate billing start dates, credits, discounts and promotional periods against the agreed commercial terms.
* Identify completed but unbilled services and drive each discrepancy through to resolution.
* Reconcile active services across customer contracts, operational records, supplier invoices and customer billing.
* Investigate unmatched, duplicated, incorrectly priced or post-cancellation supplier charges, coordinating disputes and tracking credits to completion.
* Maintain clear reporting on revenue leakage recovered, supplier costs avoided, credits received and outstanding discrepancies.

**Process and data quality**

* Maintain practical order-management controls, procedures and checklists.
* Identify recurring order errors and provide constructive feedback to Sales and other teams.
* Support improvements to ConnectWise workflows, mandatory fields, reporting and automation.
* Help maintain accurate product descriptions, supplier costs and standard customer charges.
* Support new product launches by helping define the required operational, delivery and billing processes.

**What we’re looking for:**

* Experience in order management, billing, revenue assurance, sales operations, finance administration or a similar detail-focused role.
* Strong attention to detail, with the ability to spot missing, inconsistent or commercially risky information.
* Excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple orders, deadlines and dependencies.
* Clear and confident communication, including the ability to challenge incomplete or inaccurate information constructively.
* An investigative approach to discrepancies, with the determination to establish root causes and follow actions through to completion.
* Commercial awareness and an understanding of how delays, errors and missed billing affect revenue and margin.
* Confidence using multiple systems, spreadsheets and detailed service records.
* A collaborative approach and the ability to build effective working relationships across Sales, Operations, Technical and Finance teams.

* Telecommunications, managed services, connectivity or another recurring-revenue business.
* ConnectWise or a comparable CRM, PSA or order-management platform.
* ConnectWise CPQ/Sell or a comparable configure-price-quote platform.
* Reconciling supplier invoices against customer billing or service inventories.
* Credit control, recurring billing, cancellations and supplier-dispute processes.
* Good Excel skills, including lookups, pivot tables and reconciliation techniques.

You will take ownership, work accurately and transparently, collaborate across teams and raise concerns when information or controls do not meet the required standard. ROLE AND PURPOSE

Understand requirements from the wider social housing sector – Social Housing Regulator, Ombudsman etc. – and interpret into change programmes and projects, in conjunction with senior managers within Neighbourhoods & Housing, Practice Management Team etc.  
  
Lead or support programmes and projects to deliver identified changes, improvements, and benefits. Provide knowledge, expertise and capacity in programme and project management, and in change management and improvement techniques.

Foster a positive culture within Neighbourhoods and Housing and beyond, in line with the service area’s vision and values, and those of Hull City Council more broadly.**PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:**   

1 Strategy –Research unfamiliar areas of public service delivery, in particular social housing, and establish what represents best practice in these areas.Take a lead role in creating change programmes that align to the strategic needs of service users and to agreed local strategies and corporate plans, incorporating national and local objectives, priorities, and targets, such as those published by the Social Housing Regulator, Ombudsman, DLUHC etc.Identify areas of impact beyond the core change activities, and ensure relevant stakeholders are made aware.Appropriately select and apply agreed strategies, policies, and methodologies to areas of programme and project work.The postholder will work autonomously, after receiving a broad scope from more senior officers, but will regularly check-in with progress and will receive direction and key decision-making through appropriate governance structures such as Programme Boards. These will usually be comprised of senior managers such as Heads of Service and Assistant Directors.  
  
2 Customer Focus – Be customer focused and ensure programmes/projects are utilising customer / tenant insight to plan and deliver change.Ensure programmes / projects and their benefits effectively embed the voice of the tenant / tenant needDevelop and maintain effective working relationships with key stakeholders. Ensure communication is effective at all levels, ensuring buy-in from staff and enabling change to be delivered.Work collaboratively with staff at all levels within the Council and partner organisations to ensure a clear understanding of the importance of designing for the customer / tenant when delivering change.Take the lead on transition management, ensuring that business as usual is maintained during the transition to new ways of working, and the timing of the changes are optimised to effectively integrate into the business.  
  
3 Performance Management – Co-ordinate activity on programmes and projects.Capture and report on progress against the programme/project and raise and escalate issues and risks to line manager or Programme Board as appropriate.Deliver to tight deadlines and influence others to deliver within such parameters. Establish and implement the mechanisms by which benefits can be measured. Proactively monitor benefits realisation.Monitor and review project documentation prepared by more junior colleagues.Use performance management from within / outside the service to inform and shape change programmes and projects.  
  
4 Leadership – Be an effective leader, modelling exemplary behaviour to staff and promoting a positive culture which seeks excellence in public service. Actively promote a culture of organisational learning and development, including coaching and mentoring of staff.The post holder will matrix manage a team when required; and may have permanent line management responsibility for more junior colleagues within Business Development and Change. Champion change and improvement methodologies and techniques. Embed learning into the organisation from reputable and proven external business change research and best practice. Transfer knowledge and skills to colleagues in the organisation. Work with and guide senior managers to shape and deliver change and transformation.  
  
5 Statutory Obligations – Must take account of relevant statutory obligations within business process redesign and identification of efficiencies.These will usually be, although not limited to, obligations relating to the provision of housing, which is a highly-regulated area. Where necessary seeks advice from colleagues such as in Legal Services and Practice Management.  
  
6 Manage Projects and ProgrammesProvide project and programme expertise to change programmes and projects.Decide most appropriate programme / project management methodology and techniques to use based on nature and needs of assigned projects. Identify the need for and develop appropriate project documentation. Identify synergies, potential duplication or conflicts and ensuring activities (e.g. risk management) are underpinned with recognised programme management methodologies.Ensure sufficient resources are available to undertake efficient project delivery and that the necessary resources are identified, planned and allocated to projects ensuring outputs are delivered on time and to the required level of quality. Support and lead project people resources from across the service area or other service areas in a matrix management arrangement. Oversee and report on project / programme budgets as assigned.Lead on stakeholder communication and engagement regarding programme outcomes.Ensure that new models of working are embedded successfully. Where not personally leading projects and programmes, provide project management skills to support service department staff to deliver change programmes and associated benefits. Champion change management and project management disciplines.  
  
7 Conduct analysisIdentify potential improvements to service efficiency, using skills and knowledge (e.g. change management techniques, improvement techniques, data analysis). Provide advice in service business planning, processes, and performance. Make recommendations that take advantage of opportunities such as technological innovation, based on own up to date knowledge and research.Work with service managers to turn improvement ideas/proposals into workable solutions and formulate these into detailed viable plans.Analyse and review the benefits of individual projects to support prioritisation. Communicate with all stakeholders, deal with risks and barriers, to ensure objectives are delivered on time and within resources allocated. Complete post implementation reviews to ensure that the required business benefits have been achieved and will be sustained. Produce management reports on the findings.  
  
8 Communicate and InfluenceEnsure the buy-in of stakeholders at a programme and project level (e.g., staff affected by change).Facilitate the development of a continuous improvement culture by identifying improvements, making recommendations, and providing support to and negotiating with managers to deliver change and improvement as a result of findings, dealing with any potential opposition to the proposed changes.

This is a Full Time, Fixed Term position for two years due to grant funding.  
  
The Private Housing Environmental Health Team carry out actions to discharge the Council statutory duties under various pieces of legislation particularly the Housing Act 2004 and more recently the Renters Rights Act 2025.   
  
The post holder will be an integral part of the team, working with other Housing Enforcement /Licensing Officers, and Environmental Health Officer colleagues to improve housing standards within private rented accommodation in the city.  
  
The post holder is expected to work directly alongside colleagues to ensure the council is carrying out it’s statutory duties in relation to poor housing conditions and noncompliance with statutory requirements. Some of these tasks will include dealing with poor housing conditions, organising works in default, carrying out inspections, investigating illegal eviction cases, and revisits, serving notices, attending and providing evidence at Residential Property tribunals, and serving civil penalties.   
   
If this is something of interest to you, we’d love to hear from you. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Andrea Towse on 01482 614 362 or email andreatowse@hullcc.gov.uk   
  
ROLE AND PURPOSE  
  
To assist in the discharge of the councils statutory duties in relation to housing standards and Mandatory Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation. By regulating, monitoring, maintaining, improving and enforcing housing conditions throughout the city through the effective delivery of a customer focussed service in respect of housing standards to homeowners, empty properties, an accreditation scheme, private and public sector tenants, some of whom may be from vulnerable groups, landlords, internal and external agencies.  
  
To implement and develop the Council’s programme for Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation and houses in the private sector. To work within a team of professional officers in the Private Housing (Environmental Health) team of Housing Services in discharging the City Council’s strategy, in relation to the standard of private and public sector housing and empty properties, and to help to secure the regeneration of the City’s private sector housing including development, review and operation of a landlord accreditation scheme.**PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:**  

1. To promote and safeguard the welfare of children, young people and/or vulnerable adults’.   
  
2. To undertake the day to day operational aspects of licensing private sector houses in multiple occupation and houses as required by Housing Act 2004 under the schemes currently operational (National Mandatory HMO licensing) and those being considered by Hull City Council, (Selective and Additional Licensing) including dealing with queries from landlords and tenants about standards, processing licensing applications and associated payments, determining licence conditions and the issuing of licences. To identify properties that require a licence but for which no licence application has been made by carrying out survey work, interrogation of various Council data bases, consulting landlords and other investigative procedures.  
  
3. To oversee the councils accreditation scheme. Dealing with queries, non-compliance with scheme, taking a leading role in the development and review of the scheme and production of scheme related documentation. To promote the scheme so it is recognised by tenants as a trusted brand. Producing newsletters and other promotional material using other media.  
  
4. To interpret the Housing Act 2004 and other existing legislation so as to determine, under supervision, appropriate courses of action when non-compliance with legislation or risks to public health, safety and welfare are identified. Actions will range from the provision of advice, guidance and written reports, and the service of legal notices to arranging remedial work, works in default, civil penalties, attending The First-tier Tribunal Property Chamber (Residential Property) and under taking prosecution.  
  
5. To proactively identify and when brought to the councils attention take action to bring empty properties back into use. Developing and reviewing the Councils empty property procedures ensure effective use of all of the legislation available. Assisting other departments with debt recovery by sharing ownership information when appropriate.  
  
6. To collect, prepare and collate evidence, thoroughly, professionally and in accordance with Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (PACE) and departmental procedures and to act as an expert witness in Court in taking prosecutions on behalf of the Council and also obtaining warrants to gain entry. This is in relation to the illegal operation of unlicensed houses in multiple occupation and privately rented accommodation, the contravention of licensing conditions, contraventions of the Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation Regulations 2006 and failure to comply with other statutory notices served under the Housing Acts, Building Act 1984, Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the Public Health Acts.  
  
7. To undertake high level inspections of private housing where decisions are often subjective and to interpret new and existing legislation using professional judgement; to determine compliance with licence conditions and hazards using the Housing Health and Safety Rating System in Private Housing and appropriate courses of action when non-compliance with legislation or risks to public health are identified. Actions will range from the provision of advice, guidance and written reports, and the service of legal notices to arranging remedial work or work in default to ensure the health and safety of the public and fulfil the Council’s statutory obligations. This work will often be with vulnerable tenants who may present in a distressed manner. Inspections of premises will require the use of safety, measuring and recording equipment which will have to be carried onto site. Identify the appropriate action to bring empty properties back into use. Whilst undertaking this work the post holder may come into contact with individuals whose behaviour is challenging.  
  
8. To persuade, educate and negotiate with property owners and property agents to influence them so as to carry out improvements and repairs to their properties and develop an attitudinal change in their professional management style in relationship to dealing with their tenants so as to raise the standard of accommodation and levels of management skills within the private rented sector. To utilise all of the legislative powers available to deal with poor housing conditions, including dealing with empty properties and preventing them from becoming a blight on neighbourhoods.  
  
9. To draw scale plans of houses and houses in multiple occupation, including the use of software packages (computer aided design) as necessary so as to assist in the determination of fire precautions and other remedial works required in such premises. To maintain and ensure correct up to date entries onto CIVICA APP date base and to ensure that entries by other members of staff are made correctly by monitoring the data base.

Hull City Council established its Building Safety Team in 2024 in response to major legislative changes, including the Building Safety Act, Fire Safety Act, and Fire Safety (England) Regulations, introduced following the Grenfell Tower tragedy.  
  
Our team is dedicated to ensuring the safety of multi-occupancy dwellings across the city. This includes oversight of:  
  
• 19 high-rise buildings  
• 7 medium-rise buildings  
• 4 sheltered blocks  
• 445 low-rise blocks  
  
We work in close partnership with the Housing Investment Team, which manages responsive and cyclical maintenance, specialist compliance works, planned improvement projects, and refurbishment schemes for a stock of 24,000 domestic properties. In addition, we collaborate with the High-Rise Tenancy and Facilities Management teams to deliver a comprehensive approach to building safety.  
  
The Job   
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a full-time, permanent Resident Engagement Strategy Manager to join the Building Safety Team.   
  
The postholder will be responsible for managing stakeholder communication and engagement across our high-rise blocks of flats, improving resident engagement outcomes by leading on the development and implementation of unique Resident Engagement Strategies and associated engagement activity.   
  
The role offers flexibility, with work based across offices, home, and site locations, depending on team needs and daily requirements.  
  
This post is designated as politically sensitive.  
  
For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Maria Kohler, Programme Manager on 01482 615 019 Maria.Kohler@hullcc.gov.uk, Sally Smith, Tenant Experience, and Support Manager on 01482 614 342 Sally.Smith@hullcc.gov.uk  
  
What We’re Looking For:  
The successful candidate will be professional, empathetic, and able to handle sensitive issues appropriately, referring to relevant services when necessary.  
  
To maintain high standards of competence within the Building Safety Team, ongoing training and development will be provided. Candidates must demonstrate essential skills, knowledge, experience, and behaviours aligned with the role.  
  
Please ensure that your application demonstrates how you meet the essential criteria against the person specification as listed in the job description.  
  
  
ROLE AND PURPOSE  
  
Neighbourhoods & Housing is committed to a programme of continuous improvement to develop the service offered to its tenants and customers, driven by rapid, fundamental change in the housing sector – change triggered by revised legislation, the introduction of a regulatory regime and framework, Ombudsman guidance and learning, good practice, societal factors, and opportunities presented by new and emerging technology.  
  
The postholder will:  
  
Take full responsibility for stakeholder communication and engagement regarding improving resident engagement outcomes within 22 high rise blocks of flats. Provide quality assurance for the work activity with the support of appropriate workstream leads and stakeholders across the Council, such as Anti Social Behaviour, Area Housing team, Corporate Finance, etc.  
  
Lead on the development and implementation of a unique Resident Engagement Strategy, within an overall framework for the city, for each of the 22 High Rise Flat blocks covered by the appropriate legislation (Building Safety Act 2022 and Social Housing Regulation Act 2023), ensuring that all residents aged 16 and above are listened to in the process, to ensure that they meet the specific building safety needs of each block.   
  
Ensure active overview of all resident engagement projects and activities, liaising with other services within Neighbourhoods and Housing to build strong relationships to co-design and co-deliver outcomes and benefits, linkages, identify and manage dependencies, and ensure outputs are delivered in a prioritised and logical order, mitigating duplication and maximising opportunities for efficiency.  
  
Identifying, planning, and delivering high level work activities required to deliver strategic objectives, through understanding key service issues including legislation, societal factors, sector-specific trends and demands, technology, service resources and stakeholders, and the environment in which Neighbourhoods and Housing operates. Also strong analytical knowledge and ability required to assess current situations and put forward proposals for step change continuous improvement.  
  
Manage and co-ordinate any projects which form part of the resident engagement work programme to deliver continued improvement using a broad range of technical and project skills that best suit each circumstance.  
  
Work with and guide senior managers to shape activities and the implications of activities and provide recommendations regarding robustness and achievement of expected outcomes.

**PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:**

1. To promote and safeguard the welfare of children, young people and/or vulnerable adults. The Government regulation states that the job role will need to engage with everybody in the Council flats above the age of 16.

**2. Customer focus** – Work with senior managers in Neighbourhoods and Housing, the wider council, partners, and tenants, to understand tenant and customer need and assimilate into the service outcomes and benefits.

Ensure engagement is effective at all levels, ensuring buy-in from managers and staff  and enabling change to be delivered to achieve service objectives and benefits.

Build effective relationships with partners for the co-design and co-delivery of appropriate projects and joint stakeholder engagement. These may include other Local Authorities and Registered Social Landlords, Regulatory Bodies, Voluntary Sector Providers etc.

**3. Performance Management** – Independent thinking to objectively assess and ensure appropriate Neighbourhoods and Housing staff,  subject matter experts, contractors etc., are providing agreed work deliverables.

Support appropriate Neighbourhoods and Housing staff, subject matter experts, contractors etc., in the provision of accurate progress reports, reporting and escalating areas of concern and possible solutions.

Focus on promoting a positive performance culture reporting on performance issues to ensure the delivery of effective business operations.

Lead on and own the co-ordination of ongoing day to day operation of the Resident Engagement Strategy for each building in line with building safety legislative and regulatory requirements for each block.  Leads on service monitoring and capture of data around outputs and outcomes laid out in each Resident Engagement Strategy, to establish its effectiveness in regard to block management, reduction in building safety incidents and whether residents feel safer in their homes.

To ensure business change and service improvement within Neighbourhoods and Housing is delivered effectively by managing the delivery of projects and/or work activities identified to realise that change, so that the service can keep pace with a rapidly changing sector and deliver expected customer and /or financial benefits.

**4. Statutory Obligations –** To align work activity with all relevant legislation and Council policies with particular emphasis on Housing-related legislation such as – but not limited to – the Housing Act (various), Building Safety Act 2022, Social Housing Regulation Act 2023 and other inter-related legislation and guidance.

Lead on the development and implementation of a unique Resident Engagement Strategy, within an overall framework for the city, for each of the 22 High Rise Flat blocks covered by complex new Building Safety Legislation.  Project management and effective engagement with multiple stakeholders, including the residents of each block, ensuring that all residents aged 16 and above are listened to, with officers and others as necessary in a co-design process, to ensure the Strategy produced for each block meets its specific building safety needs.

5. Contribute appropriate documents, such as the Resident Engagement Strategy, to the Building Safety Team to form Building Safety Cases and Building Safety Case Reports, as required by the Building Safety Regulator (part of the Health & Safety Executive).

6. Lead on the review of the Resident Engagement Strategy for each of the 22 high rise blocks at least every 3 years or after any significant event at the block or significant change in the demographics within the block if sooner.  Within this, decides whether and when the Resident Engagement Strategy of a particular block requires amendment taking into account a wide range of dynamics within a given block.

7. Work closely and effectively with a range of other professionals, including the Health and Safety Lead, Housing Tenancy Managers, their senior management team as necessary, in the development of the strategies, but also to ensure the effective day-to-day delivery of safe services, understanding the local context of each block.  Write and present reports and briefings to senior management and governance structures as necessary.

8. Lead on the outward communications of key building safety messages as they evolve, attending Senior Management Team meetings as necessary.  Use platforms agreed within each Resident Engagement Strategy.  Develop campaigns and new channels of communication as required.  Take account of continual change in the demographics of each block and their evolving communications needs to continually review channels used and lead channel development, from the more traditional, to social media, to those which are new and evolving, ensuring all key audience groups are reached and increasingly involved, in line with the 22 individual strategies.

9. Develop and deliver information in a variety of formats (presentations, reports, briefing notes, plans, etc.), which reflect the needs of the target audience and represent the Council as required to publicise and promote the project, department and its achievements, ensuring that a professional image is projected at all times.

10. Focal point for frequent contacts on a wide range of building safety and other issues by residents, Elected Members, external organisations, partners and other stakeholders, ensuring each contact effectively captured and actioned.

11. Develop culture of resident ownership of the Resident Engagement Strategy for each block; promote and facilitate stronger community cohesion, especially among hard-to-reach groups.   Recruit advocates and deliver training as necessary to support this.
